Probe Dependency Graph and Orchestration Manifest

Overview

Purpose: Define the Probe Dependency Graph (PDG) concept, data model, orchestration manifest, and operational procedures for coordinating evaluation probes across shadowing, quantization migration, and regression triage. The PDG ensures probes run in dependency-aware order, minimizes redundant work, and encodes quality/latency constraints for mixed-SLO workloads.

Scope: This doc covers the PDG schema, node/edge semantics, orchestration priority rules, example manifests, runtime integration points with the eval harness, and a step-by-step runbook for probe incidents and migrations. It applies to: evaluator teams, model-onboarding engineers, and the runtime/CI owners.

Why a PDG?
- Probes increasingly depend on the outputs of other probes (e.g., priming templates, cached KV artifacts, quant-safety classifiers). Without explicit dependency management, we see wasted compute, nondeterministic scheduling, and triage complexity during regressions.
- PDG centralizes dependency metadata so the eval engine can reuse intermediate artifacts, schedule co-located runs, and generate clear blame paths for regressions.

Key concepts

1) Node types (table)
| node_type | purpose | critical_fields | owner |
| probe | Primary evaluation probe (prompt+seed+slice) | id, slice_id, cost_estimate, expected_latency_ms | evaluator |
| transformer | Artifact producer (priming template generator, tokenizer shim) | id, image, cache_key | evaluator |
| quant-job | Quantization candidate run (per-model/per-profile) | id, profile, quant_level | applied-ml |
| kv-cache | Generated cache snapshot used by downstream probes | id, model_version, ttl_sec | infra |
| aggregator | Combines probe outputs into metrics (e.g., coherence, fidelity) | id, metric_list, window_size | applied-ml |

2) Edge semantics
- depends_on: downstream node must wait for upstream to complete successfully.
- uses_cache: downstream can reuse upstream artifacts; orchestration may skip run if cache is fresh.
- optional_if_failed: if upstream fails, downstream can run a degraded flow (e.g., fallback prompt) but must be tagged in manifest.

3) Contract rules
- Each node declares SLO tags: latency_budget_ms, budget_tokens, fidelity_min (0-1).
- Orchestrator enforces a soft-deadline; nodes that miss latency_budget_ms are flagged and the scheduler may deprioritize their dependents.
- Cost_estimate is required (USD/minor_units) to support eval budgeting and probe eviction.

PDG Manifest: YAML example\n# Example PDG manifest (annotated)
version: v1
manifest_id: pdg-example-card-promotion-2027
description: PDG for card-promotion ranking probe set with quant shadowing
nodes:
  - id: tkn-priming-v1
    type: transformer
    image: gcr.io/redwood/primers/tkn-priming:202701
    cache_key: primer/tkn-v1/sha256:abcd
    owner: evaluator
    outputs: [kv-cache:primer-tkn-v1]
  - id: probe-ranking-a
    type: probe
    slice_id: ranking-promo-A
    depends_on: [tkn-priming-v1]
    expected_latency_ms: 120
    cost_estimate: 0.003
    fidelity_min: 0.85
    owner: evaluator
    optional_if_failed: true
  - id: quant-shadow-low
    type: quant-job
    profile: int8-dynamic
    depends_on: [probe-ranking-a]
    owner: applied-ml
    expected_latency_ms: 500
    cost_estimate: 0.02
edges:
  - from: tkn-priming-v1
    to: probe-ranking-a
    relation: uses_cache
  - from: probe-ranking-a
    to: quant-shadow-low
    relation: depends_on

Integration points
- Eval Orchestrator API: POST /eval/orchestrate with manifest_id and run_policy (immediate | scheduled | canary). The orchestrator returns run_id and a plan

  - from: probe-ranking-a
    to: quant-shadow-low
    relation: depends_on

Integration points
- Eval Orchestrator API: POST /eval/orchestrate with manifest_id and run_policy (immediate | scheduled | canary). The orchestrator returns run_id and a plan with task-level ETA estimates.
- Cache registry: PDG nodes that declare outputs must register artifacts into the central cache service under the manifest namespace. The registry stores artifact provenance and TTL.
- Telemetry hooks: each node emits standardized spans (pdg.node.start/stop) and a final pdg.node.result with fields: status, tokens_used, wall_ms, artifact_refs (if any).

Scheduling and priority algorithm (high-level)
1. Topological sort by depends_on edges. Nodes in the same rank are prioritized by a score: score = w1*(1-fidelity_min) + w2*(cost_estimate_norm) + w3*(latency_penalty) where weights are configured per-origination (default w1=0.6,w2=0.25,w3=0.15).
2. If a node's cache_key exists and artifact is fresh (TTL not expired), skip the producer node and link the artifact ref into the plan.
3. For mixed-SLO runs (some nodes with tight latency_budget_ms, others with high-fidelity), the scheduler builds two passes: a fast-pass (best-effort low-latency nodes) and a quality-pass (full fidelity).
4. Canary policy: when running quant-shadow jobs, orchestrator schedules canary runs limited to 1% of traffic-mapped probes and pins a regression-watch window. Canary failures trigger an early abort and notify the regression triage channel.

Operational runbook

Trigger conditions:
- PDG orchestrator reports node failures > 5% in 10-minute window for any manifest
- Canary quant-shadow failure (quality drop > fidelity_min - 0.1)
- Cache registry reports corrupted artifact checksum

Immediate steps (1-5):
1) Triage lead acknowledges the alert in PagerDuty and opens a PDG incident (link to incident template).
2) Run "pdg-cli plan-status --manifest pdg-example-card-promotion-2027" to get live plan.
3) If failures are isolated to a transformer/kv-cache node, mark dependent probes as degraded: run "pdg-cli rerun --node probe-ranking-a --degraded-template=ranking-fallback-v1".
4) For quant canary failures, immediately set quant-shadow to suspend: "pdg-cli set-policy --manifest <id> --quant-shadow=paused" and notify applied-ml on Slack #applied-ml-quant.
5) Collect artifact refs and attach to the incident: use the telemetry hook to download pdg.node.result spans and attach the first-failure logs.

Post-incident analysis
- Owner: evaluator team lead.
- Deliverable within 3 business days: incident summary with root-cause hypothesis, affected slices, regressions scores, and a remediation plan (rollback, patch, or new probe).
- If root cause relates to model changes, create a regression ticket and schedule a re-run of the PDG with the previous model version pinned.

Rolling out PDG-driven workflows (checklist)
1. Create manifest and validate with 'pdg-cli validate --manifest <file>'. Validation checks: circular dependencies, required SLO tags, cost estimates, and TTLs.
2. Run locally in dry-mode: 'pdg-cli plan --manifest <file> --dry-run'. Confirm that topological order aligns with expectations.
3. Canary schedule: tag manifest with 'canary: true' and define canary_target_percent. Start with 0.5%-1% and observe

Run locally in dry-mode: 'pdg-cli plan --manifest <file> --dry-run'. Confirm that topological order aligns with expectations.
3. Canary schedule: tag manifest with 'canary: true' and define canary_target_percent. Start with 0.5%-1% and observe fidelity metrics for 48 hours.
4. Promote to scheduled daily runs once stability metrics (fidelity variance < 0.02, failure rate < 0.5%) are met for 72 hours.
5. Archive old manifests and ensure cache eviction policies are configured to avoid stale artifacts.

SLOs and alert thresholds
- Probe success rate: 99.5% per 24h window.
- Artifact freshness (kv-cache TTL): default 6 hours, must be <= 24 hours.
- Canary fidelity regression: alert if fidelity delta >= 0.05 over baseline.
- Scheduling latency: 95th percentile plan-to-start <= 30s for immediate runs.

Ownership and escalation
- Manifest author: evaluator team (primary).
- Orchestrator service owner: runtime infra (pager: infra-oncall).
- Quant jobs: applied-ml (pager: applied-ml-oncall).
- Incident triage: evaluator lead -> applied-ml lead -> runtime infra if artifact corruption suspected.

Migration notes for model-onboarding and quantization teams
- When onboarding a quant profile, attach a PDG manifest that includes both the production probe node and corresponding quant-shadow node. This guarantees an atomic relationship between the probe and its quant candidate.
- Ensure quant-job nodes declare a backward-compatibility flag: 'fallback_to: {model_version}' so rollbacks are automated.

Metrics dashboard (recommended widgets)
- PDG run rate (daily) split by manifest owner.
- Node-level failure heatmap (by node_type and slice).
- Cache hit ratio for transformer nodes.
- Canary fidelity delta timeseries per manifest.

Examples and troubleshooting scenarios
1) Scenario: Priming transformer runs unexpectedly slow during a spike.
   - Symptoms: downstream probes show increased latency and partial timeouts.
   - Quick fix: instruct orchestrator to skip transformer with 'pdg-cli override --skip tkn-priming-v1 --manifest <id>' and attach fallback primers.
   - Longer fix: scale transformer horizontally and increase cache TTL for the high-traffic slice.

2) Scenario: Quant canary passes locally but fails under shadow load.
   - Action: pause global quant rollout, run targeted long-tail probes from the PDG (use 'pdg-cli replay --manifest <id> --slice longtail-99') and collect per-slice fidelity.

Quantized Artifact Evaluation Gate and Canary Rollout

Overview
--------
This document defines the evaluation gate for quantized model artifacts and the associated canary rollout orchestration used by Redwood Inference. It codifies the entry criteria for promoting a quantized artifact from shadow/onboarding environments into production routes (hosted, dedicated, or private), the telemetry and tests required, and the rollback/troubleshooting guidance to tie into existing regression triage playbooks.

Scope
-----
- Applies to artifacts produced by the model onboarding and quantization pipelines (both automatic and manual quant profiles).
- Covers hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where binary/quant artifacts are deployed.
- Integrates with: eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, quality guardrails, and regression triage procedures.

Goals and Principles
--------------------
- Safety-first: do not promote artifacts that show statistically significant regressions on prioritized slices.
- Reproducible gating: every promoted artifact must carry provenance (checksums, quant profile, kernel pins).
- Cost- and latency-aware: accept modest throughput/latency regressions only when quality is preserved.
- Fast rollback: automated fallback to pre-quantized or previous-quant artifacts on breach of SLOs.

Acceptance Criteria (high level)
-------------------------------
All of the following must pass for a quantized artifact to be eligible for canary:

- Core prompt-set stability: weighted-regression-delta (WRD) <= 0.03 on the core prompt suite (see Prompt Suite table below).
- Embedding anchor fidelity: mean cosine similarity >= 0.995 on the embedding anchor set.
- Response Stability Index (RSI) >= 0.92 across representative interaction traces.
- Token-level divergence: KL divergence of token distributions <= 0.10 vs float baseline for the same contexts.
- Latency impact: P95 latency <= 1.25x of float baseline for equivalent batch mix.
- Resource footprint: GPU memory footprint and KV-cache size within the profile targets documented in artifact metadata.

Note: Any metric exceeding these thresholds triggers an automated failure and requires an explicit triage (see "Failure Modes").

Detailed Metrics and Thresholds
-------------------------------
- WRD (weighted-regression-delta): aggregated per-slice; slices are weighted by production traffic share. Threshold: 0.03.
- Embedding Cosine: measured on N=2k anchor pairs covering English/Spanish/FR. Threshold: 0.995.
- RSI (Response Stability Index): similarity of canonical answers measured by BLEU+semantic-similarity heuristics; threshold 0.92.
- Token KL: base-10 log KL aggregated over tokens emitted for core prompts; threshold 0.10.
- Latency P95: measured on synthetic & shadow traffic; threshold 1.25x.
- Throughput (tokens/sec/GPU): should not degrade more than 20% for same batch configuration.

Evaluation Pipeline (steps executed by rwi-eval harness)
------------------------------------------------------
1) Artifact registration
   - Upload artifact bundle to artifact storage and record metadata: model_id, model_version, quant_profile_id, checksum (sha256), source-float-checksum, kernel_pins, expected_sequence_length, supported-clients.
   - Example metadata table (see Appendix).

2) Smoke tests (automated, ~15 minutes)
   - Run unit-level generation tests (sanity responses, tokenization roundtrips).
   - Run embedding consistency sanity check on a 200-item

expected_sequence_length, supported-clients.
   - Example metadata table (see Appendix).

2) Smoke tests (automated, ~15 minutes)
   - Run unit-level generation tests (sanity responses, tokenization roundtrips).
   - Run embedding consistency sanity check on a 200-item anchor subset.
   - Command: rwi-eval smoke --artifact s3://rwi-artifacts/<id> --profile quant 

3) Full harness run (automated, parallelized, 2–6 hours depending on artifact size)
   - Execute core prompt-set, edge-case probes, multilingual anchors, and latency-quality slices.
   - Produce JSON report, per-slice diffs, and a signed acceptance artifact.
   - Command: rwi-eval run --artifact s3://rwi-artifacts/<id> --slices core,edge,multi --profile quant --output report.json

4) Telemetry snapshot
   - Snapshot baseline telemetry from the float baseline run that produced the artifact. Required fields: baseline_tokens_per_sec, baseline_P95_latency_ms, baseline_RSI, baseline_embeddings_stats.json.

5) Signoff gating
   - Automated pass/fail decision based on thresholds above.
   - If pass: artifact moves to "canary-ready" state and a canary deployment is scheduled.
   - If fail: record fail reason, notify model-owner and QE, and open a triage ticket with labels: quant-fail, artifact:<id>.

Canary Rollout Orchestration
----------------------------
Principles: incremental traffic, real-world telemetry, and short feedback loops. Canary uses the same route-level instrumentation as production (token-level, cost, latency, error breakdowns).

Canary configuration (example YAML):

---
canary_name: quant-canary-<model_id>-v<version>
initial_traffic_percent: 2
stages:
  - { percent: 2, duration_hours: 6 }
  - { percent: 10, duration_hours: 24 }
  - { percent: 30, duration_hours: 24 }
monitoring: [rsi, wrd, p95_latency, error_rate, embedding_drift]
rollback_policy:
  breach_thresholds:
    rsi_drop_absolute: 0.04
    wrd_increase_absolute: 0.02
    p95_ratio: 1.5
    error_rate_absolute: 0.01
  immediate_on_breach: true
---

Traffic routing is controlled by the canary controller (service: canary-orch) which will bump percentages according to the YAML schedule if and only if monitoring windows show no threshold breach. Canary controller posts events to #canary-observability and creates an automated incident if immediate_on_breach triggers.

Promotion checklist (pre-rollout)
--------------------------------
- [ ] Artifact metadata published and signed.
- [ ] Eval harness report uploaded and signed.
- [ ] QE and model owner sign off on per-slice notes (explicitly mark tolerated regressions).
- [ ] Canary YAML created and reviewed by infra and SRE on-call.
- [ ] Backup fallback (previous float artifact or previous quant artifact) staged and smoke-tested.

Failure Modes and Triage Guidance
--------------------------------
Common failure categories and immediate checks: 
- Tokenization / vocabulary drift
  - Symptom: high token KL and degraded RSI on short prompts.
  - First-check: verify tokenizer version and tokenization parity with float baseline.
- Kernel mismatch / pinned-kernel divergence
  - Symptom: large latency variance, small but systematic generation differences on long context.
  - First-check: confirm kernel_pins listed in artifact metadata are available and identical on target fleet.
- Quant rounding and clipping
  - Symptom: semantic shift in numeric outputs, embedding drift on numeric-heavy prompts.
  - First-check: run the per-token delta diagnostic in rwi-eval with --debug-quant to produce token-level rounding stats.
- Cache/KV interaction issues

- Symptom: semantic shift in numeric outputs, embedding drift on numeric-heavy prompts.
  - First-check: run the per-token delta diagnostic in rwi-eval with --debug-quant to produce token-level rounding stats.
- Cache/KV interaction issues
  - Symptom: failures or degraded quality after repeated multi-turns.
  - First-check: run a kv-cache stress scenario from the harness (rwi-eval kv-stress).

Linking to Regression Triage
---------------------------
When a canary breach occurs, the canary controller automatically creates a triage ticket (component: applied-ml/regression) and attaches: the full rwi-eval report, canary telemetry snapshots, and the artifact metadata. Use the regression-triage playbooks to run bisect, blame-assistant, and probe-farm if needed. Prioritize triage steps that can rule out infra/kernel mismatches before assuming a model-quality regression.

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------

- QE contact: applied-ml-qe@redwood.example.com.
- Canary controller / infra owner: infra-orch@redwood.example.com.
- On-call SRE (short link): /eng-sre/oncall-rotations/current

Synthetic Seed Generation and Resampling Protocol for Eval Stability

Overview

This document specifies Redwood's canonical protocol for generating synthetic seeds used by eval harnesses and for performing repeatable resampling during stress, stability, and regression tests. The goal is to reduce nondeterministic noise in eval results while preserving representative diversity across workloads and model variants. This protocol is intended for all eval-related automation (CI evals, nightly stress runs, private/dedicated shadowing, and benchmark suites).

Why we need a standardized seed/resampling protocol

- Eval instability is a major root cause of false positives in regression alerts and wasted developer time.
- Synthetic seeds and resampling policies control two orthogonal factors: reproducibility (exact-repeat debugging) and statistical representativeness (variance in distributional tests).
- Without standardization, teams use ad-hoc RNGs and sample sizes that lead to inconsistent F-score drift, noisy A/B comparisons, and fragile quantization verification.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to: eval-harness pipelines, prompt-set generators, synthetic workload producers, and model-onboarding testbeds.
- Out of scope: production request routing, customer data sampling (handled by data-management policies).

Key definitions

- seed: A 64-bit integer used as the root for deterministic PRNG chains.
- deterministic run: An eval execution that, given the same seed and config, must produce byte-for-byte identical synthetic inputs and stable metric computations (modulo model stochasticity when sampling is enabled).
- resample window: The policy time interval after which new synthetic seeds are introduced into continuous evals (e.g., daily, weekly).

Ownership and responsibilities

- Eval Platform (team): maintain the seed service, canonical RNG libraries, and automation for resampling. Owner: @eval-platform.
- Applied ML / Evals (team): define per-workload seed distributions, target sample sizes, and required statistical tests. Owner: @applied-ml.
- Model Onboarding Engineers: request additional deterministic seeds for debugging and certify new seed sets during model promotions.

Protocol: Seed generation and cataloging

1) Canonical RNG and format
   - Use the platform canonical PRNG: xoshiro256++ initialized from a 64-bit master seed. Implementations exist in Redwood's eval-sdks (python and go) at git:redwood/eval-sdks (module: redwood.eval.rng).
   - Seed metadata record (stringified JSON) must include: seed_id, seed_value (decimal), created_by, created_at (ISO-8601), tags (list), and checksum. Example: {\"seed_id\":\"sd-20260214-17\",\"seed_value\":\"9571623412341234\",\"created_by\":\"eval-platform\",\"created_at\":\"2026-02-14T17:23:00Z\",\"tags\":[\"nl-fewshot\",\"stress\"],\"checksum\":\"sha256:...\"}.

2) Seed catalog service
   - All seeds must be registered in the seed-catalog (internal HTTP API: seed-catalog.redwood.svc.cluster.local).
   - Seed records are immutable; if a seed is revoked, mark status=deprecated with a deprecation_reason.

3) Namespacing and tag schema
   - Use a three-part tag schema: workload-type (e.g., \"nl-classification\"), purpose (e.g., \"canary\", \"stress\"), and geography/locale (optional, e.g., \"en-US\").

4) Entropy and diversity constraints
   - For each synthetic workload generator, maintain a mapping of entropy budgets (percentiles of prompt template parameterization). The eval team must define minimum coverage constraints (e.g., template coverage >= 95% over canonical prompt set).

Resampling policy and cadence

- Static evals

Resampling policy and cadence

- Static evals (on PR): use fixed seed sets pinned in the PR config file. Re-run behavior must re-use the same seeds until the PR author updates the config.
- CI nightly/every-24h stress: rotate N seeds per workload where N depends on workload variance (see table below).
- Weekly/Canary pool: refresh 20% of the pool every week; full pool refresh every 12 weeks or when prompt-set changes exceed a threshold.

Resampling cadence table

| Eval type | Pool size (min) | Refresh policy | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------------|----------------|-----------|
| PR/unit (deterministic) | 8 | pinned per PR | Fast short runs; reproducibility prioritized |
| CI/nightly stress | 128 | rotate 8 seeds/day | Capture diversity; limit noise per run |
| Production shadow | 512 | rotate 64 seeds/day | Extensive coverage for real traffic emulation |
| Long-tail detection suite | 2048 | stratified monthly resample | Find edge-case regressions |

Statistical guidance and thresholds

- Minimum effective sample size (ESS): each eval-run must compute ESS for weighted metrics; ESS < 30 flags low-confidence.
- Metric variance threshold: 95th percentile rolling variance (7-day window) per-metric must remain below workload-specific thresholds. If variance > threshold, trigger triage flow.
- Regression alerting: require both (a) metric delta >= critical_delta and (b) p-value <= 0.01 using the recommended bootstrap test. Avoid single-run-based alerts.

Configuration examples

- YAML example for an eval job that consumes seed-catalog:

job_name: stress-qa-nl
workload: nl-generation
seed_pool: seed-catalog:tag=\"nl-generation,stress,en-US\"
pool_size: 128
rotate_per_run: 8
metrics: [bleu,rouge2,semantic-similarity]
critical_delta: 0.06
variance_thresholds:
  bleu: 0.02
  semantic-similarity: 0.015

CLI examples

- Create a new seed and register: 
  redwood-seed create --tags nl-generation,stress --created-by automated-resampler --output-json | curl -X POST \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @- https://seed-catalog.internal/api/v1/seeds

- Pull seed pool for job: 
  redwood-seed list --tags \"nl-generation,stress,en-US\" --limit 128 --format csv

Deterministic debug mode

- For failures that require exact replay, request the seed_id and run with --deterministic --seed-id <seed_id> flags. Deterministic runs use the same RNG chain and template parameterization, ensuring byte-for-byte identical synthetic inputs.

Integration with other eval concerns

- Quantization tests: tag seeds used for quant-eval as \"quant-sanity\"; keep a small dedicated pool (min 64) that is never rotated during a quant certification run to isolate numeric instability from sampling noise.
- Regression triage: link seed_id in regression tickets. The triage playbook should include steps to re-run failing workloads with the exact seed and with a nearby neighborhood of +/- 10 seeds to determine whether the failure is seed-specific or systematic.
- Prompt coverage: every resample must compute prompt-template coverage delta and fail if

seed and with a nearby neighborhood of +/- 10 seeds to determine whether the failure is seed-specific or systematic.
- Prompt coverage: every resample must compute prompt-template coverage delta and fail if coverage falls below 90% of the canonical set.

Failure modes and runbook pointers

- Symptom: high day-to-day metric variance without code or model changes.
  - Quick checks: verify seed-catalog returned the expected pool; check for unintended stochastic sampling flags; confirm PRNG library version.
  - If seed drift suspected: pin to earlier seed_id and re-run. See runbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/promotion-readiness-synthetic-quant-safety-playbook-2026

- Symptom: single-seed outliers causing regression alerts.
  - Triage: re-run with deterministic seed; run neighborhood of seeds (+/- 10); if only one seed fails, mark seed as flakey and deprecate in seed-catalog, then expand pool to maintain coverage.

Monitoring, dashboards, and SLOs

- Dashboards to create:
  - Eval Stability Overview: per-workload rolling variance, ESS, seed-pool utilization.
  - Seed Health: seed success rate, flakiness per-seed_id (failures/total runs), average runtime impact.

- SLOs:
  - Per-run ESS >= 50 for nightly stress (target) and ESS >= 30 (minimum).
  - Per-workload 7-day variance under threshold defined in workload config (default 0.03).
  - Seed catalog API 99.9% availability with 200ms median latency.

Rollout and updates

1) New seed sets must go through a staged rollout: 
   - Stage A (canary): 5% of nightly runs for 7 days, monitor variance and coverage.
   - Stage B (gradual): 25% for 14 days.
   - Stage C (full): 100% after no significant anomalies.
2) If any monitoring alert fires during canary, rollback to previous seed pool and open an incident with applied-ml and eval-platform.

Evaluator SDK: adapter patterns for private and dedicated eval integrations

Summary

This document describes the Evaluator SDK adapter patterns and operational guidance for integrating Redwood's eval harness into Dedicated and Private deployments. It covers design patterns for pluggable adapters, runtime requirements, telemetry mapping, privacy safeguards (DP-friendly workflows), quantization-aware evaluation hooks, and a recommended rollout checklist for operators. The target audience is applied ML engineers, platform engineers, and SREs responsible for operating eval pipelines inside customer-isolated environments.

Goals

- Provide repeatable adapter implementations that minimize changes to the central eval harness while allowing environment-specific integrations.
- Ensure consistent telemetry and metric semantics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private eval runs.
- Surface quantization and KV-cache artifacts in eval results to enable safe model promotion.
- Maintain privacy-preserving defaults when running shadow/recorded traffic in customer-controlled networks.

When to use this doc

- You are integrating Redwood's eval harness into a Dedicated cluster or a Private (VPC/on-prem) control plane.
- You need consistent metrics and artifact collection between hosted and private evals.
- You need a privacy-preserving shadow evaluation pipeline for customer traffic.

Design overview

The Evaluator SDK is split into three layers:

1) Core harness: evaluation logic, scoring, sample orchestration, and result aggregation.
2) Adapter interface (stable): a thin shim that implements environment-specific behaviors (persistence, RPC, telemetry, secrets).
3) Runtime plugins: small, replaceable modules that adapt to local infra (S3 vs. MinIO, Prometheus pushgateway vs. remote write, HSM vs. KMS).

Adapter responsibilities

Each adapter must implement the following logical responsibilities (interface-level):

- storage_put(key, payload, metadata): persist artifacts (responses, token traces, KV cache snapshots).
- storage_get(key): read artifact for replay or analysis.
- telemetry_emit(metric_name, value, labels): emit evaluation metrics with canonical labels.
- secret_get(secret_ref): fetch credentials (wraps KMS/HSM call if needed).
- request_send(endpoint, payload, timeout_ms): invoke a runtime endpoint (used for shadow-routing or live model probes).
- sanitize_input(input): enforce privacy filters (PII redaction/zeroization) before storing.

Pattern 1 — File-backed adapter (recommended for Private evals)

- Use case: on-prem or air-gapped evals where object stores are available via POSIX or S3-compatible APIs.
- Implementation notes: adapter writes to local object store under /var/lib/eval/artifacts/<run-id> and emits a manifest.json. Use atomic renames for finalize.

Example config snippet (confluence-style table represented in text):

| key | value | notes |
| --- | ----- | ----- |
| storage.type | s3 | MinIO endpoint for private deployments |
| storage.bucket | eval-artifacts-prod | per-customer bucket |
| auth.kms | hsm:/slot1 | optional HSM URI |

Pattern 2 — Prometheus-bridge adapter (telemetry-forwarding)

- Use case: Dedicated deployments push eval metrics into customer's Prometheus (pull) or centralized remote_write endpoint.
- Implementation notes: provide two modes — pushgateway for short-lived runs or remote_write for high-throughput. Normalize metric names to

Dedicated deployments push eval metrics into customer's Prometheus (pull) or centralized remote_write endpoint.
- Implementation notes: provide two modes — pushgateway for short-lived runs or remote_write for high-throughput. Normalize metric names to the canonical schema used by hosted evals (see Metric mapping).

Metric mapping (canonical)

- eval.samples.count (int) — total inputs run
- eval.latency.p50_ms, eval.latency.p95_ms, eval.latency.p99_ms (ms)
- eval.quality.score.<metric> (float) — e.g., bleu, f1, semantic-similarity
- eval.kv_cache.hit_rate (float) — measured on replayed long-context probes
- eval.quant.delta_perplexity (float) — difference vs. fp16 baseline

Adapters MUST emit these names or provide a 1:1 mapping table in their config.

Pattern 3 — RPC proxy adapter (for dedicated control planes)

- Use case: Dedicated control planes cannot reach the central model registry. Adapter proxies requests to local model-serving endpoints and returns standard responder objects.
- Implementation notes: validate model version IDs against a local whitelist before invoking to prevent unintended promotions. Implement circuit-breakers and exponential backoff.

Privacy & PII safeguards

When dealing with customer traffic you must treat recorded inputs as sensitive. The adapter interface includes sanitize_input which is invoked before any artifact is persisted. Default sanitization rules:

1) Remove 1st- and 2nd-party PII (emails, SSNs, credit card numbers) using Redwood's pii-redactor regex set (v2).
2) Hash long-form free-text using blake2b-64 for indexing while storing redacted text.
3) For DP-mode runs (used for shared benchmarks), the adapter should apply per-sample Gaussian noise to embedding vectors and redact token-level attention maps.

DP-mode example (YAML config snippet):

```yaml
privacy:
  mode: dp
  dp_epsilon: "2.0"
  dp_delta: "1e-6"
  embedding_noise_std: 0.03
  redact_attention: true
```

Running quantization-aware evals

Quantization introduces subtle failure modes. The Evaluator SDK provides hooks to capture artifacts that matter to promotion decisions:

- kv_cache_snapshot: capture representative KV cache after a 1k token warmup run (format: base64 gzipped protobuf).
- perf_profile: per-step flops/op timings and kernel selection logs (text).
- logits_diff: per-token L2 difference vs. float baseline for a small probe set.

The adapter must support streaming large artifacts to object storage with resumable multipart uploads. For air-gapped sites, provide an offline export tool (tar + manifest + signature).

Operational checklist for deploying Eval SDK adapters

1) Preflight (owner: platform team)
   - Confirm object store endpoints and credentials are provisioned.
   - Verify Prometheus remote_write or pushgateway is reachable.
   - Validate KMS/HSM integration with secret_get contract.

2) Canary (owner: applied ML)
   - Run a 1000-sample synthetic benchmark with dp mode off. Verify metric parity within tolerance against hosted baseline.
   - Confirm emitted metrics appear in metrics backend with correct labels.

3) Shadow validation (owner: product/platform)
   - Shadow 1% of production traffic for 24 hours with privacy.mode: redact. Compare quality.score.* and latency percentiles.

4) Promotion gating (owner: model-onboarding)
   - Require: eval.quality.score.semantic_similarity >= hosted_baseline - 0.02 AND eval.kv_cache.hit_rate >=

- Shadow 1% of production traffic for 24 hours with privacy.mode: redact. Compare quality.score.* and latency percentiles.

4) Promotion gating (owner: model-onboarding)
   - Require: eval.quality.score.semantic_similarity >= hosted_baseline - 0.02 AND eval.kv_cache.hit_rate >= 0.9
   - Require: eval.quant.delta_perplexity <= 5.0 for quantized candidates

5) Rollout (owner: eng-sre)
   - Gradual rollout schedule: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with 24h observation windows and automated rollback on regression alerts.

Integration examples

1) Minimal Python adapter skeleton\n```python
class FileAdapter(AdapterBase):
    def __init__(self, root):
        self.root = root
    def storage_put(self, key, payload, metadata):
        path = os.path.join(self.root, key)
        atomic_write(path, payload)
    def telemetry_emit(self, name, value, labels):
        # map to prometheus or local sink
        push_metric(name, value, labels)
    def sanitize_input(self, input):
        return pii_redact(input)
```

2) Example eval run command (CLI)

```bash
redwood-eval run --suite semantic-sim --samples 5000 --adapter-config ./adapter.yaml --run-id r2026-02-10-01
```

Troubleshooting & common pitfalls

- Missing metric labels: ensure adapters add the canonical labels: run_id, suite, model_id, env (private/dedicated/hosted). Alerts will trigger if run_id is absent.
- Multipart uploads failing in air-gapped mode: use the offline export tool and verify manifest signature before ingestion.
- Baseline mismatch: if quant.delta_perplexity >> threshold, capture logits_diff and kv_cache_snapshot and open a triage run using regression-triage playbook.

Ownership and contacts

- Evaluator SDK maintainer: Marco Liang (applied-ml infra) — slack: @marco.liang
- Platform adapter support: Eng Platform team — eng-platform oncall
- Security/privacy review: Aisha Patel (security)

Appendix: artifact schema (text table)

| artifact | format | retention default |
| kv_cache_snapshot | base64+gz+pb | 30d |
| perf_profile | text | 90d |
| logits_diff | csv | 30d |
| manifest.json | json | 90d |

Backwards compatibility notes

- Adapters must support the v1 storage contract until 2027-06-30. The v2 contract introduces multipart checksums and signed uploads; set compatibility: v1 in adapter.yaml to opt in.

Probe Rotation and Eval Garden Manifest

Summary and intent:

This document defines the Eval Garden pattern and the Probe Rotation Manifest: a coordinated, budget-aware system for keeping probe sets (synthetic and production-derived) fresh, diverse, and locality-aware across shadow, dedicated, and private deployments. The goal is to make continuous evaluation resilient to drift, quantization artifacts, and configuration changes while minimizing cost and annotation overhead.

Goals:
- Ensure representative probes are exercised across all serving modes (hosted, dedicated, private) on a repeatable cadence.
- Maintain an auditable, versioned rotation policy for probes so that regressions are attributable and reproducible.
- Make the eval schedule locality- and workload-aware (per-customer slices, long-tail intents, and long-context interactions).
- Integrate quantization-awareness into probe selection so probes sensitive to numeric compression are prioritized pre-rollout.

High-level concepts:
- Eval Garden: a logical collection of probe beds (groups) that map to slices, regions, and model-variant compatibility. Examples: "assistant-core", "forms-extraction-longctx", "embeddings-english-high-similarity".
- Probe: an individual test item (prompt + context + expected checks). Probes can be synthetic, anonymized production traces, or human-curated edgecases.
- Probe Bed: a group of probes with shared scheduling rules and ownership.
- Rotation Policy: per-bed schedule describing cadence, retention, sampling strategy, and budget allocation.
- Probe TTL and Decay: probes age out to prioritize new coverage; decay controls probability of re-selection.

Architecture and components:
- Probe Registry (service): stores probe metadata, labels, signatures, provenance, and quant-sensitivity flags. Every probe has a stable id: PR-<sha1>.
- Gardener Scheduler: a policy engine that materializes rotation plans as yields for the Eval Runner. Supports locality constraints (region, tenant, model-variant).
- Eval Runner / Shadow Harness: executes probes against target endpoints (shadow, dedicated, private) and records telemetry to Eval Ingest.
- Eval Ingest / Metrics Pipeline: normalizes outputs, extracts token-level deltas, embedding-similarity logs, and checklist failures.
- Probe Monitor & Alerting: computes freshness, coverage, and regression scores; surfaces P0/P1 regressions and health trends.

Probe lifecycle (detailed):
1) Authoring: probes are authored via the Probe Registry UI or CLI. Every probe includes: text, seed context, deterministic RNG seed (optional), annotations (slices, sensitivity tags), and a quant-sensitivity score (0-1) produced by a quick local check.
2) Vetting: new probes run in a preflight bucket (30 runs across model seeds) to estimate variance and flakiness. Probes with high variance flagged as "unstable" and quarantined.
3) Assignment to Bed: owners assign probes to a Probe Bed and select Rotation Policy.
4) Rotation: the Gardener Scheduler selects probes for the next cycle respecting constraints: budget (token-cost cap), locality, minimum-bed-coverage, and probe TTL.
5) Execution: Eval Runner executes probes and sends normalized results.
6) Scoring & Archival: probes that exceed failure thresholds are promoted to triage workflows or archived if obsolete.

Rotation policy template (YAML example):

# rotation-policy.yaml
name: forms-extraction-longctx-rotation
bed_id: BED-forms-longctx
cadence: weekly            # daily | weekly | monthly | on-demand
budget_tokens_per_cycle: 200000   # gross token budget across all runs
min_bed_coverage: 90       # percent

workflows or archived if obsolete.

Rotation policy template (YAML example):

# rotation-policy.yaml
name: forms-extraction-longctx-rotation
bed_id: BED-forms-longctx
cadence: weekly            # daily | weekly | monthly | on-demand
budget_tokens_per_cycle: 200000   # gross token budget across all runs
min_bed_coverage: 90       # percent of probes to touch before reusing
locality_constraints: [eu-west-1, us-east-1]
quant_priority_threshold: 0.6   # probes with quant-sens >= this get 2x weight
sample_strategy: stratified_by_slice
decay_half_life_days: 21
max_runs_per_probe: 10
flaky_retest_policy: 3
owner: feature-forms-team

Scheduling rules (bulleted):
- If quant_priority_threshold triggers, schedule those probes earlier in the cycle and mark for per-quant-mode runs (e.g., 8-bit, mixed).
- Maintain at least one warmup run on a matched-cold-cache replica before taking samples used for production gating.
- Prefer probes that have not run in last TTL days until min_bed_coverage satisfied.
- Reserve 20% of budget for high-variance probes (flaky-retest pool).

ASCII table: (example cadence vs budget allocation)

| Cadence | Budget Tokens | Retention Window | Typical Bed Size | Notes |
| daily   | 50k           | 7 days           | 200-400 probes   | focused smoke & critical slices |
| weekly  | 200k          | 30 days          | 1k-3k probes     | broader coverage & quant-sensitivity |
| monthly | 800k          | 90 days          | 5k+ probes       | long-tail, multilingual sweep |

Telemetry and signal mapping:
- Per-probe outputs: response tokens, latency p50/p95/p99, failure checklist flags, embedding similarity vs gold (cosine), top-k log-prob delta, hallucination score (syntactic and factual heuristics).
- Derived signals: probe-failure-rate (30d EWMA), probe-flakiness-index, quant-degradation-index (per-quant-mode), slice-stability-score.
- Alerts: Team-level alerts fire when slice-stability-score drops > 6% in a week or quant-degradation-index crosses 0.15.

Alert thresholds (recommended):
- P0: any probe in "critical" slice that flips to incorrect output for 100% of runs across 3 seeds -> immediate pager.
- P1: slice-stability-score drop > 6% for 7d with absolute failure-rate > 2% -> Slack triage channel.
- P2: probe-flakiness-index > 0.4 for > 14d -> ticket to steward.

Runbook: responding to a failing rotation cycle (quick path):
1) Triage owner notified by PagerDuty (P0) or Slack (P1).
2) Escalation checklist:
   a) Confirm failing probe id and bed. Collect last 7 successful runs and diffs.
   b) Check model-variant and quant-mode combinator matrix for recent rollouts.
   c) Re-run failing probe in isolated environment with deterministic seed and verbose tracing enabled.
   d) If failure reproduces only under quantized modes, tag as QUANT-REGRESSION and follow the Quant Fallback policy.
3) If regression affects multiple beds or slices, trigger shadow-rollforward containment: revert traffic to previous model-variant or enable automatic fallback route.
4) Document triage outcome in the Probe Registry ticket and attach delta artifacts (tokens, traces, attribution).

Ownership and service-levels:
- Bed owner: maintains probe bed content, rotation policy, and acts as first responder for its alerts. (Examples: feature-forms-team, embeddings-core).
- Eval Platform: responsible for reliability of Gardener Scheduler, Eval Runner infra, and metrics pipeline. SLA: 99.9% job-scheduling success per cycle.
- Onboarding requirement: any model promotion to "production" must have passed 3 full rotation cycles across affected beds with

Gardener Scheduler, Eval Runner infra, and metrics pipeline. SLA: 99.9% job-scheduling success per cycle.
- Onboarding requirement: any model promotion to "production" must have passed 3 full rotation cycles across affected beds with quant-priority runs if applicable.

Model onboarding integration notes:
- As part of inference-readiness checks: require a rotation plan that includes at least one high-confidence probe bed exercised under the target quant-mode and a verification of embedding drift < 0.02 on representative slices.
- Shadow Promotion Gate: promotion requires no new P0s and less than 1% new slice regressions after 3 rotations.

Quantization-aware guidance:
- Tag probes with quant-sensitivity: run a small local quant-scan (reference tool: tools/quant-scan) that returns a sensitivity metric. Anything > 0.6 should be executed early and at increased sample count.
- Mixed precision and hybrid deployments should have separate probe-beds to isolate numeric-compression effects.

Operational examples (CLI):
- Register a probe: 
  rwd-probe register --file probe.json --bed BED-forms-longctx --owner feature-forms-team
- Schedule a one-off rotation run: 
  rwd-gardener run --bed BED-forms-longctx --mode on-demand --quant-modes 8bit,mix16
- Query probe health: 
  rwd-probe status --probe-id PR-1a2b3c --last 30d

Sample probe manifest (JSON; stored in Probe Registry):
{
  "id": "PR-1a2b3c",
  "bed": "BED-forms-longctx",
  "text": "Extract customer name from a 2-page receipt with overlapping OCR noise.",
  "context": "{page1:..., page2:...}",
  "owner": "feature-forms-team",
  "tags": ["long-context", "ocr-noise", "critical"],
  "quant_sensitivity": "0.72",
  "created": "2025-10-04"
}

Best practices and heuristics:
- Keep probes small but representative; long probes are expensive—split into anchored micro-probes when possible.
- Maintain explicit provenance: label origin (synthetic vs anon-prod) and the sampling policy used to create the probe.
- Annotate ownership and replacement criteria so beds can be rotated by non-authors after 90 days without re-approval.
- Use the flakiness pool to periodically re-evaluate and either stabilize or retire noisy probes.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations
- False-positive regressions due to tokenization drift: mitigation -> include tokenizer version/tag in run metadata and fail gating on stable-tokenizer runs only.
- Regression only under long-context: mitigation -> pre-warm KV cache and include warmup run to get stable performance baseline.
- Quantization-induced semantic drift: mitigation -> increase sample count for quant-sensitive probes and compare embedding-similarity profiles before gating.

References and links:
- See also: "probe-lifecycle" checklist (internal link), "quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024" and "shadow-rollforward-and-mesh-simulation-playbook-2026" for rollback policies.

Micro-Canary Eval Orchestrator and Fast-Fail Protocol

Summary:

This page describes the Micro-Canary Eval Orchestrator (MCEO), a lightweight evaluation and monitoring pattern designed to detect and triage regressions from deployment events with minimal cost and low latency. The MCEO sits inside the eval-harness and is intended for fast-turnaround verification of change windows (model rollouts, quantization patches, prompt rewrites, routing rules). It complements full-stage shadow and production evaluations by catching high-signal, high-impact regressions within minutes.

Goals:
- Detect degradations that materially affect customer-facing slices within the first 1–30 minutes after a change.
- Provide deterministic fast-fail criteria and an automated mitigation/rollback trigger path.
- Keep compute and annotation cost < 3% of a full CI eval run for typical models.
- Produce actionable telemetry and a standardized triage packet for oncall and model teams.

When to run MCEO:
- Canary rollouts of new model versions or quantized artifacts.
- Prompt/template updates that change structured outputs (JSON schema changes).
- Configuration changes affecting routing, batching, or KV cache behavior.
- Emergency quick checks after hotfixes.

Architecture and Components:
1) Orchestrator service (lightweight):
   - Responsible for scheduling micro-canary jobs, collecting results, and evaluating thresholds.
   - API endpoints: POST /microcanary/start, GET /microcanary/status, POST /microcanary/abort.
   - Owner: eval-harness team.

2) Mini-workload generator:
   - A curated subset of 50–500 prompts per canary (adaptive by model type). Prompts are drawn from the production prompt catalog with stratified sampling across high-impact slices.
   - Includes payloads to exercise streaming, function-calling, and embeddings where relevant.

3) Fast-eval telemetry collector:
   - Lightweight traces (latency p50/p95/p99), token counts, model logits summary, embedding cosine drift, structured-validation failures.
   - Event tags: change_id, rollout_id, model_revision, quant_profile, route.

4) Decision engine (rule + ML hybrid):
   - Rule checks: absolute thresholds (latency > X ms, structured-fail rate > Y%) and delta thresholds (metric_regression > Z% relative to baseline).
   - ML assistant: an anomaly detector that ingests short-term windows to suppress noisy false positives for low-volume slices.

Canary Configuration (example in JSON):
```
{
  "canary_name": "microcanary-frontend-nl-2026-02-10",
  "model_revision": "redwood-v2.3-quant-a8",
  "sample_size": 120,
  "max_duration_minutes": 20,
  "slices": ["billing-clarity", "multi-turn-support", "json-schema-output"],
  "thresholds": {
    "p95_latency_ms": 500,
    "structured_validation_fail_rate": 0.025,
    "embedding_cosine_drop": 0.08
  },
  "rollback_action": "auto-rollback-on-critical",
  "notify_channels": ["#canary-alerts", "pagerduty:ml-canary-signal"]
}
```

Operational Runbook (step-by-step):
1) Schedule: trigger via CI/CD pipeline or manually from Console > Eval Harness > Micro-Canary.
2) Start: Orchestrator reserves a micro-slot against dedicated eval capacity (or falls back to burst pool).
3) Execute: the mini-workload generator issues requests to the target endpoint with recording enabled.
4) Collect: telemetry is streamed to the fast-eval collector (ingest retention 48 hours).
5) Evaluate: Decision engine runs rule checks then ML anomaly suppression.
6) Resolve:
   6.1) If no thresholds exceeded: mark canary success, annotate change with canary_id and attach summary.
   6.2) If thresholds exceeded but non-critical (e.g., minor p95 drift < configured hard-fail delta): open a P0 investigation ticket but do not auto-rollback.
   6.3) If critical thresholds exceeded (structured-validation_fail_rate >= critical threshold OR p95

thresholds exceeded but non-critical (e.g., minor p95 drift < configured hard-fail delta): open a P0 investigation ticket but do not auto-rollback.
   6.3) If critical thresholds exceeded (structured-validation_fail_rate >= critical threshold OR p95 latency >= emergency threshold): trigger configured rollback action and fire PagerDuty.

Fast-Fail Criteria (examples):
- Critical: structured_validation_fail_rate >= 5% for any high-impact slice OR p95_latency_mm >= 2000 ms for streaming endpoints.
- High: structured_validation_fail_rate in [2.5%, 5%) AND regression from baseline > 40%
- Medium: embedding_cosine_drop between 0.05 and 0.08 for production embedding-using routes (requires manual review).

Telemetry and Triage Packet (what gets produced on failure):
- Canary metadata (canary_name, change_id, timestamp, model_revision).
- Compact telemetry snapshot (latency histogram, token distribution, top 5 prompts with worst regressions).
- Response diffs: golden baseline vs candidate response for top N failures (text diffs and structured-JSON diff).
- Minimal reproduction bundle: 10 representative requests and full raw responses, links to logs and a short human-friendly summary.

Escalation and Ownership:

2) Confirm sample_size maps to at least 10 requests per slice.
3) Set thresholds relative to recent baseline (use last-7-days median).
4) Attach rollout_id and change_id to telemetry.
5) Add reviewer(s) in the canary config for manual overrides.

- Full CI eval: results of MCEO are included in the release artifact and stored for 90 days for regression analysis.
- Regression triage: MCEO failure packets automatically create a regression triage ticket with a standardized template.

- Keep canary prompts stable across short windows to avoid noisy drift. If prompts must change, version them with canary config.
- Be conservative with auto-rollback on low-signal slices; use ML suppression to reduce false alarms.
- Watch for caching-related flakiness. If canary interacts with KV cache, run a cache-warm step before measurement.
- For quantization rollouts, include deterministic prompt seeds to surface numeric instabilities.

Adaptive Context Fingerprint and Runtime Quant Routing Playbook

Overview

This playbook documents the design, probes, and operational procedures for the Adaptive Context Fingerprint subsystem and its companion Runtime Quant Routing service. The goal is to enable safe, latency-aware routing between quantized model variants at inference time based on a lightweight fingerprint of request context and live telemetry.

Intended audience
- Applied ML engineers
- Serving runtime engineers
- Oncall/eval teams responsible for rollouts and regression triage

Goals and success criteria
- Reduce per-token cost by routing up to 35% of eligible requests to 4-bit or mixed-precision variants without exceeding a 0.8 point coherence delta (on our coherence scoring metric) for any critical slice.
- Maintain tail latency P95 <= 120ms for the primary low-latency path; allow P95 <= 220ms on fallback non-latency-critical routes.
- Detect and automatically rollback quant routing within 10 minutes of detecting a fidelity regression above configured thresholds.

Scope
- Applies to text-generation and chat endpoints served by the runtime service 'inference-gateway' and the quant manager 'quant-router'.
- Not in scope: full model conversion tooling (handled by model-onboarding), dataset-level retraining, or private deployment networking restrictions (see eng-private-deployments docs).

Key concepts and definitions
- Context Fingerprint: a lossy, fixed-size descriptor derived from request metadata + prompt embedding sketch used to quickly cluster similar requests for routing decisions.
- Coherence Score: an internal metric (0-100) that measures output semantic consistency against an anchored reference for a slice. Lower is worse.
- Eligibility Predicate: deterministic checks (length, tokens, function-calls, persona flags) to opt out of quant routing.

Design overview
1) Lightweight fingerprinting: compute a 256-bit fingerprint per request at the API ingress. Fingerprint inputs: prompt token summary (first 256 bytes and last 256 bytes), intent tag, embedding sketch (64-d float quantized to 8-bit), and call_mode flag.
2) Fingerprint-to-slice mapping: fingerprint bucketization using locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) produces slice_id. Each slice_id maps to a routing policy containing preferred model variants and fallback chains.
3) Runtime quant routing decision: the quant-router evaluates slice-level telemetry (recent coherence delta, latency heatmap, token-rate) + request-level predicate to select a target variant: full-fp32, mixed-precision-8, mixed-quant-4, or cache-hit reuse.
4) Safety gates: pre-checks enforce that any request containing attachments, function calls, or privileged customer data is routed to full-fp32.

Telemetry signals and thresholds
- coherence_delta_rolling_mean (slice, 1h): trigger > 0.8 points 
- coherence_outlier_ratio (slice, 30m): trigger > 0.03 (3%)
- p95_latency (variant, 10m): soft limit > 220ms; hard limit > 300ms (immediate fallback)
- token_error_rate (variant, 10m): trigger > 0.005 (0.5%)
- kv_cache_miss_rate (slice, 5m): trigger > 0.2 for latency-sensitive paths

Eligibility rules (ordered checks)
1) If request contains function-calls -> route to full-fp32.
2) If request.customer_tier == "enterprise-sensitive" -> route to full-fp32.
3) If prompt_length

2) If request.customer_tier == "enterprise-sensitive" -> route to full-fp32.
3) If prompt_length > 8192 tokens -> route to full-fp32.
4) If request has strong negative-safety-flag -> route to full-fp32.
5) Else consult slice routing policy.

Probe synthesis and evaluation strategy
- Purpose: create targeted synthetic probes that exercise the coherence and latency boundaries of a slice under quant variants without exposing production traffic.
- Probe types:
  - Minimal-context probes: short prompts that check token-level fluency and function-call behavior.
  - Long-context probes: sequences designed to stress KV cache and attention patterns (8k–32k token equivalents).
  - Persona fidelity probes: anchored Q/A pairs where answers must match gold-standard responses within a semantic threshold.

- Probe cadence: generate 200 probes per slice for a new quant profile; schedule nightly against a shadow cluster.
- Scoring and acceptance: metric suite returns coherence_delta, hallucination_rate, token-level edit distance, and latency. A profile is acceptable if coherence_delta <= 0.5 and hallucination_rate <= 0.01 across critical slices.

Runtime routing policy schema (human-readable table)
| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| slice_id | logical fingerprint bucket | slice_2026_04_ml_readme |

Rollout and promotion workflow (for a new quant profile)
1) Author prepares quant-profile artifact and baseline evaluation report. Upload to artifact store 'quant-artifacts'.
2) Create a promotion MR with attached probe results and slice map. Tag reviewers: runtime, eval, SRE.
3) Stage shadow rollout: 100% of probes + 0.5% of mirrored production traffic on 'shadow-quant' cluster for 24 hours. Monitor telemetry.
4) Canary rollout: apply routing policy to 1% production traffic for 2 hours -> if stable expand to 5% for 4 hours -> 20% for 8 hours -> 50% for 24 hours -> 100% after 48 hours of stability.
5) Automated rollback triggers if any soft threshold is exceeded for more than 2 consecutive windows or a hard threshold is exceeded once.

Monitoring and alerts
- primary dashboards:
  - Quant routing health (per-slice coherence_delta, p95_latency, token_error_rate)
  - Variant capacity and queue depth (model-serve-pool dashboards)

Triage and rollback playbook (quick steps)
1) Acknowledge alert and identify affected slice(s) from dashboard.
2) Switch routing policy to next-safe fallback (immediate API call to quant-router): PATCH /routing/slices/{slice_id} -> set primary_variant = fallback_chain[2] (usually FP32).
3) Re-run targeted probe set to confirm mitigation within 10 minutes.
4) Open regression triage ticket with dataset and probe artifacts attached. Assign to eval-oncall.
5) If no mitigation, escalate to Model Onboarding + Runtime Kernel team.

Safety considerations and known limitations
- Fingerprint collisions: LSH bucketization can group semantically distinct prompts; maintain conservative coherence budgets for high-cardinality buckets.
- Cold-start slices: new slices without sufficient probe history default to conservative routing (mp8 -> fp32) until N=200 probes collected.
- Privacy: fingerprint must not retain raw prompt text. Use hashed sketches only. Compliance checked in 'probe-privacy-audit' job.

Promotion Readiness: Cross-Stage Synthetic Simulation & Quantization Safety Playbook

Summary

This playbook defines a combined evaluation and safety protocol used to decide when a model artifact can be promoted from evaluation (canary/validation) into production routing. It coordinates three corridors of checks: 1) synthetic user simulation to validate behavioral and distributional stability, 2) quantization & kernel-sensitivity safety checks for performance-preserving transforms, and 3) lightweight runtime smoke and canary procedures to exercise operational invariants. The goal is deterministic, reproducible promotion decisions tied to explicit pass/fail signals and rollback criteria.

Scope and Use Cases

- Applies to any model promotion that will be served by Redwood runtime variants where quantized or variant kernels (FP16/INT8/QLoRA-style) are in the promotion path.
- Intended for models with expected production throughput above 1 qps/customer or with regulatory/data-sensitivity constraints (customer PII handling).
- Not required for experimental sandbox promotions under 24h unless flagged by product as critical.

Definitions

- Promotion: the act of moving a model from staging/canary to a production route where customer traffic is served.
- Synthetic Actor: a deterministic user-simulation profile used to exercise prompts and contexts representative of production usage.
- Quant Safety Check: a set of deterministic tests that validate output fidelity and KV-cache integrity across quantized kernels.

Ownership and Roles

- Model Owner (primary): ML engineer who produced the model artifact and is responsible for test bundles, prompt sets, and baseline metrics.
- Eval Owner: engineering squad responsible for running the synthetic actor harness and interpreting results.
- Runtime Owner: infra/runtime team responsible for quantization tooling, kernel selection, and performance baselining.
- Release Approver: product or platform PM with final sign-off for non-emergency promotions.

Acceptance Criteria (summary table)

- For each criterion below the format is: Criterion | Pass Threshold | Primary Signal | Escalation
  - Behavioral stability | Delta <= 1.5% on core pass-rate metrics across prompt-slices | aggregate pass-rate time series (7k sample window) | Auto-fail -> regression-triage
  - Semantic drift | Embedding cosine shift < 0.06 median across intent clusters | embedding distribution KL (staging vs baseline) | Review required
  - Exact-match integrity for CI prompts | 100% for deterministic QA prompts | golden-answer diff report | Auto-fail
  - Quantized fidelity | Top-1 response similarity >= 95% (ROUGE-L or BLEU for fixed tasks), and human-annotated quality delta <= 0.5 on sampled prompts | batch-diff + human spot-check | Rollback & quant-retry
  - KV-cache parity | no cache corruption observed in 10k simulated long-context requests | kernel log parity + checksum | Runtime rollback
  - Latency and tail | p99 < target_latency and p99_tail_spikes < 10% over baseline | telemetry time-series | Canary throttling

Design: Synthetic Actor Harness

- Purpose: emulate real user behavior without shipping customer data.

Design: Synthetic Actor Harness

- Purpose: emulate real user behavior without shipping customer data. Synthetic actors combine prompt skeletons, variable slot content generators, and timing distributions.
- Actors are stored as JSON bundles: {actor_id, intent_weight, prompt_templates[], context_length_dist, slot_generators[]}. Example actor fragment below.

Example actor JSON (representative):

{
  "actor_id": "support_search_v2",
  "intent_weight": "0.18",
  "prompt_templates": [
    "User: {{query}}\nAssistant:",
    "Given the following product description: {{desc}}\nSummarize:"
  ],
  "context_length_dist": "poisson(λ=64)",
  "slot_generators": ["wiki-snippet-sampler", "customer-nounizer-v2"]
}

- Scenario catalog (must cover):
  1) Short-form Q&A (<=64 tokens) - 40% weight.
  2) Long-context summarization (>=1024 tokens) - 25% weight.
  3) Multi-step instruction with tool-calls emulation - 10% weight.
  4) Edge adversarial variants (typos, hallucination probes) - 15% weight.
  5) Rare-entity and numeric reasoning - 10% weight.

- Execution: run 3 independent seeds per actor with deterministic RNG to allow diffs. Collect full traces including prompt, logits (sample), KV-cache checksums, and returned tokens. Store artifacts in the eval artifact bucket with the tag: promotion/<model>:<sha>.

Quantization & Kernel Safety Checks

- Purpose: verify that quant transforms and kernel selections do not induce unacceptable semantic/functional regressions.
- Automated checks:
  - Layer-wise output delta: run a 500-sample micro-batch and compute per-layer L2 and cosine delta vs baseline FP32. Thresholds: median L2 < 1e-3, cosine > 0.999.
  - End-to-end behavioral delta: use the synthetic actor prompt set, compute pass-rate deltas and embedding shifts.
  - KV-cache replay: for long-context runs, serialize and replay KV-cache through quantized kernels and validate checksums.
  - Failure-mode detector: fuzz a subset of kernels with perturbed inputs to detect NaNs/inf or divergence outliers.

- Tooling commands (example):
  - Quant bake: 
    redwood-quant bake --model model.tgz --profile int8-s90 --output quantized/model-int8.tgz
  - Layer compare: 
    redwood-compare-layers --base model_fp32 --candidate model_int8 --samples 500 --out report.html

Runtime Smoke Test Suite

- Purpose: exercise operational invariants (metrics, logs, tracing) before opening production traffic.
- Keys:
  - Load profile: synthetic actors at 1x, 5x expected qps for 10 minutes each.
  - Observability checks: ensure traces propagate, token-level billing counters accurate, request IDs preserved.
  - Telemetry asserts: no more than 0.2% errors, p95 latency regression < 10% of baseline.

Canary Promotion Procedure (numbered)

1) Artifact upload: Model owner uploads artifact, test bundles, and promotion metadata to the staging registry.
2) Preflight: CI runs unit tests, deterministic QA prompts, and the synthetic actor harness end-to-end. Reject on auto-fail signals.
3) Quant safety pass: Runtime Owner runs quant checks and signs off or files quant-issue ticket.
4) Smoke run: Deploy to isolated canary pool (1% traffic) with synthetic traffic overlay and 30m observation window.
5) Rollout phases: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% by automated policy, each stage gated by acceptance criteria

isolated canary pool (1% traffic) with synthetic traffic overlay and 30m observation window.
5) Rollout phases: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% by automated policy, each stage gated by acceptance criteria evaluation window (30m for small models, 60m for L>8k contexts).
6) Monitoring guardrails: automated rollback triggers include: behavioral stability fail, KV-cache parity fail, p99 latency > threshold, or error rate spike > configured delta.
7) Post-promotion audit: collect artifacts, diff reports, and human spot-check on 200 sampled prompts.

Automated Alerting and Rollback Rules

- Alert channels: PagerDuty to Runtime on severity=1 (KV-cache corruption), Slack #runtime-ops for severity=2, email to model-owner for degraded quality signals.
- Auto-rollback thresholds (examples):
  - Behavioral pass-rate drop >= 2% absolute in sliding 10m window -> automatic rollback.
  - KV-cache checksum mismatch (any) during canary -> immediate rollback and incident start.
  - p99 latency > baseline_p99 * 1.5 for 10 minutes -> gradual throttle and rollback if persists.

Data and Artifact Retention

- All synthetic-run artifacts and diff reports for a promotion must be retained for 90 days under eval-artifacts/<model>/<sha> with TTL tags.
- Human annotation records from the spot-check should be stored with reviewer id and comments.

Failure & Triage Process

- If automated checks fail, create a regression ticket with: title, failing signals, links to artifacts, investigator assignment. Use label: regressions/promotion.
- Regression triage steps:
  1) Reproduce in isolated environment (runtime owner + model owner).
  2) Run layer-diff and kernel-fuzz tests.
  3) If quant-related, attempt quant-profile fallback (e.g., int8->int8-s95 or int16) and re-run harness.
  4) If behavioral, escalate to applied-ml for annotation and root-cause.

Auditability & Sign-off

- Each successful promotion must include the following artifacts in the promotion ticket: artifact SHA, synthetic-run summary report, quant-compare report, smoke-run telemetry snapshot, human spot-check results, release approver signature.
- The Release Approver records the promotion decision and any exceptions in the promotion ticket.

Hybrid slice-eval and quant-aware prompt-rewrite playbook

Summary

This playbook defines the hybrid slice-driven evaluation workflow that combines: (a) stratified slice evaluation across production-like prompt distributions, and (b) quantization-aware prompt rewrites used as a lightweight mitigation for quality regressions introduced by lower-precision model variants. The goal is to detect, triage, and (where safe) automatically mitigate quality regressions caused or amplified by quantization and runtime interactions without blocking throughput or availability.

Why this exists

- Quantized model variants and mixed-precision rollouts reduce cost but can cause localized failure modes on specific prompt slices (e.g., numeric tables, code, multi-step reasoning).
- Existing holistic evals hide slice-level failures; owners need a repeatable way to detect degradations, diagnose root cause (model vs prompt sensitivity vs cache interaction), and apply minimal interventions such as prompt rewrites or routing rules.

Scope and exclusions

- In scope: text generation and chat endpoints, embeddings when downstream quality depends on prompt framing, integration with the eval-harness for batch and shadow runs, quant profiles (int8/int4/hybrid) handled by the runtime.
- Out of scope: training-time fixes, privacy-preserving DP transforms (see privacy-first-shadow-eval elsewhere), large-scale dataset relabeling.

Ownership and contacts

- Playbook owner: Applied ML — Maya Chen (author)
- Runtime integration: Serving Runtime Team — Diego Ramos
- Quant profiles and verification: Inference Research — Harpreet Kaur
- Pager/contact for urgent regression: #ml-regressions (Slack) and oncall-applied-ml rotation

Definitions and key metrics

- Slice: a subset of prompts defined by label rules (regex, metadata, token patterns, language, prompt-template).
- Prompt rewrite: deterministic transformation applied to the user prompt before inference (e.g., explicit context headers, answer-format anchors, numeric formatting).
- Quant variant: model binary compiled to a specific quant profile (e.g., fp16, int8, int4).

Primary metrics collected per slice per variant:

- Slice Success Rate (SSR): percent of responses passing a slice-specific acceptance check (boolean or thresholded semantic similarity).
- Response Stability Index (RSI): normalized similarity between reference (gold) and response distribution across seeds (0-100).
- Per-token latency and tail-p99 latency (ms).
- Token-economic delta: tokens generated and kv-cache reuse percentage.
- Human-review CTR: for slices flagged, rate of escalation to human review.

Acceptance thresholds (example)

- SSR drop tolerated: <= 2% drop vs baseline for low-risk slices; <= 0.5% drop for high-safety slices (PII extraction, compliance prompts).
- RSI decrease tolerated: <= 5 points.

---

2) Eval harness integration: a job type that can run an eval across multiple model binaries and quant-profiles and emit per-slice metrics.

3) Canary traffic mirror: ability to run shadow runs at production sampling rates and attach telemetry to trace IDs.

High-level workflow (summary)

1) Slice sampling: generation of representative prompts for each slice from prod logs (time-windowed) with stratified sampling to maintain distributional weighting.
2) Baseline run: run chosen reference binary (usually fp16) to generate gold outputs and metric baselines.
3) Quant sweep: run each quant profile against the same prompt set; collect per-slice metrics and difference deltas.
4) Detection: automatic rules flag slices with metric regressions above acceptance thresholds.
5) Triage: triage path splits into (A) root cause: quantization artifacts vs prompt-sensitivity vs cache/latency-induced failure; (B) automatic mitigations: prompt rewrite heuristics, routing to higher-precision variant, cache TTL adjustments.
6) Canary release: if mitigation is accepted, create a canary route with mitigation enabled for a small % of production traffic and monitor RTT metrics before promotion.

Detailed step-by-step procedure

1) Build slice set
   - Run slice-extractor CLI: `rwd-slice-extract --window 7d --min-usage 100 --out slices/quarterly.yaml`
   - Ensure each slice includes at least 500 examples or mark as low-sample and schedule for synthetic augmentation.

2) Generate rewrites
   - For each flagged slice, produce candidate prompt rewrites. Rewrites follow these rules:
     a) Do not change user intent (strictly prefix/suffix or formatting fixes).
     b) Keep token overhead < 20 tokens or mark as acceptable if latency budget allows.
     c) Explicit annotations only when helpful (e.g., \"OutputFormat: JSON; Fields: name, price\").

   - Example rewrite ruleset (text):
     - numeric-table-extraction: prefix \"Task: extract table columns as CSV. Numeric fields keep 2 decimals.\"
     - code-synthesis: append \"Provide only code in a fenced block, include no explanations.\"

3) Run quant-aware A/B evals
   - Eval config YAML (example):

       name: quant-sweep-run-2026-02
       prompt_set: slices/quarterly.yaml
       seeds: [42, 123, 256]
       models:

4) Automated detection rules (examples)

5) Triage checklist (on flagged slice)
   - Verify reproducibility: run single-seed debug with full logs and KV-cache disabled to rule out cache-induced nondeterminism.

Dynamic Probe Priority Scoring and Synthesis Blueprint

Summary
-------
This blueprint defines a production-ready system for dynamically scoring and synthesizing evaluation probes ("probes") across the eval-harness. The goal is to prioritize limited human annotation and synthetic probe generation capacity toward probes that maximize signal for quality regressions, quantization fragility, latency-related failures, and customer-impacted slices.

Motivation
----------
- Probe budgets are constrained: annotation and compute cost mean we cannot exhaustively evaluate all slices continuously.
- Static prioritization leads to stale signals: workload drift, model updates, and quant changes shift the set of important probes.
- We need a unified, explainable scoring function that combines telemetry, model-change sensitivity, and business impact to 1) rank existing probes for evaluation and 2) seed new synthetic probes automatically where coverage gaps exist.

Scope
-----
This document covers:
- The priority scoring feature set and weight defaults.
- Algorithms for dynamic probe scoring.
- Synthetic-probe seeding heuristics and templates.
- Integration points: eval-harness scheduler, probe fabricator, and telemetry ingestion.
- Rollout plan, monitoring, and ownership.

Out of scope: human annotation UI and billing flows (see probe-curation-stewardship page).

Priority scoring design
----------------------
We represent each probe (existing or synthetic candidate) with a feature vector computed from telemetry and metadata. The final priority score is a weighted, normalized sum of feature contributions with a small stochastic exploration component (epsilon-greedy) to avoid blind spots.

Core features and default weights
(used to compute score = sum(weight_i * normalized(feature_i)))

| Feature name | Signal source | Purpose | Default weight |
|-------------|---------------|---------|----------------|
| Recent-Failure-Rate | eval telemetry (last 7d) | Prioritize probes with rising failure rates | 0.28 |
| Exposure | production shadow/sample rates | Ensure probe matches real traffic slices | 0.14 |
| Model-Change-Sensitivity | diff-of-eval-metrics pre/post model build | High sensitivity means likely regression | 0.20 |
| Quantization-Delta | replays across quant profiles | Detect probes that degrade under quant | 0.12 |
| Customer-Impact | tenant mapping / SLA score | Business-critical slices score higher | 0.10 |
| Latency-Tail-Exposure | p95/p99 per-slice | Latency sensitive prompts prioritized | 0.08 |
| Exploration-Bonus | random seed / novelty | Ensure coverage and avoid stagnation | 0.08 |

Normalization: each feature is normalized to [0,1] using clip-to-99.9th percentile and min=0 baselines computed over a sliding 30d window.

Telemetry ingestion and feature computation
------------------------------------------
- Inputs: eval results, production shadow traffic samples, per-tenant usage, quantized-replay outputs, model promotion diffs.
- Storage: feature aggregates stored in the eval-metrics-store as daily rollups (table: eval_probe_features).
- Freshness: features must be recomputed within 2 hours of new eval telemetry arrival for high-severity slices; otherwise stale flags are set.

Example SQL to compute Recent-Failure-Rate (simplified)
```
SELECT probe_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN

Example SQL to compute Recent-Failure-Rate (simplified)
```
SELECT probe_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'fail' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS recent_failure_rate
FROM eval_results
WHERE occurred_at >= now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY probe_id;
```

Scoring pseudocode
------------------
```
features = fetch_features(probe_id)
score = 0
for name, weight in WEIGHTS.items():
  score += weight * normalize(features[name])
# add small randomized exploration
score = (1 - EPSILON) * score + EPSILON * random_uniform(0, 0.2)
return score
```

Dynamic weight tuning
- Default weights above are starting points. We run weekly bayesian optimization using historical detection throughput (true positives for real regressions found) as objective, constrained to maintain interpretability (max single-weight <= 0.4).
- All weight changes require a canary run and sign-off by the evaluation-steering panel.

Synthetic probe synthesis (seeding)
----------------------------------
When the scorer indicates coverage gaps (low exposure but high model-change-sensitivity or quantization-delta), the fabricator will generate candidate synthetic probes. There are two families of synthesis: template-driven and mutation-driven.

Template-driven synthesis
- Use curated prompt templates per product domain (customer-support, code-assist, summarization). Templates include placeholder slots with type constraints (numeric, name, code-snippet).
- Fill slots from a synthetic-lexicon derived from production anonymized tokens and prohibited-list filtering.
- Example template: "User asks to summarize the following transcript: [TRANSCRIPT_SNIPPET]" with TRANSCRIPT_SNIPPET length sampled from heavy-tail distribution to stress context window.

Mutation-driven synthesis
- Take high-value probes and apply controlled mutations: token-level paraphrase, meaning-preserving swap, adversarial perturbations (typos, punctuation changes), and context truncation/extension.
- Each mutation has an associated risk score; only mutations with acceptably low semantic drift are used for production seeding.

Synthesis quality controls
- Semantic similarity gate: new synthetic probe must score >= 0.65 cosine similarity in embedding space to an anchor family when mutation-driven, to avoid generating irrelevant tests.
- Privacy gate: all placeholder substitutions must pass PII detection; any candidate flagged is dropped and logged.
- Diversity cap: limit synthetic probes per fingerprint cluster to 3 per week to avoid overfitting.

Scheduler integration and lanes
----------------------------
We integrate scoring outputs into the eval-harness scheduler which supports lanes: real-eval (human-annotated), synthetic-eval, and stress-eval. Lanes have capacity budgets and SLOs.

- Allocation rule: allocate top-K scored probes to lanes according to a configurable split (default: 40% real, 40% synthetic, 20% stress).
- Backpressure: if annotation backlog > 48h, reduce real-eval allocation by 50% and move budget to synthetic-eval.
- Preemption: high-priority probes (score > 0.85) preempt lower-priority scheduled runs in the next 2-hour window.

  "preemption_score_threshold": 0.85,
  "max_synth_per_cluster_per_week": 3
}
