Hybrid eval cost-fidelity splitter and routing framework

Summary:

This document defines the "Hybrid Eval Cost-Fidelity Splitter" (HECFS) — a deterministic policy and runtime component that routes evaluation probes across multiple fidelity tiers (smoke, standard, deep) to maximize coverage and failure signal while enforcing a configurable cost budget. HECFS provides (1) an allocation algorithm, (2) runtime routing knobs, (3) operational SLOs/metrics, and (4) a small runbook for triage when the splitter misbehaves.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers operating the eval harness and shadow fleets
- Platform engineers integrating probe routing into shadow and federated evaluators
- Product owners responsible for evaluation cost/perf tradeoffs

Why this exists:
- Continuous evaluation at scale has variable marginal value: not every probe needs full-fidelity instrumentation.
- Without systematic allocation, teams either overspend on deep evaluation or under-detect regressions.
- HECFS provides a principled way to amortize eval spend while preserving sensitivity to regressions.

Scope and definitions:
- Probe: a single evaluation input (prompt + metadata) executed by the harness.
- Fidelity tiers:
  - smoke: single seed, lightweight metrics, fast, lowest cost.
  - standard: deterministic seed set, additional metrics (coherence, hallucination proxies).
  - deep: multi-seed, function-call simulation, quant-shadow comparison, human review gating.
- Cost unit: normalized token-cost equivalent (used by the budget allocator).
- Sensitivity score: dynamic estimate of how likely a probe is to reveal a regression (0.0–1.0).

High-level design:
1) Offline profiling produces per-slice base-cost and baseline-variance. Profiling includes quant-shadow runs and prefix-cache sensitivity.
2) A lightweight estimator assigns each incoming probe a sensitivity score s and an expected token_cost c for each fidelity tier.
3) The Splitter uses a knapsack-inspired allocator to distribute probes into fidelity buckets given the global budget B and soft quality target Q (target detection probability).
4) A small rebalancer runs every minute to migrate probes (where possible) from standard -> deep or deep -> standard based on live telemetry (e.g., rising variance, new latency anomalies).
5) Routing decisions are recorded in the probe registry and emitted as telemetry (route_reason, expected_cost, chosen_tier, estimator_version).

Allocation policy (concise):
- Prioritize high-sensitivity probes for deep evaluation until marginal detection gain < marginal cost fraction.
- Maintain a minimum coverage floor: at least X% of probes in each important slice must be run at standard fidelity to preserve baseline comparability.
- Reserve a small opportunistic budget P for on-demand deep escalations triggered by anomaly detectors.

Configuration table (example):
| parameter | meaning | recommended default | notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| global_budget_B | total token-cost budget per-hour for eval fleet | 15_000_000 | set at account/team level |
| quality_target_Q | target detection probability (0-1) | 0.92 | soft target used by allocator |
| floor_coverage_slice | min percent of probes per

| 15_000_000 | set at account/team level |
| quality_target_Q | target detection probability (0-1) | 0.92 | soft target used by allocator |
| floor_coverage_slice | min percent of probes per slice at standard | 0.10 | important slices set by ownership |
| opportunistic_reserve_P | percent of B reserved for escalations | 0.06 | used for anomaly-driven deep runs |
| estimator_version | model id used to compute sensitivity | v2025-11-17 | pinned per-deployment |

Estimator notes:
- The estimator uses a small ensemble: a lightweight classifier over probe metadata + recent telemetry (token length, tenant, historical failure rate) and an uncertainty proxy (variance estimate from prior seeds).
- Estimator must be validated offline against prior incidents (see validation checklist below).

Pseudocode: allocation loop

# Inputs: probes[], B, Q, floor_coverage, P
# Outputs: routing decisions {probe_id -> tier}

1. sort probes by sensitivity_score descending
2. allocate_reserved = B * P
3. remaining_budget = B - allocate_reserved
4. ensure per-slice floor: for each slice s, mark floor_count(s) = max(floor_coverage * count(s), 1) and allocate those at standard tier, deducting expected cost
5. for probe in probes (high -> low sensitivity):
     expected_deep_cost = cost(probe, deep)
     marginal_gain = marginal_detection_gain(probe, deep vs standard)
     if remaining_budget >= expected_deep_cost and marginal_gain / expected_deep_cost >= threshold(Q):
         assign probe -> deep; remaining_budget -= expected_deep_cost
     else if remaining_budget >= cost(probe, standard):
         assign probe -> standard; remaining_budget -= cost(probe, standard)
     else:
         assign probe -> smoke
6. opportunistic pool: route up to allocate_reserved probes to deep when anomaly detectors flag them

Operational metrics (emitted every minute and available in Console dashboards):
- route_distribution: pct {smoke, standard, deep} (goal: stable within 5% of configured target)
- budget_utilization: used_B / B (alert at > 0.95)
- detection_gain_curve: marginal_detection_vs_cost (visualization to tune threshold)
- false_negative_rate_estimate (post-hoc labeling pipeline)
- escalations: count of opportunistic_reserve usages (alert if > configured P limit)
- estimator_drift_index: KL divergence of estimator feature distribution vs training baseline

SLOs and thresholds:
- Evaluator sensitivity SLO: maintain estimated detection probability >= Q - 0.03 (soft).
- Budget SLO: no more than 1% of hours with budget_utilization > 1.0 (hard).
- Escalation SLO: opportunistic_reserve usage limited to configured P within a 24h window.

Rollout plan (canary -> graduated):
1. Canary (5% of eval fleet across low-risk tenants): run HECFS in audit mode (make routing decisions but do not enforce; log "shadow_route" field) for 48-72 hours. Compare budget/utilization predictions and detection_gain_curve vs baseline.
2. Soft-enforce (25%): enforce routing, but keep a doubled opportunistic_reserve to allow manual escalations. Run human-in-loop reviews for any missed high-sensitivity probes.
3. Enforce (all): full policy, enable automated rebalancer.

Promotion checklist (must pass before increasing traffic fraction):
- estimator false positive/negative rates on canary labels <

human-in-loop reviews for any missed high-sensitivity probes.
3. Enforce (all): full policy, enable automated rebalancer.

Promotion checklist (must pass before increasing traffic fraction):
- estimator false positive/negative rates on canary labels < 10%
- budget_utilization predictions within 8% of observed
- detection_gain_curve monotonic (no counter-intuitive inversions)
- monitoring dashboards verified and alerting wired to oncall

Failure modes and runbook (top 5):
1) Overbudget (budget_utilization > 1.0)
   - Immediate action: toggle global_budget_B to emergency-reduced value (CLI: hecfs-cli set-budget --id <env> --value <reduced_B>) and scale opportunistic_reserve_P to 0
   - Triage: check estimator version, recent traffic spike, and any new slices with unexpectedly high deep_cost
   - Postmortem: corrective action may include increasing economy of standard tier or adjusting floor_coverage_slice

2) Estimator drift (estimator_drift_index > drift_threshold):
   - Action: revert to fallback_estimator (rule-based) and open ticket for retraining.

3) Detection regression (false_negative_rate_estimate increases > baseline + 0.05):
   - Action: pause deep -> standard demotions, temporarily promote top N high-sensitivity probes to deep for human review.

4) Router lag (routing decisions delayed > 2s):
   - Action: switch to stateless fallback routing (round-robin based on slice priority) and scale routing workers.

5) Telemetry loss: missing route_reason or chosen_tier fields
   - Action: pause enforcement, enable audit-only mode until telemetry pipeline repaired.

Validation and bench tests (recommended suites):
- Synthetic spike test: create a burst of high-sensitivity probes in a low-budget simulation and assert opportunistic_reserve limits are respected.
- Regression injection: replay a historic incident (known regression) and verify detection probability under HECFS >= baseline detection.
- Cost simulation sweep: run iterated allocators across B values to produce detection_vs_cost frontier for stakeholders.

Interfaces and example CLI commands:
- hecfs-cli evaluate-batch --input probes.json --budget 15000000 --estimator v2025-11-17 --output routing.csv
- hecfs-cli set-budget --env staging --value 10000000

Heterogeneous Workload Shadow Orchestration and Telemetry Spec

Overview

Purpose: This document defines a standardized orchestration and telemetry specification for running 'shadow' evaluations across heterogeneous customer workloads (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, multi-turn stateful flows) and across deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to produce actionable, production-realistic signal for model promotion, quantization impact, and regression triage while preserving privacy and minimizing production risk.

Scope: eval harness components, sampling strategies, fingerprinting and workload signatures, capacity-aware routing, telemetry schema, data retention, onboarding steps, and remediation/fast-fail playbook. This is intended for ML Engineers, SREs, and Product owners responsible for model promotion and quality guardrails.

High-level principles

- Non-disruptive: Shadow traffic must not add user-visible latency or affect customer SLOs.
- Representative: Sampling must preserve distributional properties of the target workload (intent mix, sequence length, token distribution).
- Traceable: Every shadow request is tagged with identifiers that tie back to deployment configuration, quant profile, and sampling provenance.
- Cost-aware: Orchestrator must throttle shadow replication under capacity pressure.
- Privacy-first: Use local PII filtering and differential-privacy sampling when required by customer configuration.

Architecture and components

1) Mirroring Proxy (mirrord)
- Deployed as an ingress-layer sidecar or region-edge service.
- Responsible for duplicating production requests to a shadow queue without affecting production response path.
- Tags traffic with: workload_fingerprint, sample_bucket_id, region, model_variant, quant_profile.

2) Shadow Sampler (sampler-service)
- Implements sampling policies (fixed-rate, stratified, capacity-aware, slot-based).
- Maintains per-workload counters and safety budgets.
- Supports on-the-fly rate adjustments via the Control Plane.

3) Replay Store (replay-blob / kafka topics)
- Short-term durable store for shadow payloads (30–90 days depending on retention policy).
- Indexes by fingerprint and sample_bucket.

4) Eval Runner (evald)
- Pulls from Replay Store, executes against target model variant(s) and quant profiles, produces evaluation artifacts.
- Runs both lightweight (latency/throughput) and fidelity evals (semantic-similarity, task-specific metrics).

5) Telemetry Collector (telemetry ingestion layer)
- Central schema-enforced collector that receives delta metrics, logs, and artifacts.
- Emits normalized events to observability pipeline and to the eval dashboard.

6) Audit & Triage UI (eval-console)
- Surface diffs between baseline and candidate variants, grouped by fingerprint slice and quant-profile.
- Provides explainability overlays and links to raw artifacts.

Workload fingerprinting (why and how)

- Fingerprinting objective: group similar requests so shadow sampling preserves within-slice distributions and we can prioritize critical slices.
- Fingerprint components: route_id, intent_hash (top-level classification of user intent), token_length_bucket, device_context (web/mobile/api), language, privacy_flag.
- Implementation: deterministic hash of normalized request headers + canonicalized prompt text (PII redacted).

Sampling strategies

1) Capacity-Aware Stratified Sampling (default)
- Stratify by fingerprint slice (intent + length bucket + language).
- Allocate sampling budget proportional to slice-contribution to production traffic, with minimum floor to ensure coverage of

Capacity-Aware Stratified Sampling (default)
- Stratify by fingerprint slice (intent + length bucket + language).
- Allocate sampling budget proportional to slice-contribution to production traffic, with minimum floor to ensure coverage of low-frequency critical slices.
- Backpressure: when GPU pools approach 85% utilization, reduce non-critical slice replication by multiplicative decrease.

2) Focused Safety Sampling
- For newly onboarded prompt sets or after model changes, temporarily boost sampling for slices tagged as safety-sensitive by product owners.

3) Weighted Reservoir for Long-Tail
- Maintain a small reservoir of long-tail examples sampled uniformly across customers; useful for regression discovery.

4) Differential Privacy-Constrained Sampling
- Optionally enabled per-customer: samples are drawn in a way that enforces local epsilon budgets; shadow artifacts are tagged and processed under private lanes.

Telemetry schema (key events and fields)

All telemetry events use the eval_event schema v2. Fields below are top-level strings or simple numeric values; evaluators must surface them in dashboards.

- event_type: "shadow_request" | "eval_result" | "model_diff" | "resource_pressure"
- timestamp: ISO8601 string
- request_id: unique id (matches production request)
- workload_fingerprint: string
- sample_bucket_id: string
- route_id: string
- model_variant: string (e.g. redwood-phi-3b-v2)
- quant_profile: string (e.g. q4_0_dynamic)
- deployment_mode: string (hosted|dedicated|private)
- latency_ms: integer (end-to-end execution on shadow path)
- tokens_consumed: integer
- similarity_score: float (-1..1) // semantic similarity to baseline output if applicable
- fidelity_delta: float // positive means candidate improved against baseline on chosen metric
- failure_code: string | null
- privacy_flag: true|false
- capacity_flag: OK | THROTTLED | DROPPED

(Example JSON event)
{
  "event_type": "eval_result",

Acceptance criteria and thresholds

Hybrid Probe Fabrication and Traceability Guide

Summary
---
This document defines a repeatable process for fabricating evaluation probes (synthetic examples), anchoring them to production traffic, and tracking provenance so that mixed synthetic/real evals (hybrid fusion) are auditable and actionable. It is intended for ML engineers, evaluation owners, and SREs running the eval-orchestrator and probe-farm services.

Motivation
---
Teams increasingly rely on hybrid evaluation runs that mix synthetic probes with shadowed production samples to stress-test models across quality and latency SLOs. Without a standard fabrication and provenance process, regressions are hard to triage, sample bias proliferates, and remediation is slower. This guide specifies design patterns, metadata, sampling rules, and triage playbook steps to address those gaps.

Scope
---
- Applies to: probe generation for text-only and multi-turn chat workloads evaluated by eval-orchestrator and shadow-sequencer.
- Not covered: human labeling details (see label-runbook), legal data-retention constraints (see security-and-compliance).

Key Principles
---
1. Anchoring-first: Every synthetic probe must have at least one anchor (production-derived exemplar) or a documented rationale for synthetic-only creation.
2. Deterministic provenance: Probes are immutable artifacts with stable IDs, creation metadata, and hash signatures.
3. Reproducible fusion: Hybrid runs must record fusion policy and the exact seed set used for sampling.
4. Minimally invasive: Probes should not alter production routing or customer-visible metrics.

Definitions
---
- Probe: A single evaluation input (prompt + context + optional metadata) used by the eval-harness.
- Anchor: A production-derived exemplar (anonymized) that a probe is designed to mimic or stress.
- Fusion policy: A declarative rule that defines how many probes vs. production samples are mixed, with weighting and prioritization.
- Provenance record: Machine-readable metadata that accompanies a probe through creation, storage, and evaluation.

Fabrication Procedure (step-by-step)
---
1) Identify target slices
   - Use telemetry-driven hotspot reports from probe-farm: top failing slices by semantic-stability and kv-cache-miss-rate.
   - Prioritize slices with high traffic and high business impact (example: chat-assistant/checkout).
2) Select anchors
   - Query shadow-logs for exemplars matching slice criteria (service: product-signal-collector).
   - Anonymize PII using scrub-tool v2.1; retain conversational structure and token positions.
3) Draft synthetic probe variants
   - Create at least three perturbation families: lexical swaps, priming (few-shot adjustments), and coherence breaks.
   - For prompt templates, parameterize slots and list expected valid continuations.
4) Run local micro-simulation
   - Use evaluator-adapter local runner with flag --seed=<stable-seed> and --kv-warmup=3. Confirm deterministic artifact hash.
5) Review and sign-off
   - Submit a probe bundle for review via the probe-review workflow (label: probe-eval-needed). Reviewer checklist: anchor match, privacy scrub, coverage matrix.
6) Publish to probe-farm
   - Upload via CLI: probectl publish --bundle <bundle.tgz> --provenance-json <meta.json>

Anchoring Strategy and Examples
---
- Soft anchor: probe captures distributional properties (length, role sequence, topic) but not lexically identical content.

Anchoring Strategy and Examples
---
- Soft anchor: probe captures distributional properties (length, role sequence, topic) but not lexically identical content.
- Hard anchor: probe is a close paraphrase of a production exemplar used to reproduce a specific failure mode.

Example: Hard-anchor mapping
- Anchor id: PROD-2025-08-17-9f1b
- Probe id: PROBE-HARD-2026-00042
- Rationale: Reproduces truncated completion observed for long-context checkout flow.

Provenance Metadata Schema (required fields)
---
All probe bundles must include a provenance file named provenance.json. Required fields: probe_id, created_by, created_at (UTC), anchor_ids (list), bundle_hash (SHA256), semantic_slice (string), privacy_level (one of 'anonymized' or 'synthetic-only'), fusion_compat (policy id), seed (string). Optional: notes.

Telemetry and Sampling Configurations
---
Attach a sampling manifest for hybrid runs. Example (yaml-like):

fusion_policy:
  name: 'balanced-weighted-1:3'
  description: '1 probe for every 3 shadowed production samples; prefer probes when slice-specific failures present'
  weights:
    probes: 0.25
    production_shadows: 0.75
  max_probe_replication: 4
  kv_warmup: 2
  latency_priority: true

Operational thresholds (used by eval-orchestrator):
- semantic-stability drop alert: greater than 3.0 percentage points relative to baseline
- 95th latency regression: greater than 20% relative increase or absolute > 250ms
- coherence-index (CI) drop: greater than 2.5 points

Runbook: Investigating a Hybrid Run Regression
---
1) Triage summary (owner: eval-oncall)
   - Fetch run snapshot: evalctl snapshot --run-id <id>
   - Evaluate top failing slices by semantic-stability and error-classification tags.
2) Confirm provenance
   - For each failing probe, open provenance.json and validate bundle_hash against artifact storage.
   - If probe is anchored: retrieve anchor exemplar via safe-anchor-retriever --id <anchor_id> and verify anonymization.
3) Reproduce locally
   - Re-run probe bundle with same seed and kv warmup to check determinism: evaluator-run --bundle <bundle> --seed <seed> --replay-mode deterministic
   - If non-deterministic, tag with 'non-deterministic' and escalate to runtime-team.
4) Quick mitigation (if quality regression impacts customers)
   - Roll back to previous model variant via rollout-service. Document rollback in incident ticket.
5) Deep analysis
   - Compare attention maps, token-level logprobs, and KV-cache hit profiles across failing probes and anchors using probe-analysis-tool --run <run-id> --diff anchors.

Failure modes specific to hybrid fusion
---
- Anchor leakage: synthetic probe accidentally contains customer-identifying tokens. Mitigation: automated scrub and manual reviewer confirmation.
- Overfitting to anchor templates: probes too similar to anchors produce false positives; require perturbation families >= 3.
- Sampling bias: fusion policy skew causes undercoverage of critical production traffic. Mitigation: periodic calibration against production holdout.

Promotion and Acceptance Criteria
---
A probe bundle or hybrid-run may be used for promotion when all of the following are met:
- At least 90% of artifact hashes reproduce deterministically in local replay.
- Semantic-stability baseline is within 1.5 percentage points of anchor baseline for the same slice.
- Privacy scan returns zero PII

At least 90% of artifact hashes reproduce deterministically in local replay.
- Semantic-stability baseline is within 1.5 percentage points of anchor baseline for the same slice.
- Privacy scan returns zero PII flags.
- Two reviewers have approved via probe-review workflow.

Eval Budget Ledger and Cost Attribution Framework

Summary
-------
This document defines the Eval Budget Ledger: a lightweight, canonical accounting model and operational framework for tracking, attributing, and governing the cost of evaluation work (shadow runs, probes, synthetic workloads, and human review) across the eval harness. It standardizes cost buckets, attribution rules, reporting artifacts, and a minimal runbook for triaging unexpected spend. The ledger enables reproducible cost rollups for feature teams, platform owners, and finance.

Goals
-----
- Provide a single source-of-truth CSV/JSON artifact (the ledger) for every eval campaign.
- Define deterministic attribution rules to map compute, human labeling, and storage costs to owning teams and probes.
- Enable near-real-time spend dashboards and budget alerts tied to probes, model variants, and environments (shadow/staging/prod).
- Reduce surprise spend from large synthetic sweeps and regression investigations; support pre-commit budget gating.

Definitions
-----------
- Probe: An atomic evaluation input or workload slice submitted to the eval harness.
- Campaign: A collection of probes executed as part of a single objective (e.g., shadow rollout of model-v2, quantization stress sweep).
- Ledger row: A single line in the canonical CSV representing cost attribution for one probe execution.

Ledger schema (CSV columns)
--------------------------
The ledger is produced by the eval orchestrator after each batch and stored in S3 and the eval index. Each ledger row is CSV with these columns (pipe-delimited in examples below for readability):

- ledger_id (string): UUID for the row.
- campaign_id (string): stable id for the campaign.
- probe_id (string): stable id for the probe.
- model_variant (string): e.g., redwood/gptx-8b-q4_latest.
- environment (string): shadow|staging|prod.
- start_ts (ISO8601): run start time.
- end_ts (ISO8601): run end time.
- compute_seconds (float): wall-clock GPU/CPU seconds consumed attributed to this probe.
- gpu_type (string): e.g., A100-80GB, L4x.
- memory_gb_seconds (float): memory usage * seconds (for cross-instance memory costs).
- tokens_in (int): input tokens.
- tokens_out (int): output tokens.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio (float): fraction for reuse-based discounts.
- human_label_seconds (float): paid human reviewer seconds attributable.
- storage_gb_months_fraction (float): short-lived artifact storage prorated to run.
- infra_cost_usd (float): computed infra cost allocated to row (see cost model).
- human_cost_usd (float): human labeling cost.
- total_cost_usd (float): infra_cost_usd + human_cost_usd + amortized tooling.
- owning_team (string): team slug owning the campaign (e.g., search-platform).
- billing_tag (string): optional billing tag for downstream finance mapping.
- notes (string): free text for special adjustments or credits.

Cost model and attribution rules
--------------------------------
1) Compute pricing table (example):

| resource | unit | nominal_price_usd | comment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| A100-80GB | per GPU-hour | 3.20 | spot pricing baseline for eval fleet |
| L4x | per GPU-hour | 1.10 | cheaper short-live experiments |
| vCPU | per vCPU-hour |

A100-80GB | per GPU-hour | 3.20 | spot pricing baseline for eval fleet |
| L4x | per GPU-hour | 1.10 | cheaper short-live experiments |
| vCPU | per vCPU-hour | 0.05 | for non-GPU workloads |
| RAM | per GB-hour | 0.002 | memory charge for long-running jobs |

2) Compute allocation: infra_cost_usd = sum(resource_seconds * price_per_unit_hour / 3600) adjusted by kv_cache discount. For probes that benefit from prefix/KV cache, apply a KV discount factor: cost *= (1 - kv_cache_hit_ratio * kv_cache_savings). Default kv_cache_savings = 0.45.

3) Human labeling: human_cost_usd = human_label_seconds * human_rate_usd_per_second. Default human_rate_usd_per_second = 0.004 (equivalent to $14.4/hour for contractor labeling).

4) Storage and tooling amortization: short-lived artifacts (replays, logs) are prorated and summed into storage_gb_months_fraction * storage_unit_price_usd. Tooling and infra overhead (e.g., eval queue, orchestrator overhead) is allocated to rows as a percent uplift (default 5%) and recorded in notes.

Ownership and governance rules
------------------------------
- Campaign owner (owning_team) is responsible for setting a campaign budget and tagging critical probes with high-priority flags.
- Platform (eval-harness) owns the compute_price table and publishing weekly baseline rates to the ledger generator.
- Finance owns final mapping of billing_tag to GL codes.

Operational artifacts and examples
--------------------------------
Example ledger row (CSV):
ledger_id|campaign_id|probe_id|model_variant|environment|start_ts|end_ts|compute_seconds|gpu_type|memory_gb_seconds|tokens_in|tokens_out|kv_cache_hit_ratio|human_label_seconds|storage_gb_months_fraction|infra_cost_usd|human_cost_usd|total_cost_usd|owning_team|billing_tag|notes
123e4567|camp-202602|probe-009|redwood/gptx-8b-q4|shadow|2026-02-10T14:02:03Z|2026-02-10T14:02:09Z|6.1|A100-80GB|49.6|152|420|0.38|0.0|0.00002|0.0054|0.0000|0.0054|search-platform|GL-APPL-011|kv-cache applied

Quick CLI to produce per-campaign rollup (example SQL using ledger table):
1) Per-campaign cost: SELECT campaign_id, SUM(total_cost_usd) AS campaign_cost_usd, COUNT(DISTINCT probe_id) AS probes FROM eval_ledger WHERE start_ts >= '2026-02-01' AND environment = 'shadow' GROUP BY campaign_id;
2) Team allocation: SELECT owning_team, SUM(total_cost_usd) FROM eval_ledger WHERE start_ts >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY owning_team;

Budget gating and alerting
-------------------------
- Preflight: campaign owners must declare a soft_budget_usd before launching non-trivial campaigns (> $5000 expected). The orchestrator rejects submission without a soft_budget or explicit approval for campaigns estimated > $25,000.
- Alerts: platform publishes per-campaign and per-team burn-rate metrics to Grafana. Alert thresholds: 50% of soft_budget (warning), 85% (action required), 100% (auto-pause candidate).
- Auto-pause policy: When a campaign crosses 100% and has no explicit approve_overage tag, orchestrator moves non-critical jobs to paused state and notifies owners via Slack and email. Critical jobs (marked critical=true) continue but generate P0 paged messages to the campaign owner.

Runbook: Investigating an unexpected spike
-----------------------------------------
1) Identify the campaign(s) with increased burn (Grafana or ledger query).
2) Drill into probe-level ledger rows for top-K cost contributors: SELECT probe_id, model_variant, sum(total_cost_usd) FROM eval_ledger WHERE campaign_id = 'camp-202602' GROUP BY probe_id ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 50;
3) Check model_variant token stats and kv_cache_hit_ratio: sudden token_out increases or cache_hit drops are common causes.
4) If compute_seconds look anomalous, check orchestration logs for retries or timeouts (orchestrator/job-runner). If human_cost spikes, check labeling batch sizes or misconfigured annotator pools.
5) If budget

cache_hit drops are common causes.
4) If compute_seconds look anomalous, check orchestration logs for retries or timeouts (orchestrator/job-runner). If human_cost spikes, check labeling batch sizes or misconfigured annotator pools.
5) If budget was exhausted and auto-pause triggered, owners should: a) mark urgent probes as critical if necessary; b) request funding via the campaign's Jira billing request; c) schedule a short review to adjust probe sampling.

Integration notes
-----------------
- The ledger writer is integrated into the eval-orchestrator post-processing stage (hook: /eval/orchestrator/postprocess->ledger-writer).
- A small shim (ledger-normalizer) converts raw runtime traces into the ledger schema and applies price tables fetched from SSM periodically.
- For Private deployments, the ledger generator accepts a custom pricing file and billing_tag mapping. Private deployments must opt-in to sending ledgers to Redwood; default retention is 90 days unless overridden by customer contract.

Rollout plan
------------
1) Q1 2026: pilot with three product teams (search-platform, chat-core, insights) using a nightly shadow campaign.
2) Q2 2026: add automated preflight enforcement and Grafana dashboards; finance mapping for billing_tag.
3) Q3 2026: enforce soft_budget for all campaigns over $2,000; export periodic reports to cost-center owners.

Metrics to monitor
------------------
- Daily eval spend (USD) - global and per-team.
- 7d rolling average cost per probe and cost per 1k tokens.
- Top-50 probes by cost (weekly).
- Fraction of campaigns with declared soft_budget.

Open questions and future work
-----------------------------
- Incorporate token-based QoS pricing (discounts for batched micro-inference).
- Experiment with dynamic kv_cache_savings per-model instead of a fixed default.
- Better human cost modeling for in-house vs vendor labelers.

Probe priming, hot-swap, and cost-aware scheduler playbook

Overview
========
This playbook describes a repeatable lifecycle for probe priming, live hot-swap of probe sets, and a cost-aware scheduler used to allocate evaluation budget across shadow and canary cohorts. It is intended for evaluation engineers, SREs who operate evaluator fleets, and model-onboarding teams coordinating quantization rollouts. The procedures balance fidelity, cost, and tenant isolation while enabling rapid response to regressions caused by quant or cache changes.

Why this exists
---------------
- Probe priming reduces noise when moving between model variants and quant levels by ensuring warm seeds and anchor examples are present before measuring drift.
- Hot-swap of probe sets enables fast replacement of flaky or high-cost probes without full evaluator redeploys.
- The scheduler enforces a cost budget and allocates probes across cohorts (shadow, canary, production-sampled) according to policy and SLO constraints.

Scope and non-goals
------------------
Scope:
- Shadow and canary evaluation within Redwood-hosted evaluator fleet and private evaluator sidecars.
- Interaction with quant shadow cohorts and KV-cache–sensitive workloads.

Non-goals:
- Full annotation workflows (use annotator playbooks).
- External third-party evaluator federation protocols (covered in evaluator-interchange-format docs).

Roles and ownership
-------------------
- Owner: Applied ML Evaluations team (primary contact: Marina Kwon).
- Fleet SRE: implements and operates the scheduler service (alerts, scaling).
- Onboarding PM: approves budget window, target cohorts.
- Incident runbook owner: Eng SRE on-call.

High-level workflow
-------------------
1. Define probe seed set and priming criteria in the Probe Manifest. Include anchor examples, per-probe cost estimate, and sensitivity metadata.
2. Reserve evaluation budget for the rollout window (daily token cap for shadow).
3. Run priming stage: synthetic warmups + anchor replay to populate KV caches and warm model weights.
4. Start soft canary with low traffic and scheduler-enforced budget.
5. If metrics pass thresholds, increase traffic; if not, hot-swap probes and/or rollback per rollback policy.

Probe Manifest schema (text table)
--------------------------------
| field | description | example | required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| probe_id | unique id for asset | anchor-en-us-001 | yes |
| category | semantic slice label | payment-instruction | yes |
| estimated_tokens | average tokens per probe | 42 | yes |
| cost_weight | relative cost multiplier for scheduler | 1.2 | yes |
| priming_hits | number of anchor replays recommended | 10 | no |
| sensitivity_tags | tags indicating quant/cache sensitivity | kv-cache-sensitive, low-temp | no |

Scheduler policy and rules
--------------------------
- Inputs: daily_token_budget, max_cost_per_probe, cohort_weights (shadow:canary:prod-sample), probe_priority_score (computed).
- Probe priority score = base_priority * sensitivity_multiplier / sqrt(estimated_tokens) where sensitivity_multiplier is 2.0 for kv-cache-sensitive probes.
- Scheduler enforces: total_estimated_daily_tokens <= daily_token_budget; never schedule > cohort_max_concurrency per tenant.

- Scheduler enforces: total_estimated_daily_tokens <= daily_token_budget; never schedule > cohort_max_concurrency per tenant.
- Backoff rule: if a probe causes > 3% spike in latency tail or > 2x token cost deviance, throttle that probe and mark for hot-swap.

Configuration examples
----------------------
YAML example for an evaluator job (annotated):

scheduler:
  daily_token_budget: 5_000_000
  cohort_weights:
    shadow: 0.5
    canary: 0.2
    prod_sample: 0.3
  max_cost_per_probe_usd: 0.12
  hot_swap_thresholds:
    latency_tail_p99_pct_increase: 3.0
    token_cost_variance_multiplier: 2.0

probe_manifest:
  - probe_id: anchor-en-us-001
    category: payment-instruction
    estimated_tokens: 42
    cost_weight: 1.2
    priming_hits: 8
    sensitivity_tags: [kv-cache-sensitive, functioncall]

Priming procedure (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1. Reserve a priming window of 30m to 2h depending on model cold-start characteristics.
2. Deploy priming runner: replay anchor probes with decreasing temperature and incremental context lengths.
3. Verify warmup metrics: KV hit-rate > 90%, model initialization latency < baseline * 1.1, no OOMs.
4. Snapshot primed state if running in private evaluator sidecars (artifact id).
5. Signal readiness to the scheduler to begin live canary.

Hot-swap procedure (fast replacement)
------------------------------------
1. Detection: scheduler flags probe as degraded (based on telemetry contract).
2. Quarantine: reduce probe sampling weight to 0 and move to quarantined bucket.
3. Replace: pick next candidate probe from replacement pool (match on category and tokens).
4. Priming: run quick priming mini-run (priming_hits=2) for the replacement.
5. Resume: restore normal sampling weight and monitor for stabilization window (default 60 minutes).
6. Postmortem: tag original probe with failure reason, cost delta, and owner for triage.

Telemetry contract (required signals)
-----------------------------------
- per-probe: probe_id, timestamp, probe_latency_p50/p90/p99_ms, tokens_consumed, model_version, quant_profile, kv_cache_hit_rate, cohort, tenant_id (if applicable), error_class.
- per-job: total_tokens_consumed, total_cost_usd_estimate, scheduled_probe_count, priming_status, scheduler_decisions (reason for skip/hot-swap).

SLOs and alert thresholds
-------------------------
- Scheduler correctness: 99.9% decisions executed within 5s of decision time.
- Priming success rate: target 95% of priming runs meet warm-up KPIs (kv hit-rate, latency).
- Hot-swap detection precision: > 90% of flagged probes correspond to measurable cost or quality regressions on follow-up.
- Alerts: page SRE on any priming run OOM or >5% error_rate during canary.

Cost accounting and attribution
------------------------------
- Per-probe cost = estimated_tokens * region_token_price * cost_weight.
- The scheduler writes daily ledger entries to the Eval Ledger service with tags: probe_id, model_version, quant_profile, tenant_id.
- Chargebacks: Owned teams are charged internal evaluation credits for shadow runs exceeding allocated budget windows.

-------------------------------

- [ ] Daily token budget approved by Finance for the rollout window.
- [ ] Scheduler policy set and dry-run simulated for 48h.
- [ ] Priming run passes warm-up KPIs.
- [ ] Canary run at 1% traffic for 6h

Rollback and mitigation ladders
------------------------------
Immediate rollback triggers:
1. Delta fidelity regression > threshold (slice-anchored metrics).
2. Token cost exceedance > 2x forecast for three consecutive intervals.
3. Sustained latency tail increase > 5% at p99 for 30 minutes.

Mitigation steps (fast path):

2. Hot-swap to alternative probe set or previous model artifact.
3. If caused by quant profile, fallback to higher-precision variant and notify model-onboarding.

Post-incident triage items to capture
-----------------------------------
- root cause hypothesis (code, quant, data, scheduling mistake)

Crossroad Eval Orchestration and Quant Compatibility Blueprint

Overview

Purpose: This blueprint defines a pragmatic, auditable contract between the evaluation harness, prompt/catalog stewardship, model onboarding, quantization handover, and regression triage systems. It codifies the runtime and offline checks required to promote a model variant across environments (shadow -> staged -> canary -> prod) when quantized artifacts or prompt transformations are involved. The goal is to reduce surprise regressions while preserving inference cost improvements.

Scope and audience
- Scope: eval orchestration, quant handoff, prompt-set preservation, shadow-synchronization, regression fast-paths, and on-call playbooks.
- Audience: Evaluator team, Model Onboarding, Runtime, SRE, and Product Engineering.

Key outcomes
- A single set of contracts that gates model promotion when quant artifacts exist.
- Deterministic shadow synchronization semantics to ensure probes and production traffic are comparable.
- A triage ladder for regressions attributable to quantization or prompt rewrites.

Definitions
- Probe: a single eval input used by the eval harness.
- Shadow environment: runtime that mirrors production traffic for evaluation without returning responses to users.
- Quant-handoff: automated process that creates quantized model artifact, associated metadata, and signature vectors.
- Integrity contract: a JSON manifest that travels with an artifact and enumerates checks, thresholds, and lineage.

Architecture (text diagram)
- evaluator-service -> probe-orchestrator -> shadow-fleet (mirror) -> quant-handoff-service -> artifact-registry -> promotion-guard -> canary-fleet -> prod-fleet

Roles & ownership
- Evaluator team: owns probe catalog, scheduling, and evaluator-service.
- Runtime team: maintains shadow-fleet and runtime telemetry collection.
- Model onboarding: owns the promotion-guard and promotion checklists.
- Quant engineering: owns quant-handoff-service and artifact-registry metadata schema.
- SRE / oncall: owns SLA monitoring and rollback automation.

Integrity contract schema (summary table)
| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| artifact_id | unique artifact UUID | art-20260803-1 |
| base_model | upstream model/version | hugface/linexa-v2.1 |
| quant_profile | quantization profile id | qprofile-int8-kv-safe |
| kv_cache_compat | boolean 'true' if KV caching validated | true |
| tokenization_fingerprint | sha256 of tokenizer files | ab12..9f |
| eval_seed_set | id of probe set used for artifact certification | probe-seed-42 |
| coherence_delta | max allowed coherence drop (0-1) | 0.03 |
| latency_p50_delta_ms | allowed p50 increase vs baseline | 10 |
| rollout_tier | allowed promotion path (shadow, canary) | shadow->canary |
| owner | team or person | model-onboarding-team |

Operational contracts and thresholds
- Quality gates (artifact must pass all):
  1) Coherence (semantic agreement) delta <= 0.04 on the certified probe set.
  2) Safety sentinels: zero high-severity sentinel failures in the last 24h for the probe set.
  3) Latency: p95 increase <= 25ms vs float baseline under representative traffic.
  4) Token cost: per-token cost delta must be <= -5% (i.e., quant should

the last 24h for the probe set.
  3) Latency: p95 increase <= 25ms vs float baseline under representative traffic.
  4) Token cost: per-token cost delta must be <= -5% (i.e., quant should reduce cost) or have a compensating business justification.
  5) Tokenization fingerprint must match onboarded tokenizer or be documented with translation mapping.

Shadow synchronization protocol (ensuring comparability)
1) Probe anchoring: Every probe executed in shadow includes a stable seed and a probe metadata header: {probe_id, probe_seed, probe_context_hash, traffic_cohort}.
2) Warmup parity: Shadow runtime executes a warmup sequence (identical priming tokens) for 3 preceding requests to stabilize KV effects.
3) Deterministic alignment: For models with nondeterministic sampling, the eval harness runs N=5 fixed-seed replicates and uses the median coherence score.
4) Telemetry alignment: Shadow telemetry must include the same routing, batching, and cache-hit labels as production for the evaluated request.

Prompt and Catalog preservation rules
- Prompt canonicalization: The prompt set associated with any promotion must be recorded using the canonicalized form and checksum. Changes to prompt wording require a labeled re-certification step.
- Prompt transformation mapping: If the runtime applies prompt truncation/compaction (e.g., context slicing), a documented mapping must be attached to the integrity contract.

Model onboarding checklist (promotion to canary)
1) Artifact integrity contract present and signed by quant-team.
2) Shadow run: 48h of shadow traffic with probes + 1% sampled production traffic mirrored.
3) Metric stability: coherence_delta <= 0.03 and deployment_sentiment score unchanged.
4) Canary plan: staging -> 5% canary traffic for 24h, with automatic rollback triggers.
5) Communication: announce to #eval-alerts and runbook-linked stakeholders 2 hours before canary start.

Rollback and regression triage ladder
- Automatic rollback triggers (applied by promotion-guard):
  - coherence drop > 0.06 on live-sampled probes in any 10-minute window.
  - safety sentinel trip (high severity) on a live probe.
  - production error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points and absolute error rate > 1.5%.
- Manual triage steps:
  1) Triage lead (oncall-evaluator) captures failing probe ids and artifact_id.
  2) Compare shadow vs prod telemetry using the alignment keys.
  3) Run focused replay: replay failing probes through float baseline + quant artifact with identical runtime labels.
  4) If regressions reproduce in replay -> escalate to quant engineering and model-owner.
  5) If regressions are absent in replay -> inspect routing, batching, and tokenizer differences; route to runtime team.
  6) Tag regression root-cause (quant|prompt|runtime|data-drift) and create an incident if severity meets thresholds.

Instrumentation and telemetry requirements (minimum)
- evaluator-service: probe_execution_time_ms, probe_seed, probe_context_hash, evaluator_version.
- shadow-fleet: p50/p95 latency, token_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size, sampling_seed_note.
- artifact-registry: artifact_id, quant_profile, fingerprint, certified_probe_set_id, certification_time.
- promotion-guard: last_promotion_run_id, checks_passed[], rollforward_deadline.

- Probe-run availability: 99.9% monthly.
- Shadow telemetry freshness: < 60s lag from production events.

Probe Resynthesis & Budget Simulator: operator manual

Summary:

This page describes the Probe Resynthesis & Budget Simulator (PRBS): an operational tool and set of procedures used by Applied ML to synthesize realistic probe sets from live telemetry, simulate evaluation budget allocation, and surface candidate probe-resynthesis strategies that minimize cost while preserving slice coverage and detection power. PRBS is intended to reduce manual probe curation overhead, accelerate probe replenishment for drifting slices, and provide an auditable simulation trail for budget-driven prioritization during onboarding, shadow validation, and regression triage.

Why PRBS exists:

- We observe expensive manual annotation cycles when longtail prompt slices drift or when quantization/timeout changes require fresh probes.
- Teams need to reason about trade-offs between probe volume, annotation cost, and detection latency for regressions.
- PRBS provides deterministic simulations using historical telemetry + a workload-cost model to recommend resynthesis policies.

Scope and applicability:

- Applies to: eval harness teams, model onboarding, regression triage, and the quality guardrails workflows.
- Not for: production inference routing, customer-facing A/B decisions, or one-off handwritten benchmarks.

High-level workflow (operator view):

1) Ingest: pull telemetry fingerprint snapshots from Eval-Mesh (daily/weekly cadence).
2) Fingerprint synth: cluster pockets of drift and generate seed anchors using the inkling heuristic (see config table).
3) Resynthesize: produce candidate probes for each slice using the selected synthesis policy (seeded paraphrase, adversarial-noise, or hybrid).
4) Simulate: feed synthesized probes into the cost simulator with target annotation rates, expected annotator agreement, and quantization noise models.
5) Score & prioritize: output ranked actions (resynthesize X, retire Y, escalate Z), with estimated cost, expected recall improvement, and detection latency.
6) Promote: selected probe batches are committed to the probe registry and scheduled for annotation.

Key concepts and definitions:

- Probe: an input-record (prompt + metadata) used by eval harnesses to exercise model slices.
- Slice: a semantically grouped set of probes (e.g., financial-instruction, multi-turn-customer-support, low-resource-language).
- Resynthesis policy: algorithmic rule used to generate new probes from seeds (paraphrase, noise-perturbation, translation-backtranslate).
- Budget simulation: deterministic calculation of annotation cost and expected detection performance given probe set composition.

Operational SLOs and thresholds:

- Probe coverage SLO: 95% of active high-priority slices must have >= N_min probes (N_min depends on slice criticality; see table).
- Detection latency SLO: median time to detect a 5% fidelity regression for high-priority slices <= 72 hours under normal resynthesis cadence.
- Budget adherence: recommended resynthesis plan must remain within the monthly eval budget +/- 10% unless approved by Eval PMO.

Parameter table (common configs):

| parameter_name | default | notes |
|---|---:|---|
| resynthesis_window_days | "14" | window of telemetry used to seed resynthesis |
| seed_per_slice | "10" | number of seed anchors sampled per slice |
| target_annot_per_probe | "1" | number of annotations per probe for majority-label tasks |
| annotator_unit_cost_usd | "0.75" | default annotator cost used in sim |
| critical_slice_threshold | "0.05" | fraction of

slice |
| target_annot_per_probe | "1" | number of annotations per probe for majority-label tasks |
| annotator_unit_cost_usd | "0.75" | default annotator cost used in sim |
| critical_slice_threshold | "0.05" | fraction of traffic to mark slice as critical |
| quant_noise_factor | "0.03" | conservative estimate for token-level degradation under int8 quant |

(Use these values as starting points; teams may override at the slice-level in the PRBS config.)

Command-line quickstart:

1) Fetch telemetry snapshot:
$ prbs fetch --snapshot-date 2026-02-01 --out snapshots/2026-02-01.json\n2) Run resynthesis simulation with hybrid policy:
$ prbs simulate --snapshot snapshots/2026-02-01.json --policy hybrid --budget 5000 --out sims/hybrid-2026-02-01.json
3) Review top recommendations:
$ prbs summarize --sim sims/hybrid-2026-02-01.json --top 20

The tool emits a CSV with recommended probe actions and an audit JSON for reproducibility (store audit files in s3://redwood-evals/prbs-audit/).

Example policy YAML (annotated):

policy_name: hybrid-resyn-1
resynthesis_window_days: 14
seed_selection:
  method: stratified
  per_slice: 10
synthesis_generators:
  - paraphrase
  - adversarial-noise: {max_perturb: 0.12}
  - backtranslate: {langs: ["fr","es"]}
scoring:
  cost_weights: {annotation: 0.6, detection_power: 0.3, freshness: 0.1}

(Operators copy this YAML into the PRBS policy registry when creating new strategies.)

Integration points and telemetry signals:

- Eval-Mesh snapshot: primary source for per-slice telemetry (latency, tokens, error-rates, fidelity).
- Registry: probe-registry (write access for promotion).
- Annotator pipeline: annotation-queue service (submit batches).
- Evals billing: cost-accounting ledger to reconcile simulated vs actual spend.
- Regression triage: output recommendations create work items in the Regression Board with links to probe batches.

Scoring heuristics (how candidate batches are ranked):

- Detection power estimate: measured as expected lift in slice-level signal-to-noise given additional probes; computed via bootstrap on historical slice variance.
- Cost estimate: annotator_unit_cost_usd * probes * target_annot_per_probe + labeling overhead (10%).
- Freshness score: inverse of median age (days) of probes in slice.

Decisioning matrix (example):

1) If cost per expected-detection > $1200 and slice traffic < critical_slice_threshold => defer resynthesis.
2) If detection latency expected > 72h and slice is critical => escalate to Eval leads and request emergency annotation credit.
3) If quant_noise_factor > 0.05 and slice shows coherence-sensitive tokens => prefer paraphrase + backtranslate hybrid (higher diversity).

Procedure: from simulation to production promotion (numbered steps for operators):

1. Run prbs simulate with the latest snapshot.
2. Review sims/*/summary.csv and open the top-N predicted actions.
3. Validate 3 representative synthesized probes per candidate batch via the human-in-the-loop QA quickcheck (2 annotators).
4. Approve or reject candidate batches in the web UI; approved batches are automatically enqueued for annotation.
5. After annotation, wait for the annotation-completion webhook and run prbs reconcile --batch <id> to update the registry and cost ledger.
6. If the annotated batch triggers a regression detection improvement < expected, file a follow-up triage with the regression-triage template.

Onboarding checklist (model/service teams):

- [ ] Register slice taxonomy with Eval-Mesh and link to PRBS slice IDs.
- [ ] Provide criticality tiers for slices (low/medium/high).
- [ ] Set monthly eval budget and escalation contacts.
- [ ] Run a baseline PRBS sim and

Eval-Mesh and link to PRBS slice IDs.
- [ ] Provide criticality tiers for slices (low/medium/high).
- [ ] Set monthly eval budget and escalation contacts.
- [ ] Run a baseline PRBS sim and review recommendations with Applied ML lead.

Failure modes and mitigations:

- Mode: Synthesized probes are syntactically valid but semantically irrelevant -> Mitigation: tighten seed-selection (higher similarity threshold) and increase human QA sample size to 5 per batch.
- Mode: Simulator underestimates annotation latency -> Mitigation: add per-region latency slack and tie annotation SLA to live queue metrics.
- Mode: Excessive churn in probe registry -> Mitigation: apply retire-after policy for probes older than 540 days and introduce probe-stability gating.

Auditability and reproducibility:

- Every simulation run produces an audit bundle: {snapshot-id, policy-id, seed-rng-seed, scoring-hash}. Store audit bundles in S3 and attach to regression board tickets.
- Use prbs replay --audit <id> to reproduce the exact candidate set.

Quality guardrail interactions (short):

- PRBS must be run against the same eval contracts used by quality-guardrails (fidelity thresholds, sentinel tests). Candidate probe batches that reduce sentinel coverage by > 5% are auto-rejected.
- If quantization profiles are in play, PRBS will simulate quant_noise_factor effects and surface batches with high sensitivity for manual review.

Observability and dashboards to monitor (owners):

- PRBS-run-rate (ops) - how frequently sims run per week.
- Probe-recommendation-accept-rate (product) - percent of recommended batches approved.
- Sim-vs-actual-cost-delta (finance) - monthly reconciliation metric.
- Slice-detection-latency (SRE) - median detection time for top-50 slices.

Ownership and escalation contacts:

- Tool owner: Applied ML - Eval Orchestration (team alias: #applied-ml-eval).
- Primary oncall for PRBS failures: eval-harness oncall (see oncall rota).
- Budget escalation: Eval PMO (eval-budget@redwood.ai).

Appendix: quick triage checklist for regression incidents related to probe gaps:

1) Confirm whether the failing slice has recent PRBS recommendations (search audit bundles).
2) If yes, check whether recommendations were approved/enqueued for annotation and whether annotation completed.
3) If annotation incomplete and slice is critical, escalate for emergency annotation credit and run an interim limited-synthesis with max_perturb=0.05.
4) If annotation complete but detection power did not improve, open a root-cause with hypothesis: (a) seed selection bias, (b) insufficient diversity, (c) quantization collapse.

- Regression triage quickstart: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026

functioncall-eval-contracts-and-onboarding-checklist-2026

Summary:
This guide defines a standard evaluation contract and an onboarding checklist for models that use function/tool-calling interfaces (a.k.a. functioncall or toolcall). It covers: what to measure, how to construct prompt and probe sets, quantization considerations, quality gate thresholds, and a regression triage fast-path for function-calling failure modes. Use this doc to certify a model (hosted, dedicated, or private) for production traffic that exercises the tool-calling surface.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: applied ML engineers, model infra owners, SREs, platform QA, and product engineers integrating tools.
- Scope: text-only and multimodal models that expose structured function output or tool invocation APIs. Not for purely embedding-only endpoints.

Why this matters:
Function-calling expands app capabilities but creates deterministic integration contracts (JSON schema, sequence-of-calls semantics, and failure/retry behaviors). Failures manifest as malformed JSON, wrong tool selection, missing params, or silent no-op calls — which have higher user-impact than standard free-text regressions. We need a reproducible, automated way to validate these behaviors across model variants, quantized artifacts, and rollout channels.

Evaluation contract (machine-readable):
Every model onboarding request must supply an eval contract json that declares the following fields. This schema is the minimum expected artifact attached to a model card.

Example eval_contract.json:
```
{
  "model_id": "redwood-llamax-13b-v3",
  "interface": "functioncalling-v1",
  "schemas": [
    {"name": "search_file", "json_schema": "{\\\"type\\\":\\\"object\\\",...}", "required_samples": 200},
    {"name": "summarize_page", "json_schema": "{\\\"type\\\":\\\"object\\\",...}", "required_samples": 150}
  ],
  "quant_profiles_tested": ["fp16","int8-ggml"],
  "primary_prompt_set": "/datasets/functioncall/checkout-2026-v1",
  "slo_targets": {"parse_rate": 0.995, "correct_tool_selection": 0.98, "latency_ms_p95": 800}
}
```

Key contract fields (human-readable):
- model_id: canonical model reference used in runtime routing.
- interface: cataloged interface type (functioncalling-v1, functioncalling-v2, toolchain-v1).
- schemas: list of named function/tool schemas with their canonical JSON Schema and minimum sample count for evaluation.
- quant_profiles_tested: quantization artifacts that must be validated (list).
- primary_prompt_set: pointer to the canonical probe/prompt dataset.
- slo_targets: minimal quality/latency thresholds to pass the gate.

Prompt & probe design principles:
1) Intent diversity: For each declared schema, include probes that exercise intent synonyms, misspellings, nested requests, and numeric edge cases.
2) Structural fuzzing: Include syntactic noise that commonly breaks parsers: mismatched punctuation, truncated sentences, and nested JSON in text blocks.
3) Multi-step sequences: For function chains (tool A -> tool B), model must demonstrate correct ordering under simulated session state.
4) Latency-sensitive probes: Tiny-context and long-context variants — measure p50/p95/p99 for both token-generation and post-processing (parse time).
5) Quantization sensitivity: For each probe, run on floating-point baseline and at least two quantized variants to capture divergent behavior.

Sample prompt matrix (short table represented as text):
- schema: search_file | probes: 200 | categories: exact-match, fuzzy-query, truncated-path, escaped-characters
- schema: summarize_page | probes: 150 | categories: long-context, single-sentence, list-based, nested-bullets

Automated checks (must pass to promote to canary):
- Parse success rate (parse_rate): fraction of probes

exact-match, fuzzy-query, truncated-path, escaped-characters
- schema: summarize_page | probes: 150 | categories: long-context, single-sentence, list-based, nested-bullets

Automated checks (must pass to promote to canary):
- Parse success rate (parse_rate): fraction of probes returning syntactically valid JSON matching schema. Target >= slo_targets.parse_rate.
- Tool selection accuracy (correct_tool_selection): fraction of probes that select the expected function/tool. Target >= slo_targets.correct_tool_selection.
- Semantic correctness (semantic_score): automated heuristics + small human annotation sample. Thresholds depend on product (default >= 0.85 for conversational tool workflows).
- Latency SLOs: token-generate + parse <= slo_targets.latency_ms_p95.
- Determinism budget: For deterministic routes, p95 token divergence <= 1.2x baseline variance.

Quality guardrails and blocking failures:
- Blocker: Returning top-level free-text when schema required (e.g., response is plain text instead of JSON) — immediate rollback for canaries.
- Blocker: Incorrect tool invoked when expected tool has security implications (delete/write operations).
- High-severity: Missing required keys in returned JSON across >2% of probes.
- Medium-severity: Parsable but semantically incorrect params (e.g., wrong file id).

Quantization & artifact considerations:
- All quantized artifacts used in production must be part of the eval_contract.quant_profiles_tested list.
- Run the quantized-replay orchestrator (see /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/quantized-artifact-eval-gate-and-rollout-2026) with the same seed and prompt ordering to detect brittle tokenization-induced parse fractures.

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1) Prepare artifacts: model binary, tokenizer config, eval_contract.json, primary_prompt_set (as JSONL), and a human annotation plan.
2) Local smoke: run 100 probe smoke harness with both baseline and quantized artifacts.

Latency-Quality Slice Optimizer Playbook

Overview

Purpose
- Provide a repeatable, slice-driven evaluation and promotion workflow that balances latency SLOs and output quality when deploying quantized or heterogeneous model variants.
- Reduce regressions by combining targeted slice benchmarking, telemetry contracts, and automated gating.

Scope and audience
- Applies to model onboarding, private and dedicated deployments, and hosted canary rollouts.
- Intended for ML engineers, serving runtime owners, SREs, and product owners.

Definitions
- slice: a named subset of production traffic grouped by intent, length, or feature flags.
- latency SLO: 95th percentile server-side model generation latency budget for a route.
- quality delta: measured expected change in task-specific metric vs baseline model.

Key SLOs and thresholds
- Global production latency SLO: p95 <= 180 ms for interactive text routes.
- Quantized candidate guardrail: quality delta <= 2.5% relative drop on primary slice metric OR absolute metric delta defined per slice.
- Regression alarm: any slice with quality drop > 5% or p95 latency increase > 30% triggers immediate rollback.

Slice catalog (example)
- onboarding-guidance: short instruction following prompts, expected median tokens 12. Primary metric: accuracy@top1.
- long-context-support: multi-turn doc summarization, median tokens 1200. Primary metric: coherence score.
- embeddings-search-q: short queries for vector similarity, median tokens 8. Primary metric: embedding cosine stability.
- api-batch-worker: high-throughput noninteractive batch calls. Primary metric: throughput and tail latency.

Telemetry and signals required
1) Per-slice quality metrics (task metric, confidence distribution, top-k disagreement).
2) Per-slice latency histogram and p50/p95/p99.
3) Token economy: generation tokens and input tokens per request.
4) Feature tags: model variant id, quant profile id, hardware type, route id.
5) Drift indicators: prompt fingerprint rate change, anchor-response divergence.

Evaluation harness configuration examples
- When adding a new candidate, create a harness job with the following attributes:
  - deterministic seed sets for 3 replicate runs
  - slice weightings matching production traffic fractions or importance weights
  - synthetic amplification for rare slices until N=500 example coverage

YAML snippet for an eval job (illustrative)
```
job_name: latency_quality_slice_eval
model_variant: candidate-v2
replicates: 3
slices:
  - name: onboarding-guidance
    weight: 0.35
  - name: long-context-support
    weight: 0.25
  - name: embeddings-search-q
    weight: 0.25
  - name: api-batch-worker
    weight: 0.15
metrics:
  - name: primary_task_metric
    compare: relative
  - name: p95_latency_ms
    compare: absolute
augmentation:
  rare_slice_min_examples: 500
```

Promotion gating and automated policy (high level)
1. Run harness with baseline model and candidate concurrently. Produce per-slice report with confidence intervals and p95 latency.
2. Apply gate rules in order: safety checks -> latency gates -> quality gates -> cost appreciations.
3. If all gates pass, schedule canary rollout with 5% traffic for 4 hours and expanded telemetry retention.
4. If any gate fails, run targeted regression triage (see Runbook) and block promotion until triage resolves

gates pass, schedule canary rollout with 5% traffic for 4 hours and expanded telemetry retention.
4. If any gate fails, run targeted regression triage (see Runbook) and block promotion until triage resolves causes and a new candidate is evaluated.

Gate examples
- Safety checks: zero high-severity safety sentinel hits across 3 replicates.
- Latency gate: p95(candidate) <= max( p95(baseline) * 1.15, absolute_slo )
- Quality gate: per-slice primary_task_metric delta >= -2.5% for critical slices, >= -5% for noncritical slices.

Regression triage runbook (summary)
1. Triage kickoff: create incident in tracker, tag model id and quant profile. Notify owner_team and oncall.
2. Reproduce: run harness with failing slice example set and deterministic seed. Capture full token-level diffs and KV-cache traces.
3. Isolate: compare candidate vs baseline on short micro-benchmarks: 1) tokenizer alignment, 2) decoding detokenized mismatch, 3) top-k logit shifts.
4. Test hardware sensitivity: replay eval on alternate device types and with and without kernel fallback.
5. If quantization suspected: run full-precision shadow and mixed-precision variants to narrow failure mode.
6. Repair options: prompt rewrite, quant profile relax, small fine-tune, or rollback. Document chosen remediation path and validation evidence.

Runbook snippets and CLI examples
- Trigger a slice evaluation run: rci eval run --job latency_quality_slice_eval --model candidate-v2 --slices onboarding-guidance,long-context-support
- Fetch per-slice report: rci eval report --job-id 0xabc123 --format table
- Promote to canary: rci rollout create --model candidate-v2 --percent 5 --duration 4h --observability retention=72h

Operational best practices
- Keep slice definitions small and orthogonal: prefer intent-based slices over ad hoc query buckets.
- Maintain a slice ownership map and ensure one owner per slice.
- Refresh rare-slice seed sets monthly or when production distribution changes > 10%.
- Archive long-context examples with token boundaries and session context to enable deterministic replay.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary oncall: eval-platform-sre rotation.
- Escalation: after 30 minutes unresolved, escalate to runtime-performance team lead and product owner.

Telemetry-driven Eval Prioritization and Hotspot Triage

Summary
This document describes a telemetry-first system for prioritizing offline and online evaluation jobs and a structured hotspot triage playbook for high-impact model behavior regressions. It targets the evaluator orchestration layer and SRE/Applied-ML engineers who run and act on model quality telemetry for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Motivation
- The eval backlog grows faster than evaluation capacity. Manual triage leads to missed regressions and wasted compute on low-impact slices.
- Telemetry (production errors, user rejections, SLA anomalies) is an early indicator of quality regressions but needs automated translation into eval work.
- We need a deterministic, auditable prioritization pipeline that: (1) converts telemetry to eval tasks, (2) assigns cost-aware priority, and (3) feeds actionable triage runbooks to on-call and ML engineers.

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  - Surface the top-K evaluation tasks that reduce user-impact most per compute dollar.
  - Ensure high-recall capture of hotspots without overwhelming evaluators.
  - Provide an operator-facing triage checklist with concrete rollback/fallback actions.
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a model promotion gate (that remains the model-onboarding pipeline).
  - It does not supersede security or privacy reviews for customer data.

Principles
1) Signal-first: prioritize signals with clear business impact (error rates, retention drops, user-text flags).
2) Cost-awareness: include token/throughput cost estimates in prioritization.
3) Explainability: each prioritized eval job must include the telemetry-derived rationale and suggested slices.
4) Fast feedback: support micro-canaries and quick smoke evals (<30m) before full-scale runs.

Telemetry signals (inputs)
- Production traces: streaming error labels (500-series), latency p99/p50 spikes, timeouts.
- User feedback: explicit thumbs-down, A/B experiment metrics (CTR/retention deltas).
- Quality analytics: semantic drift detectors, embedding-distance anomalies, stability score drops.
- Routing & capacity: fallback events (requests routed to cheaper model variants).

Signal enrichment steps
1) Attach context: request metadata (model version, route, top-k prompts), tenant_id, and sequence length buckets.
2) Cluster related events: temporal proximity (5–15m windows), similar prompt fingerprints (edit distance or embedding cosine > 0.92).
3) Score impact: compute an impact score (0–100) combining user count, error severity, and retention delta.

Priority scoring algorithm (overview)
- Inputs: impact_score, estimated_eval_cost (core-hours or token-cost), urgency_multiplier (customer SLA tier), seasonality_factor.
- Priority = (impact_score * urgency_multiplier * seasonality_factor) / (1 + log(1 + estimated_eval_cost))
- Normalization: scale to 0–100 and bucket into: critical (>80), high (60–80), medium (30–60), low (<30).

Eval task generation
1) Auto-slice suggestion: generate 3–7 candidate slices using clustering (intent, length, locale, prompt-token prefix).
2) Quick smoke: spawn a 30m micro-eval on a 500–2k sample (approx 5–20k tokens) to confirm signal.
3) Full evaluation: if smoke fails, schedule full eval with stratified sampling across traffic segments.

Hotspot triage playbook (operator steps)
1) Acknowledge: Owner (on-call ML or SRE) acknowledges the prioritized task in the evaluation dashboard within 30 minutes for critical tasks.
2) Run smoke eval: launch the micro-sample smoke eval. If pass -> mark as false-positive and document reasoning.
3) If smoke fails: run a targeted full eval job and fetch comparison baselines (previous model version and quantized variant).
4) Determine root cause categories (choose one primary):
   - Model drift / distribution shift
   - Quantization-induced degradation
   - Serving KV-cache/latency artifact
   - Prompt-processing bug (pre/post-processing mismatch)
   - Data corruption / formatting errors
5) For each root cause, follow the remediation checklist below.

Remediation checklists (short)
- Model drift:
  - Compare top-k token distributions and embedding centroids versus baseline.
  - Re-run eval with increased context/contextual shots.
  - If confirmed, create model-promotion hold ticket; notify product and release manager.
- Quantization-induced degradation:
  - Re-run on full-precision replica and mixed-precision replicas.
  - If degradation isolated to q4/q8 profile, revert to higher-fidelity profile for affected routes and open quant-team ticket.
- KV-cache / latency artifact:
  - Check per-token latency, cache hit rates, and request-shard mapping.
  - Warm caches for affected routes and schedule a controlled roll-forward.
- Prompt-processing bug:
  - Replay raw request through offline preprocessing; compare outputs.
  - Patch preprocessor and deploy a canary.
- Data corruption:
  - Validate ingestion pipelines and normalization; block bad batches and backfill missing fields.

Escalation and rollback policy
- Critical priority: if a full eval shows regression (>5% degradations on primary metric for top-tier customers), perform an emergency rollback to the last certified model and notify Incident Response.
- High priority: consider partial route-level fallback to a previous variant; schedule a postmortem if rollback is performed.

Probe Activation Matrix and Quant-Fallback Runbook

Overview

Purpose: This document defines the Probe Activation Matrix (PAM) — a deterministic policy that decides when to run targeted eval probes across hosted/dedicated/private fleets — and the accompanying Quant-Fallback Runbook used when quantization variants cause measurable quality regressions. PAM is intended to reduce eval noise, prioritize probes for customer-impacting SLOs, and automate safe fallback actions for quant migration.

Scope: applied-ml probes, runtime telemetry signals (latency, tail-pct, error-rate), quality signals from eval harness (delta-coherence, anchor-score), and quant variant rollout orchestrations. Does not replace the model-onboarding certification matrix but integrates with it via the "promotion hooks" section.

Owners and stakeholders

- Primary owner: Applied ML (probe-fabrication)
- Secondary owners: Serving Runtime (quant rollouts), Eng SRE (alerting & capacity), Product (SLO definition)
- Escalation contact: oncall-applied-ml -> oncall-eng-sre -> oncall-platform

Definitions and signals

- Probe: A synthetic, annotated input (usually from the probe registry) executed through the full serving stack and evaluated by the eval harness.
- Activation signal (examples):
  - SLO breach: production 99th latency > configured SLO by 20% for 5m.
  - Quality drift: rolling anchor-score delta > 0.08 vs baseline over 1h.
  - Quant anomaly: increase in token-level entropy variance combined with increased coherent-failure count.
- Probe priority classes: P0 (customer-visible SLA), P1 (high-risk slices), P2 (background/coverage), P3 (low-priority longtail)

Probe Activation Matrix (PAM) design

Goal: map runtime and quality signals to a minimal set of probes to run, with rules for escalation, sampling, and scheduled replays. PAM emits an activation manifest consumed by the eval-orchestrator.

Activation rules (summary):
1) Immediate activation (P0):
   - Trigger when any of: 99th latency > SLO*1.2 for 2 consecutive windows (5m each), or live anchor-score delta > 0.08 and user-impact flag true.
   - Probes: top 25 production-sampled probes for affected route + 5 targeted canary probes from the anchor family.
   - Run mode: high-fidelity (deterministic seeds, n=50 runs, mixed-quant variants enabled).

2) Priority activation (P1):
   - Trigger when: 95th latency increases > 15% or comp-similarity drift on an important slice is detected.
   - Probes: top 100 representative probes for slice, 10 targeted adversarial probes.
   - Run mode: fidelity medium (n=20, seeded), include quant baseline and current variant.

3) Scheduled regression scan (P2):
   - Trigger: daily background schedule or after model promotion from shadow -> canary.
   - Probes: stratified sample across tenant cohorts (n=500 total).
   - Run mode: low-fidelity (single run, mixed seeds).

4) Longtail harvest (P3):
   - Trigger: triggered by periodic annotation jobs or when storage backlog > 24h.
   - Probes: rare-slice catalog entries.
