Model Promotion: Canary, Chaos and Load Validation Protocol

This document defines the canonical protocol for promoting a candidate model from staging to production in Redwood inference environments. The protocol combines canary traffic validation, targeted chaos experiments, and load-scaling verification to ensure models meet functional, performance, cost, and robustness requirements before full promotion.
Provide a repeatable, auditable process that reduces risk when rolling out new model versions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Ensure compatibility with quantized artifacts, KV-cache behavior, and downstream prompt sets and metrics used by product features.
Applies to all model promotions handled by the Model Onboarding and Serving teams: text generation and chat models, embedding variants, and quantized model builds. Does NOT replace safety evaluations or legal/compliance checks (those must be completed separately).
Candidate model: the specific model artifact/weight bundle being promoted. Canary cohort: a small percentage of production traffic routed to the candidate. Chaos test: deliberate fault injection into dependencies or resources (network latency, GPU eviction simulation). Metrics baseline: historical SLI windows against which the candidate is compared.
- Production baseline dataset and key prompt sets prepared (see 'related_pages')
- Candidate model registered in model-catalog with version tag and quantization profile attached
- Monitoring hooks instrumented: latency, p95/p99, error-rate, token-cost, quality scores (BLEU/ROUGE/CLARITY where applicable)
- Rollout policy defined in Redwood Console (traffic split, automatic fallback thresholds)
- Stakeholder approval (owners and reviewers listed in this doc)
High-level phases: 1) Staging validation and synthetic stress, 2) Canary traffic validation (functional & quality), 3) Chaos experiments (dependence and degradation), 4) Load scaling validation (autoscale/steady-state), 5) Full promotion or rollback. Each phase has pass/fail criteria and required artifacts recorded in the promotion ticket.
1) Staging smoke: run the eval-harness smoke suite against the candidate (sanity prompts, adversarial prompt subset, and quantization integrity tests). Record the run id.

2) Canary setup: define a canary cohort (default 1% traffic) and snapshot baseline SLI window (previous 7 days). Configure canary to route to both original and candidate for identical request sampling where possible.

3) Functional quality check (0–24h): evaluate prompt-set agreement and business metrics: acceptance threshold default: quality score drift <= 2% absolute and false-positive/undesired-behavior rate delta <= 0.5 percentage points. If the candidate fails, abort and open regression triage.

4) Latency & cost check (0–24h): ensure p95 latency regression <= +15ms or +10% (whichever is smaller), p99 within SLA bounds. Token-cost-per-response must not exceed configured budget for the route (see config_table).

5) Chaos tests (24–48h): run two targeted chaos experiments: a) network elevation: inject 50–150ms additional latency to model host egress paths; b) scheduler preemption simulation: reduce available GPU capacity by 25% for a 30-minute window. Expected outcome: graceful degradation on candidate equal or better than baseline; automatic

latency to model host egress paths; b) scheduler preemption simulation: reduce available GPU capacity by 25% for a 30-minute window. Expected outcome: graceful degradation on candidate equal or better than baseline; automatic fallback must trigger per routing policy without elevated error budget.

6) Load validation (48–72h): increase traffic to 25% of production via staged ramp (1% -> 5% -> 15% -> 25%), each stage held for >= 30 minutes of stable metrics. Verify autoscaling behavior and observe queue/backpressure metrics.

7) Final decision gate: if all checks pass and no new class of failure is observed, promote to 100% with a 30-minute guarded window for automated rollback if SLOs degrade beyond thresholds.
Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Quality regressions on specific prompt sets: run prompt-slicing to isolate failing prompts, revert candidate or pin model to a narrower quant profile; file a regression-triage ticket referencing the eval-harness run id.
- Tokenization/response truncation with long context: verify KV-cache compatibility and sequence-length handling; if failure present, fall back to non-quantized variant or adjust sequence-limits in route config.
- Latency spike under load: reduce canary traffic and enable slower-safe-fallback routing policy (route to smaller-latency variant); open performance bug with runtime team.
- Chaos-induced cascading failures: immediately enable global fallback to baseline model and execute incident playbook 'eng-oncall/incident-process'.
Key metrics captured during each phase (thresholds are defaults; product owners may tighten):
- Functional quality: variant-accuracy (or task-specific metric) — drift <= 2% absolute
- Safety regressions: new safety-flagged responses <= 0.1% of sampled requests
- Latency: p95 <= baseline + 15ms or +10% (min of the two), p99 within SLA (route-specific)
- Error-rate: 5xx rate increase <= +0.05 percentage points
- Cost: tokens-per-response change <= +8%
- Availability: success-rate >= 99.95% during ramp windows

All metrics must be annotated with eval-harness run ids and monitoring-snapshot ids for auditability.
| Field | Purpose | Default/Recommended | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| canary_percent | Fraction of production traffic to route during canary | 1% -> 25% staged | Start at 1% and only increase when all checks pass |
| canary_hold_min | Minimum hold time per stage | 30m | Use longer holds if traffic patterns are bursty |
| quality_drift_threshold | Absolute allowed drift on quality metric | 2% | Configurable per-product |
| latency_regression_limit | Allowed p95 regression | min(+15ms, +10%) | Combined absolute and relative limits |
| chaos_latency_inject | Simulated added latency during chaos | 50-150ms | Run two levels (moderate/strong) depending on risk appetite |
| autoscale_headroom | Extra capacity to reserve during load test | +20% above normal | Prevents false negatives due to transient limits |

Shadow Deployment Evaluation Playbook for Private & Dedicated Environments

Overview:

This playbook defines the standard process and acceptance criteria for "shadow" (non-traffic, mirrored) evaluation deployments of new model builds and quantized model variants in Redwood Private and Dedicated environments. Shadow deployment is intended to provide realistic, safety-aware, and cost-conscious validation without exposing production traffic to unvetted model behavior.

Goals:
- Detect functional regressions and quality drift early when promoting model builds to Dedicated or Private customer pools.
- Verify quantization/3rd-party compilation impacts under representative workload shapes.
- Validate operational metrics (latency p50/p95, memory pressure, KV cache hit distribution) in the target deployment topology.
- Produce deterministic promotion signals for canary/fallback policies in the Redwood Console.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: model promotions intended for Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) installs that will be pinned or exposed to customer traffic.
- Not intended for hosted-only experimentation (use hosted eval harness).

Key definitions:
- Shadow deployment: A deployment that receives a copy of production-like requests (via sampling or replay) but does not return responses to end users.
- Evaluation cohort: A configured set of prompts, demographic slices, and synthetic adversarial cases used during the shadow period.
- Quantization variant: Any model build with reduced precision or kernel-level compilation differences (int8, bfloat16, fq4) intended to lower unit costs.

Prerequisites:
1. Model build has passed unit and integration tests and a baseline acceptance in the central eval harness (see related eval-harness matrix).
2. Target Dedicated/Private environment is provisioned with matching runtime version and kernel profiles.
3. Baseline production telemetry snapshot captured (last 7 days) for comparison.
4. Owner, SRE, and customer (if applicable) sign-off on shadow window and data collection.

Evaluation inputs (test sets & strategies):
- Live-sampled traffic (1-5% of production routed to shadow) OR replayed request traces from the last 72 hours.
- Seeded prompt set: 500 in-distribution prompts representative of heavy-usage features (summarization, instruction-following, extraction).
- Robustness seed: 200 adversarial/noise prompts (typo/obfuscation, ambiguous instructions).
- Long-context stress: 100 prompts with >8k token context to exercise KV cache and attention kernels.
- Safety vectors: 250 safety-sensitive prompts focusing on policy and hallucination triggers.
- Quant-sensitivity partition: the above seed sets with token lengths and shot counts sampled to match expected CTA distributions.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds (promotion-oriented):
- Quality: semantic-similarity-based regression <= 5% drop relative to baseline on the seed test set (metric: pairwise BLEU/ROUGE + embedding cosine > 0.88 for key tasks).
- Safety: no new high-risk safety failures (severity >= 4) introduced; critical safety count must be zero.
- Latency: p50 delta <= +10ms, p95 delta <= +40ms relative to baseline.
- Memory: peak GPU memory <= baseline + 5% for Dedicated; for Private, must meet node

must be zero.
- Latency: p50 delta <= +10ms, p95 delta <= +40ms relative to baseline.
- Memory: peak GPU memory <= baseline + 5% for Dedicated; for Private, must meet node capacity headroom >= 10%.
- KV cache behavior: cache hit-rate change <= 3 percentage points; cold-start token overhead <= 12%.
- Regression triage score: composite (quality, safety, perf) must be green for automated promotion. See scoring formula below.

Composite regression triage score (used to decide automated gating):
- Quality (50%), Safety (30%), Latency & Memory combined (20%).
- Score mapping: Green >= 90, Yellow 70-90 (manual review), Red < 70 (reject).

Shadow deployment configuration example (table as plain text):

- model_variant: my-model-v3-quant-fq4
- routing_mode: mirror (no user-facing responses)
- traffic_sample: 0.02  # 2% of production requests

- eval_window: 48h
- data_retention_for_debug: 30d
- telemetry_enabled: true (tokens, delta-logs, raw-outputs hashed)

Procedure (step-by-step):
1) Preparation (Day -3 to -1)
   - a) Create shadow deployment config in Redwood Console with owner, SLOs, and telemetry toggles.
   - b) Register evaluation cohort (IDs for seed prompt sets, adversarial cases, long-context suite).
   - c) Capture production baseline metrics snapshot (p50/p95 latencies, token cost per request, KV cache distribution).
   - d) Notify SRE and customer success of shadow start time and debug contact.
2) Launch & warm-up (Day 0)
   - a) Start shadow at 0.1% traffic-sample using mirror routing for 2 hours to validate no impact on production.
   - b) Validate telemetry ingestion (token-level breakdowns, kernel selection tags, memory traces).
   - c) Escalate and rollback if initial memory or latency anomalies exceed thresholds (see rollback criteria).
3) Full shadow evaluation (Day 0–2)
   - a) Ramp to target sampling rate (e.g., 2%).
   - b) Run scheduled seeded tests (nightly regression suite) and continuous adversarial stream.
   - c) Run quant-sensitivity comparisons: run paired inference for float vs quant variant on matched requests to compute per-request delta metrics.
4) Analysis (Day 2–3)
   - a) Produce evaluation report summarizing quality, safety, perf, and regression triage score.
   - b) If Yellow, schedule manual triage with ML owner, SRE, and Safety SME; for Red, block promotion and open a regression ticket.
5) Promotion decision (Day 3+)
   - a) If Green, proceed to canary traffic rollout as defined in the canary promotion playbook.
   - b) If manual remediation required, iterate on model or runtime config and re-run shadow.

Rollback criteria (immediate or automated):
- Any critical safety failure (severity >= 4) observed in the shadow outputs.
- Sustained p95 latency exceeding baseline + 100ms for >10 minutes.
- GPU memory OOM or >95% sustained memory utilization for >5 minutes.
- KV cache churn leading to cold-start amplification >25% over baseline.

Onboarding acceptance rubric: KV-cache, quantization, and prompt calibration

Summary
-------
This page defines a prescriptive acceptance rubric for promoting new models (or model variants) into Redwood Inference service stages where the combination of KV-cache behavior, quantization profile, and prompt calibration can materially affect customer-facing quality and cost. It bundles automated checks, sample workloads, and explicit rollback triggers so model owners and SREs can make deterministic release decisions.

Context and goal
----------------
When a model is introduced or migrated (new weights, quantized artifact, or cache strategy) it may introduce subtle regressions: prefix-coherence loss, embedding drift, KV cache miss amplification, token-cost regressions, or tail-latency spikes. This rubric targets three cross-cutting failure modes we see most often in onboarding:
- Cache degradation: higher-than-expected cold-start miss rate or KV eviction-induced coherence regressions.
- Quantization artifacts: hallucination frequency increase, coherence loss for long context, or numeric instability in functioncall args.
- Prompt mismatch: previously calibrated prompt templates that relied on tokenization or temperature defaults behaving differently.

Acceptance philosophy
---------------------
- Gate first on safety & correctness (do not promote a model that increases hallucinations or safety alerts beyond SQC thresholds).
- Gate second on user-impacting regressions (coherence, functioncall correctness, embedded search recall).
- Only after quality gates are satisfied evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs and operational mitigations (adaptive KV-cache sizing, mixed-precision fallback).

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Model owner (author): prepares artifact, provides baseline metrics, and runs offline eval harness.
- Applied ML evaluator: runs the acceptance tests and annotator QA for flagged slices.
- Serving runtime owner: validates KV-cache plumbing and deployment knobs.
- SRE oncall: signs off on rollout plan, monitors live metrics during canary.

Pre-promote checklist (automated and manual steps)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Artifact metadata and reproducibility
   - Provide model artifact SHA, quantization recipe (bits, per-channel/per-tensor, lambda), and tokenizer snapshot.
   - Provide a reproducible Docker image or bundle for private/dedicated deployments.

2) Unit and regression tests (pass/fail)
   - Unit tests: tokenization parity, deterministic seed runs for N=3 seeds show low variance (response divergence < 0.02 normalized JS).
   - Regression probe suite: run full prompt-slice baseline (see Sample workload set below).

3) Safety & correctness gates
   - Safety sentinel pass rate >= baseline - 0.5 percentage points OR delta flagged and annotated with mitigation plan.
   - Functioncall integrity: 99.5% of functioncall responses must preserve schema and required keys on synthetic contract tests.

4) Coherence and semantic fidelity
   - Coherence index (see Metrics section) relative delta <= 1.5 points for high-sensitivity slices.
   - Named-entity recall for QA-style probes: delta <= 3% absolute.

5) KV-cache stability checks
   - Cold-start miss amplification: measured miss-rate in micro-sim shadow < 1.25x baseline for 95th percentile context length.
   - Eviction churn (evictions per minute per model instance) <= baseline +

KV-cache stability checks
   - Cold-start miss amplification: measured miss-rate in micro-sim shadow < 1.25x baseline for 95th percentile context length.
   - Eviction churn (evictions per minute per model instance) <= baseline + 10%.

6) Quantization-specific checks
   - Token-level perplexity increase <= 6% on calibration corpus.
   - Calibration-driven hallucination delta <= 0.8% absolute on adversarial probe set.
   - Per-layer numeric anomaly scan: no layers with activation overflow/underflow events in stress runs.

7) Prompt calibration and token budget checks
   - Tokenization drift (prompt -> token count) <= +5% for canonical prompts.
   - Temperature/Top-p sensitivity: response variance must be within expected band given same sampling settings.

Sample workload set (must be run under the eval harness)
------------------------------------------------------
- Canonical customer prompt family (N=10k probes): intents across translation, summarization, code-completion, and multi-turn chat.
- Long-context stress set (N=2k): 8k–32k token priming, measuring KV-cache hit/miss and tail-latency.
- Functioncall contract set (N=500): schema-anchored calls that assert type and key presence.
- Adversarial coherence set (N=1k): purposely perturbations and priming traps to surface hallucination regressions.

Metrics and explicit thresholds
-----------------------------
All metrics below are measured relative to the baseline model (the currently promoted artifact in stage). Absolute thresholds are listed where appropriate.
- Safety sentinel delta: +0.5 pp tolerated; >+0.5 pp requires annotated mitigation and manual review.
- Coherence index (0–100): high-sensitivity slice delta <= 1.5 points; medium slices <= 2.5.
- Embedding drift (cosine similarity mean on canonical corpus): delta >= -0.02 tolerated; worse requires embedding rebaseline plan.
- Cold-start miss-rate (micro-sim, 99th pct): <= 1.25x baseline.
- Eviction churn (evicts/min/instance at 95th pct): <= baseline + 10%.
- Token cost delta (per-token expected cost): <= +12% tolerated with cost-contingency plan.
- Tail-latency (p99 generation time): <= baseline * 1.2.
- Functioncall schema failure rate: <= 0.5% absolute.

Example acceptance table (pass/fail guidance)
----------------------------------------------
| Gate | Measure | Pass condition | Action if fail |
|------|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Safety | Safety sentinel | delta <= 0.5pp | Reject; escalate; security review |
| Coherence | Coherence index (high) | delta <= 1.5 | Hold; targeted annotation run |
| KV-cache | Cold-start miss 99p | <= 1.25x baseline | Reduce cache pressure; increase per-tenant TTL; re-eval |
| Quant | Token-level perplexity | <= 6% increase | Try per-channel quant; fallback to mixed-precision |
| Prompt | Tokenization drift | <= +5% | Re-calibrate prompts; update canonical templates |

Operational runbook for marginal passes
--------------------------------------
When a model passes quality but violates cost/latency knobs, use an adaptive rollout:
1) Canary: 1–2% traffic for 24 hours with tight telemetry (coherence, safety, cost, p99 latency).
2) If any SQC alert fires, hold traffic and run fast rollback (see Rollback triggers).
3) If cost delta >

2) If any SQC alert fires, hold traffic and run fast rollback (see Rollback triggers).
3) If cost delta > +8% but quality unchanged, enable:
   - Token budget hard-limits via Redwood Console route config.
   - Dynamic batching aggressive thresholds for low-latency slices.
   - Mixed-precision fallback for non-critical tenants.

Rollback triggers (automated)
----------------------------
- Safety sentinel rate increase > +1.0 pp over baseline within rolling 30m window.
- Coherence index drop > 3.0 points on any high-sensitivity slice within 60m.
- Tail-latency p99 increase > 40% sustained for 15m.
- Eviction churn > baseline + 25% for 10m.
If triggered: stall the rollout, immediately execute rollback job (repoint route to previous artifact), create incident ticket with priority = P0 and notify owners.

Telemetry and dashboards to verify during canary
------------------------------------------------
Create a dedicated canary dashboard with these panels:
- Safety sentinel rate (per-tenant) 1m/5m/30m windows.
- Coherence index time series by slice and tenant.
- Cold-start miss-rate histogram and 99th percentile.
- Eviction churn (evicts/min) heatmap by instance.
- Token cost trend (per-route tokenized count * cost per token).
- P99 generation latency and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Functioncall schema failures with detailederror samples.

Calibration procedure for prompts (step-by-step)
----------------------------------------------
1) Run canonical prompt family through tokenization snapshot for both baseline and candidate; compute tokenization drift.
2) For any prompt with drift > +5%, run a priming-level A/B test locally to measure semantic alignment.
3) For templates that are token-compact vs token-expanded, produce two calibrated variants and include routing hint in route config for tenant-level overrides.
4) Update canonical prompt registry with the chosen token-stable variants and mark as locked for the rollout.

Quantization remediation playbook
--------------------------------
If quantization causes a quality regression:
- Immediate actions: increase representative calibration dataset size (add adversarial probes), switch from per-tensor to per-channel where supported, and/or relax clipping.
- Medium-term: re-run mixed-precision hybrid compile with explicit layer exclusions for sensitive layers (embedding and attention-key layers).
- Long-term: maintain a quant-failure catalog mapping probe-to-layer-susceptibility to speed future remediation.

- 0–1h: Verify telemetry ingestion and alerting correctness.
- 1–8h: Monitor safety and coherence slices every 30m and annotate anomalies.
- 8–24h: Compare embedding drift across representative tenants; run lightweight shadow probes.
- 24–72h: Review cost impact and eviction patterns; finalize any token-budget mitigations.

Cohort Synthesis and Mixed‑Precision Onboarding Manual

Summary

This document defines a reproducible process for synthesizing tenant cohorts, validating mixed‑precision (quantized) model variants for production, and integrating cohort‑aware evals and regression triage. It ties together: eval harness integration, prompt/benchmark selection per cohort, quantization profile safety checks, and an incident playbook for cohort‑level regressions. The goal is to reduce deployment risk when migrating live traffic to mixed‑precision model artifacts while preserving per‑tenant quality SLAs.

Scope and applicability

- Services: text-generation API (redwood-serve), chat routing (chat-proxy), and reranking service (ranker-core).
- Deployment modes: hosted API and Dedicated pools.
- Audience: model onboarding engineers, applied ML evaluators, SRE oncall, and solutions engineers running private deployments.

Definitions

- Cohort: a traffic slice grouped by stable attributes (tenant_id, primary_locale, average_context_length, feature_flags).
- Cohort fingerprint: fixed set of probes and telemetry that characterizes expected behavior for a cohort.
- Mixed‑precision onboarding: staged rollout of a quantized model variant (e.g., int8/float16 hybrid) with monitoring and fallback to fp32.

Why cohort synthesis matters

Large tenants and long‑tail tenants react differently to quant changes — some show embedding drift or function‑call instability. Cohort synthesis provides:

1) Representative probes for targeting high‑value regressions instead of global averages.
2) Efficient eval budgets by prioritizing cohorts with the largest cost/quality leverage.
3) Deterministic rollback triggers mapped to cohort‑level KPIs.

Cohort synthesis procedure (step‑by‑step)

1) Collect cohort candidates (data engineer / onboarding lead)
   1.1) Query 30 days of anonymized request metadata: tenant_id, model_id, avg_tokens, locale, function_call_rate.
   1.2) Compute candidate attributes: 95th percentile context length, mean response latency, embedding‑usage frequency.
   1.3) Flag cohorts with >0.5% global traffic share or those with prioritized SLAs.

2) Build cohort fingerprint (applied ML)\   2.1) Select 500–2,000 probe inputs per cohort using stratified sampling across intents and context lengths.
   2.2) Include three probe families: canonical_examples (deterministic intent), boundary_contexts (max tokens / truncated contexts), functioncall_scenarios (tool invocation templates).
   2.3) Label each probe with: probe_id, seed_context_hash, expected_response_anchor (text or structured).

3) Define acceptance criteria (product + SRE + applied ML)\   - Quality SLOs (per cohort): coherence_score >= 0.84 OR fall within 4% of baseline fp32 BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity anchor.
   - Latency SLO: P95 <= baseline_P95 + 40 ms for the same allocation tier.
   - Token cost delta: expected token cost <= baseline_token_cost * 0.95 (target) or <= 1.02 (upper bound).
   - Embedding drift threshold: average cosine shift <= 0.06 for embedding‑based similarity probes.

Eval harness integration checklist

- Create a cohort eval job in the eval orchestrator (eval-orch):
  - job_type: cohort_fingerprint_eval
  - model_variants: [fp32_reference, quant_int8_candidate, hybrid_fp16_int8]
  - probes: path/to/cohort/{{cohort_id}}/probes.jsonl
  - telemetry: capture tokens_per_response, kv_cache_hit_rate, function_call_success_rate, embedding_cosine_shift

- Configuration example (YAML):

  job:
    name: cohort-{{cohort_id}}-mixed-precision-eval
    targets: [fp32-ref, quant-candidate]
    probes_file: s3://eval-assets/cohort/{{cohort_id}}/probes.jsonl
    metrics:
      - name: coherence_score
        aggregator: mean
      - name: embedding_cosine_shift
        aggregator: mean
      - name: p95_latency_ms

telemetry: capture tokens_per_response, kv_cache_hit_rate, function_call_success_rate, embedding_cosine_shift

- Configuration example (YAML):

  job:
    name: cohort-{{cohort_id}}-mixed-precision-eval
    targets: [fp32-ref, quant-candidate]
    probes_file: s3://eval-assets/cohort/{{cohort_id}}/probes.jsonl
    metrics:
      - name: coherence_score
        aggregator: mean
      - name: embedding_cosine_shift
        aggregator: mean
      - name: p95_latency_ms
        aggregator: percentile(95)

- Run schedule: daily for canary window (N=7 days), then hourly during ramp.

Prompt and benchmark guidance for cohorts

- Prompt families: aim for 3 canonical templates + 2 adversarial perturbations per intent.
- Budget: prioritize probes that cause stateful differences (long context continuation, multi‑turn referents).
- Benchmark metrics: coherence_score (human proxy model), instruction_adherence, factuality_sampler (precision@k), functioncall_correctness.

Quantization profile safety checks

Before any shadow or canary rollout, run this checklist:

1) Numeric stability sweep: run ten seeds on the eval harness and compare distributional metrics against fp32 reference (statistical significance test: two‑sample KS test, alpha=0.01).
2) KV cache compatibility: ensure candidate retains cache consistency across chunked streaming for contexts >8k tokens.
3) Function call determinism: for functioncall probes, verify structured output (JSON schema) matches reference for >=98% of probes.
4) Edge slices: test long‑token prompts (tail 1%) and high‑tooltip prompts (URLs/code) explicitly.

Quant tuning knobs to document per model

- layer_skip_threshold: string value (e.g., "top2-fp16")
- per_channel_scale: "true" | "false"
- clamp_strategy: "global" | "adaptive"
- fallback_policy: "immediate-rollout-hold" | "gradual-hedged-fallback"

Example JSON snippet to include in model manifest (store as string here):

{"model_id":"gptx-12b","quant_profiles":[{"name":"int8-hybrid","layer_skip_threshold":"top2-fp16","per_channel_scale":"true","notes":"optimized for long-context workloads"}]}

Staged rollout plan (operations)

1) Shadow validation: mirror 5% of cohort traffic to quant-candidate in shadow for 48–72 hours. No user-visible change. Telemetry: error_rate, coherence_score_delta, embedding_shift.
2) Micro‑canary: route 0.5% of cohort traffic to quant variant via canary route with immediate fallback to fp32 on per‑request failure. Ramp schedule: 0.5% -> 3% -> 10% over 24–72 hours if acceptance criteria met.
3) Mixed‑pool release: introduce quant nodes into dedicated pool at 10% capacity and measure cross‑tenant interference for 7 days.
4) Full cutover: proceed if P95 latency and embedding drift remain within acceptance.

Ownership and runbook triggers

- Owner: model_onboarding_team (primary), applied_ml_evals (secondary).
- SRE oncall notified when embedding_cosine_shift > 0.06 for any cohort OR coherence_score_drop > 0.05 absolute.
- Immediate actions on trigger:
  1) Pause ramp and revert canary routing via routing-control CLI: 
     rdc route update --route canary-{{cohort_id}} --action revert --reason "cohort-quality-trigger"
  2) Kick off Regression Triage runbook (steps below).

Regression triage runbook (cohort emphasis)

1) Triage owner assigned (applied_ml lead) and page created with: cohort_id, last_accepted_model, candidate_model, elapsed_ramp_time.
2) Automated bisect: run eval‑orchestrator bisect between fp32_ref and candidate, isolating by:
   - probe subfamily (functioncall vs long_context)
   - intent cluster (intent_id)
   - token‑budget bucket (short/medium/long)
3) Compare per‑probe diffs and prioritize top‑10 failing probes. Attach diff artifacts and topk embeddings shift table.
4) Hypothesis examples to test: 
   - "quant noise in early layers causing hallucination on multi‑turn

3) Compare per‑probe diffs and prioritize top‑10 failing probes. Attach diff artifacts and topk embeddings shift table.
4) Hypothesis examples to test:

   - "per_channel_scale mismatch for code blocks causing tokenization shifts"
5) Rapid mitigations: rollback, tighten fallback_policy, or apply targeted prompt rewrite for affected cohort.

Observability and dashboards

Minimum dashboard panels per cohort:
- Cohort traffic share (1h / 24h)
- Coherence score trend (baseline vs candidate)
- Embedding cosine shift distribution (boxplot)
- P95 latency by model variant
- Token cost delta and KV cache hit rate

Retention and audit

- Store every cohort eval job snapshot and probes.jsonl for 180 days in s3://eval-snapshots/{cohort_id}/.
- Keep a promotion ledger entry in model_registry: {model_id, cohort_id, timestamp, promotion_state, owner}.

Notes and future work

- Investigate automated prompt rewrite templates as a mitigation baked into the canary route when drift is detected.

Model Exfiltration: Evidence Capture, RBAC Containment, and Compliance Packaging

Overview:

This document defines the standard operating procedure for responding to suspected or confirmed model exfiltration incidents involving Redwood-hosted inference systems. It combines RBAC containment controls, audit log evidence capture queries, data-residency and retention considerations, secure-SDLC remediation guidance, and the compliance packaging checklist required for regulatory/enterprise customers.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to all incidents where model internals, embeddings, prompt corpora, or customer-provided data may have been exfiltrated from any Redwood environment (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Focus is on rapid containment, defensible forensic evidence capture, and creating a reproducible compliance evidence package for audits.

Goals:
1. Stop ongoing exfiltration within 15 minutes of detection where possible.
2. Preserve forensic evidence with documented chain-of-custody.
3. Limit blast radius via RBAC and credential containment.
4. Produce a compliance artifact that supports SOC2/ISO/GDPR inquiries.

Threat model (concise):
- Insider misuse of privileged machine/service accounts.
- API key leakage used to drive high-rate queries and streaming token capture.
- Side-channel or model extraction via repeated adaptive queries.
- Compromise of a private deployment (customer-managed) that can be used to move artifacts to unauthorised locations.

Ownership and responders:
- Incident Commander (IC): Security Oncall (primary).
- Forensics Lead: Security Engineering.
- Service Owner(s): Runtime / Serving (if hosted) or Customer Success for private deploys.
- Legal & Privacy: notified immediately for potential data subject impact.
- Communications: Customer Success and PR as required.

Priority classification:
- P0: Confirmed exfiltration of customer PII or model weights/secret prompt corpora.
- P1: Strong indicators of extraction attempts (high similarity outputs, repeated boundary probing).
- P2: Unusual query patterns without clear exfil evidence.

Immediate triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
1. IC logs timeline and assigns Forensics Lead.
2. Snapshot current access tokens and session table. Note: do NOT revoke yet if live forensic capture is required—coordinate with Forensics Lead.
3. Temporarily throttle or rate-limit suspected API keys/routes.
4. Place affected model endpoints into maintenance mode (deny external requests) if P0/P1.
5. Preserve volatile state: export KV caches, current LRU for KV cache, last-10K request traces for the model shard.

Containment actions (RBAC-focused):
- Immediate actions (if P0):
  1. Revoke all session tokens associated with implicated service identities and API keys via central auth service.
  2. Disable short-lived service principals and mark for rotation (mark "rotating=true" in identity registry).
  3. Apply a temporary deny policy on the model-serving role for all non-essential principals:
     - Example deny policy (pseudo-YAML):
       deny: true
       principal_tags: ["external", "service-account", "developer"]
       resources: ["/models/*/serve", "/models/*/stream"]
       timeframe: "T+0 to T+72h"
- Isolation for private deployments: instruct customer to disable external egress in VPC and snapshot the deployment. Provide step-by-step commands (see "Private deploy containment" below).

Audit log evidence capture (guidance and example queries):
- Preserve immutable audit streams first: forward the affected time window to evidence-bucket with write-once retention (see audit retention policy).
- Minimum evidence fields to capture per request:
  - timestamp, request_id,

Forensic capture checklist (ASCII table):

Data residency & retention considerations:
- If evidence contains EU personal data, keep evidence within EU-bound storage only unless Legal approves cross-border transfer. Mark exports with residency tag: residency=eu|na|apac.
- Evidence retention for compliance packaging:
  - Primary evidence: retain 7 years encrypted (for high-sensitivity incidents) or at least 1 year for lower severity.
  - Secondary artifacts: retain 1 year unless requested otherwise.
  - All retention decisions must be logged in the incident ticket and approved by Legal.

Private deploy containment (customer instructions snippet):
1) SSH into management node: ssh ops@<customer-vpn-ip>
2) sudo iptables -I OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j DROP  # blocks new external connections
3) sudo systemctl stop redwood-agent.service
4) Snapshot /var/lib/redwood/models and upload to customer-provided S3 with immutable flags

Secure SDLC & remediation steps after containment:
1. Triage root cause: credential leakage, model attack pattern, or config issue.
2. Create a scoped fix PR with: code changes, unit tests for input sanitization/rate-limits, and regression prompt-set evals (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).
3. Require mandatory security review and replay of the incident pattern in non-prod for validation.
4. Backport fixes to any maintained runtime branches.
5. Extend CI to include an automated exfiltration smoke-test (detect high-output response patterns).

Compliance evidence packaging (deliverable checklist):
- Cover letter: incident timeline, summary, impact assessment, decision log.

Risk and exceptions governance (temporary elevated access):
- Any emergency elevation for triage must be approved by: IC + Forensics Lead + One Legal approver. Approval must be recorded in the ticket with a start/expiry time (max 72 hours).

Operator preflight: telemetry, security, and runtime prerequisites

Summary

This page is an operator-facing preflight checklist and acceptance template for Redwood Private (VPC / on‑prem) deployments that focuses on three areas often missed during handoffs: telemetry sampling & retention, security (KMS/HSM and image provenance), and runtime / hardware prerequisites. Use this doc before a customer handoff, pre-install dry runs, or an upgrade window to ensure the deployment will meet SLOs, compliance evidence requirements, and day‑2 observability needs.

Scope

- Applies to all Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem) delivered by the Field Engineering and Private Deployments teams.
- Targets initial commissioning and major upgrades (model swap, runtime upgrade, control plane migration).
- Excludes tenant application-level instrumentation (customer responsibility), but includes our agent/collector and runtime telemetry contracts.

Owners and Contacts

- Document owner: eng-private-deployments (Operational Readiness)
- Primary contact: Asha Menon (Field Engineering) — asha.menon@redwood.ai
- Escalation path: Private Deployments Pager -> eng-sre oncall -> Security oncall

Acceptance Criteria (pre-install)

A deployment is considered ready to go live only when all core items below are checked and evidence artifacts are attached to the ticket: configuration export, sample telemetry traces, KMS policy ARN sample, and a signed image provenance manifest. The ticket must include:

1) Telemetry sample file (1 hour synthetic traffic, gzipped JSON or ndjson).
2) KMS / HSM integration verification (kms-test.log).
3) Hardware inventory (serials + firmware versions).
4) Runtime smoke test output (latency, throughput, kv-cache warmup).

Preflight checklist (detailed)

1) Hardware and runtime environment
- GPU type and count: validated against customer capacity workbook (e.g., 8x A100-80GB per tenant for r1 workload).
- Firmware and BIOS: all NICs and BMCs running firmware >= vendor-min for TLS offload and SR-IOV. Document versions in hw-inventory.csv.
- Host OS and kernel: RHEL 8.6+ or Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with kernel >= 5.15. Ensure required modules (nv_peer_mem, rdma) are present if using RoCE.
- Local storage: runtime ephemeral storage >= 500GB for model swap + 2x expected artifact size for safe staging.
- Network MTU: confirm jumbo frames (9000) on data plane where keras/rocksdb replication is used.

2) Network & connectivity
- Control plane egress: allowlist our control plane IPs and TLS fingerprint.
- Model artifact registry access: outbound HTTPS to registry endpoints, TLS1.2+; validate with curl and sha256.
- Tenant subnet design: separate control, data, and operator subnets. Confirm security group rules in vpc-security.yaml.
- Latency requirement: max e2e RTT between operator plane and data plane < 20ms (target), document measured RTTs.

3) Security and key management
- KMS/HSM: confirm key policy supports Envelope Encryption and that our runtime service principal can decrypt keys. Attach kms-test.log demonstrating Encrypt/Decrypt cycle for sample key.
- Key rotation: provide rotation window and automatic rotation script tested in staging.
- Image signing: image manifest must be signed (cosign or equivalent). Provide cosign signature and public key.
- Host attestation: for airgapped sites, TPM attestation report required for first commissioning.
-

script tested in staging.
- Image signing: image manifest must be signed (cosign or equivalent). Provide cosign signature and public key.
- Host attestation: for airgapped sites, TPM attestation report required for first commissioning.
- Secrets injection: confirm secrets delivered via CSI driver or cloud KMS integration; do not persist keys in plain text in runtime config.

4) Telemetry, sampling, and retention (operator contract)
- Telemetry components: runtime-metrics (Prometheus), traces (OpenTelemetry), logs (structured JSON to fluentd/forwarder).
- Sampling strategy: default is adaptive sampling with three tiers:
  - Critical traces (errors, fallback events): 100% sampled
  - High-latency user requests (> 300ms): 20% sampled
  - Background / debug traces: 1% sampled
- Telemetry sampling config (example):
  telemetry:
    traces:
      sampling_strategy: adaptive
      rules:
        - name: critical-errors
          match: "span.attributes.status == 'error'"
          sample_rate: 1.0
        - name: high-latency
          match: "span.duration_ms > 300"
          sample_rate: 0.2
        - name: default-low
          match: "*"
          sample_rate: 0.01
- Retention policy: default local retention for raw traces = 72h, archived nightly to customer S3 for 365 days when requested. Logs: 30 days hot, 365 days cold (compressed). Metrics: 90 days 1s resolution, 3 years aggregated.
- Privacy & PII: ensure PII redaction rules are applied at the collector; attach redaction.yaml demonstrating regex rules and PII tokenization examples.

5) Observability acceptance tests (pre-install smoke)
- Generate synthetic workload of 100 qps for 15 minutes that includes model-compute-heavy and cache-hit patterns. Collect: Prometheus scrape, OTLP traces, sample logs.
- Expected telemetry outputs:
  - Prometheus: key metrics visible (inference_latency_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_utilization).
  - Traces: at least 10 error traces, and representative sampled high-latency traces.
  - Logs: structured logs with fields: request_id, tenant_id, model_name, latency_ms, status.
- Attach synthetic_telemetry_YYYYMMDD.ndjson to ticket.

6) IAM and operator permissions
- Operator service principal permissions: minimal set required to perform runtime operations (pull images, start/stop pods, read secrets). Provide example AWS IAM policy snippet or GCP IAM role mapping.
- Access review: confirm RBAC role binding for operator, and an operator-only emergency-control-plane role for rapid rollback.
- Audit logging: ensure operator actions are logged to a tamper-evident audit sink (CloudWatch/Stackdriver or on‑prem ELK).

7) Model artifacts and compatibility
- Model quantization profile: pre-agreed quantization profiles listed in quantization-profiles.csv.
- Artifact schema: model artifact must include manifest.json (fields: name, version, framework, sha256, tokenizer_sha256, prod_compat_matrix).
- Warm-start validation: runtime must be able to warm KV cache within 120s for the working set. Provide warm-start test output.

Upgrade & rollback prerequisites (before any major upgrade)

- Snapshot: take control-plane and runtime state snapshot; label with ticket id and time.
- KV-cache checkpoint: the operator must create a consistent KV checkpoint export.
- Compatibility gate: run offline compatibility matrix tool against the new runtime and attached models; record report.
- Canary plan: minimum 5% of traffic to canary group with automatic rollback criteria: p95 latency increase > 20% sustained for 5 minutes OR error rate increase > 1% absolute.
- Rollback playbook:

- Rollback playbook: ensure operator has prepopulated rollback_playbook.md in ticket with commands and evidence locations.

Post-install day‑2 observability and SLOs (operator checks within first 24h)

- SLOs to validate:
  - Availability (serving endpoint): 99.95% per tenant for the first 7 days
  - Latency: p95 < 450ms for small models; p95 < 1s for large models (documented per-tenant).

Eval Workflow Optimizer for Mixed-SLO Scenarios

Overview:

This document describes the Eval Workflow Optimizer: a scheduling and orchestration pattern for running evaluation workloads across mixed SLO (latency/cost/quality) targets. The optimizer is intended for the eval-harness fleet and for shadow/onboarding runs used during model promotion, quantization readiness checks, and regression triage.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a repeatable algorithm and reference implementation for prioritizing evaluation probes when budgets or capacity are constrained.
- Support heterogeneous SLO objectives per probe (e.g., 95th percentile latency <= 120ms, quality delta <= 0.5% loss, cost-per-probe <= $0.002).
- Integrate with model-onboarding gates, quantization profile checks, and regression bisect workflows.
- Applicable to scheduled bulk evals, continuous probe streams, and interactive canary runs.

Motivation:
Evaluation queues at Redwood must balance three competing hazards:
1) Missing regressions because parity probes were deprioritized for cost.
2) Cost overruns by running high-fidelity probes unnecessarily.
3) Slow feedback for promotion because latency-sensitive probes are starved.
A single prioritization policy that is aware of SLOs, historical variance, and operational constraints reduces these risks.

High-level goals:
- Multi-objective priority scoring: combine quality-risk, latency-sensitivity, and cost-sensitivity into a single score.
- Explainability: each priority decision should be traceable with contributing factors recorded in probe metadata.
- Pluggability: support alternate scoring modules (e.g., ML-based risk predictor) without changing runtime orchestration.
- Auditability: outputs feed into regression triage and oncall playbooks with deterministic tie-breaking for fast rollback.

Key terminology:
- Probe: a single eval input (prompt set slice) + expected metric(s).
- Eval job: a batch of probes executed together against a model variant.
- SLA class: a label representing a prioritized SLO bucket (e.g., realtime_lowlatency, low_cost_background, high_fidelity).
- Risk score: estimated probability that a probe will reveal a regression above a threshold.

Design overview:
1) Probe metadata enrichment (ingest stage):
   - Every probe includes: probe_id, slice_id, sla_class, expected_token_count, historical_variance, last_seen_delta, quant_profile_id (optional), and onboard_flag.
   - Enrichment service fetches historical telemetry and annotator-derived failure priors.

2) Scoring function (stateless microservice):
   - Inputs: enriched probe metadata + current capacity/cost budget snapshot + model variant attributes (quantization, kv-cache policy).
   - Output: numeric priority score and explanation vector.

3) Scheduler (stateful orchestrator):
   - Pulls prioritized probes and packs them into eval jobs using a packing heuristic that respects per-job max_tokens and latency headroom budgets.
   - Emits job manifests to the cluster and records expected cost.

Priority scoring (reference formula):
- score = w_quality * risk_score_norm + w_latency * latency_impact_norm + w_cost * inverse_cost_norm
- where each component is min-max normalized against a sliding 7-day window.
- default weights (tunable per-team): w_quality=0.5, w_latency=0.3, w_cost=0.2

Component details:
- risk_score_norm: normalized estimate (0..1) of regression likelihood computed from historical failures, semantic-shift signals, and seed-anchored probe variance.
- latency_impact_norm: normalized factor representing the delta to 95p latency if this probe were executed on candidate model (estimated via perf profiles). Higher values indicate probes that expose latency-sensitive regressions.
- inverse_cost_norm: normalized (1 / expected_cost_per_probe). This

representing the delta to 95p latency if this probe were executed on candidate model (estimated via perf profiles). Higher values indicate probes that expose latency-sensitive regressions.
- inverse_cost_norm: normalized (1 / expected_cost_per_probe). This biases towards cheaper probes when cost weight is high.

Explainability and provenance:
- Each scored probe includes explanation vector: [risk:0.72, latency:0.18, cost:0.10] and a short text reason.
- The scheduler writes an entry to the eval ledger: {probe_id, score, model_variant, run_id, timestamp, explanation}. The ledger is append-only for audit.

Operational policies and SLO alignment:
- SLA class mapping examples:
  - realtime_lowlatency: w_latency=0.5, w_quality=0.4, w_cost=0.1, run window: 00:00-23:59 (preemptive on dedicated pools).
  - high_fidelity: w_quality=0.8, w_latency=0.05, w_cost=0.15, run window: batch-friendly offhours.
  - cost_background: w_cost=0.7, w_quality=0.2, w_latency=0.1, run window: cheapest cloud region preference.
- Fairness rule: at least 5% of high_fidelity probes are scheduled per day for each active model-variant to avoid blind spots.

Workflows and playbooks:
A) Model onboarding (promotion path)
1. Start: model candidate pushed to staging and assigned an onboarding job with mixed SLO bundles.
2. The optimizer schedules: small realtime_lowlatency probe set (fast feedback), prioritized high_fidelity probes (quality gate), and cost_background breadth probes.
3. Promotion decision rules (examples):
   - Must pass high_fidelity gate: quality delta <= 0.25% on critical slices.
   - Latency gate: 95p latency no worse than baseline + 25ms for realtime slices.
   - Cost gate: expected cost increase <= 10% over baseline or quantization-mitigated.
4. If any gate fails, create regression-triage ticket and enqueue targeted bisect probes.

B) Continuous probe stream (production monitoring)
1. Live telemetry feeds risk spikes to enrichment service.
2. Optimizer reweights probes dynamically (increase w_quality when drift detected).
3. If aggregated risk > threshold, run an urgent canary: 2x high_fidelity probes with human review.

C) Regression triage integration
1. When a regression alert is raised, the triage playbook triggers a focused eval job: probes are scored with w_quality=0.9 and packed for fastest execution (prefer pre-warmed hosts).
2. Bisect strategy: binary search across recent model changes and quantization_profile_id variants.
3. Triage output: causal hypothesis, evidence probes, and recommended rollback or mitigation (e.g., quant-fallback).

Configuration reference (table):

| max_tokens_per_job | int | 200000 | scheduler packing limit |
| max_concurrent_jobs | int | 12 | cluster-level throttle |
| cost_budget_per_hour | float | 5.0 | USD/hour target for eval pool |
| quant_profile_id | string | qpf-2026-03 | optional quantization profile to test against |

Multi-tenant KV-cache and Quantization Fallback Onboarding Playbook

Overview
========

Purpose: This playbook defines the operational, telemetry, and safety checklist for onboarding a model variant into Redwood's multi-tenant serving environment when the deployment path includes both KV-cache sensitive performance characteristics and quantization fallbacks (mixed-precision or int8 variants). The document targets ML engineers, release engineers, and platform owners.

Scope:
- New model variants that will serve multiple tenants behind a shared routing layer.
- Rollouts that plan to use an unquantized baseline with quantized fallback(s) enabled for cost/latency optimization.
- Integration with existing shadow/production evaluation harness and canary pipelines.

Why this is needed:
- KV-cache (prefix + KV) behavior leads to amplification of small distribution shifts; quantization can change token-level generation patterns; combining both without explicit evaluation causes hard-to-detect regressions for tenants with long-context or few-shot priming.

Owners and Contacts
-------------------
- Playbook owner: Priya Menon (ML Infra)
- Runtime owner: Arjun Rao (Serving Runtime)
- Observability owner: Maya Alvarez (Platform Observability)
- Oncall alias for rollout day: #model-rollouts (Slack)

Acceptance Criteria (high level)
------------------------------
1. No increase in tenant-facing fidelity regressions above defined thresholds (see "SLOs and thresholds").
2. KV-cache hit/miss distribution remains within delta window after rollout (see "Telemetry contract").
3. Quantization fallback path does not trigger for >5% of requests in steady-state unless configured for burst policy.
4. Automated rollback trigger tests validate end-to-end path within 10 minutes of detection.

Preflight checklist (table)
-------------------------
| Item ID | Check | Expected value / action | Responsible |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Eval suite: multi-tenant slice coverage executed | All slices green (pass/fail threshold defined in eval matrix) | ML Engineer |
| P2 | Shadow traffic run (24h, representative) | Latency/QLoss within baseline ±10% | Release Engineer |
| P3 | KV-cache warmup profile collected | Baseline and new model priming curves recorded | Runtime Owner |
| P4 | Quant fallback artifact verified | Checksum + unit tests | Model Owner |
| P5 | Telemetry ingestion validated | Traces, token-level metrics, and sample capture functioning | Observability |
| P6 | Security/DP review | No additional PII leakage vectors added | Security |

Note: If any P* fails, block rollout and follow the Regression Investigation flow.

SLOs and thresholds
-------------------
- Fidelity regression alert: mean fidelity score drop > 2.0 points on prioritized prompt set (see eval matrix) for >30m.
- Latency SLO (p95): must not increase by more than 20ms or 10% (whichever is larger) on multi-tenant routes.
- KV-cache hit rate delta: absolute change <= 3 percentage points within first 1h of rollout.
- Quant-fallback triggering rate: <= 5% at steady state (after 1h); can be higher during controlled burst phases but must

delta: absolute change <= 3 percentage points within first 1h of rollout.
- Quant-fallback triggering rate: <= 5% at steady state (after 1h); can be higher during controlled burst phases but must be documented.

Telemetry contract (what must be emitted)
----------------------------------------
- token_generation.metrics: {
    "token_latency_ms",
    "quant_fallback_flag" (0/1),
    "kv_cache_hit" (0/1),
    "model_variant",
    "tenant_id",
    "request_id"
  }
- trace/span naming: /serving/<model_variant>/generate with tags: tenant_id, route, sequence_length, kv_prefix_len
- periodic 5m rollup: per-tenant p50/p95 latency, kv hit rate, fallback rate, fidelity score (from samplers)

Rollout strategy (step-by-step)
-------------------------------
1. PREPARE (T-72 to T-2 hours)
   - Run the full onboarding eval harness against static probe set + tenant-prioritized slices.
   - Produce baseline and candidate artifacts (model binary, quant params, kernel hints) in artifact registry.
   - Schedule 24h shadow run using representative traffic (sample ratio 1:1 to shadow).
2. SHADOW VALIDATION (T-48 to T-12 hours)
   - Observe KV prime/warm curves. If warmup curve lag > 25% vs baseline, adjust cache TTL or prewarm strategy.
   - Check token-level divergences: run automated delta-annotation for top-500 diffs.
3. CANARY (T-6 to T+1 hours)
   - Route 1% of production traffic (stratified by tenant size) to candidate variant with quant fallback enabled.
   - Configure aggressive alerting: fidelity drop, p95 latency increase, quant fallback rate > 10% in canary window.
4. GRADUAL ROLL (T+1 to T+24 hours)
   - If canary healthy, ramp 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 30–60 minute observation windows between steps.
   - For each ramp step, run a short micro-eval of 200 prioritized prompts (automated) and compare fidelity; must be within threshold.
5. POST-ROLL (T+24 to T+72 hours)
   - Maintain increased fidelity telemetry and sample collection for 72 hours.
   - Run full regression triage on any failures and create a postmortem with mitigation.

Rollback and fast-fail triggers
------------------------------
Automatic rollback triggers (immediate rollback):
- Fidelity regression alert fires (see SLOs).
- Quant-fallback rate exceeds 20% for >10 minutes on any tenant flagged as high-sensitivity.
- p95 latency increases by >50ms and error rate increases >0.5% simultaneously.

Manual rollback triggers (investigate then rollback):
- KV-cache hit-rate degradation >6 percentage points for >30 minutes.
- Repeated user-reported semantic regressions from >3 distinct tenants in 1h.

Rollback steps (fast path):
1. Run rollback command (example CLI below).
2. Disable quant fallback (if that was the source) using runtime flag and revert model variant to baseline.
3. Notify #model-rollouts and schedule immediate triage.

Example CLI and YAML snippets
----------------------------
CLI: roll forward / rollback
- rwdctl model rollout --model-id candidate-2026-01 --route multi-tenant-prod --percent 1
- rwdctl model rollback --route multi-tenant-prod --to model-baseline-2025-12

Runtime YAML (serving policy fragment):
---
model_variant: candidate-2026-01
quant_fallback:
  enabled: true
  threshold_tokens: 512
  max_trigger_rate: 0.05 # 5%
kv_cache:
  ttl_seconds: 3600
  prewarm_strategy: "prefix-sample"
  warm_threshold_requests: 100
ramp_policy:
  steps:

model rollback --route multi-tenant-prod --to model-baseline-2025-12

Runtime YAML (serving policy fragment):
---
model_variant: candidate-2026-01
quant_fallback:
  enabled: true
  threshold_tokens: 512
  max_trigger_rate: 0.05 # 5%
kv_cache:
  ttl_seconds: 3600
  prewarm_strategy: "prefix-sample"
  warm_threshold_requests: 100
ramp_policy:
  steps: [1,5,20,50,100]
  observe_minutes: 45
---

Investigation playbook (if a regression is detected)
--------------------------------------------------
1. Triage owner acknowledges on Slack and opens an incident ticket (prefix MODEL-ROLL).
2. Attach sample payloads from token_generation.metrics and the 500 top divergence examples.
3. Run degrad-bisect to determine whether divergence is due to quantization or KV-cache interaction.
   - degrad-bisect --model-a model-baseline --model-b model-candidate --slice tenant:sensitive,context:long
4. If quantization implicated: reproduce locally with quantized artifact and run token-by-token diff; consult quant-profile team.
5. If KV-cache implicated: replay priming sequences and inspect cache keys + eviction timings; consult runtime scheduling team.
6. Prepare short-term mitigation: tighten fallback threshold, increase cache TTL, or pause rollout.

Operational tips and best practices
----------------------------------
- For long-context tenants, prefer gradual cache prewarm strategies and explicit priming probes during shadow runs.
- Use tenant-aware ramping: small tenants can be enrolled earlier; large/high-sensitivity tenants should be included last.
- Maintain a curated set of 1,000 tenant-prioritized prompts for continuous micro-eval during all rollout phases.
- Keep quant fallback artifacts in immutable registry with signed checksums and short LRU of active candidates.

Appendix A — Sample micro-eval command
------------------------------------
 rwd-eval run --suite micro-priority --model candidate-2026-01 --topk 1 --sample 200 --out results/candidate-micro.json

Appendix B — Example telemetry query (SQL-like)
------------------------------------------------
SELECT tenant_id,
  COUNT(*) as requests,
  AVG(token_latency_ms) as avg_token_ms,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY token_latency_ms) as p95_token_ms,
  SUM(quant_fallback_flag)::float / COUNT(*) as fallback_rate,
  SUM(kv_cache_hit)::float / COUNT(*) as kv_hit_rate
FROM token_generation_metrics
WHERE model_variant = 'candidate-2026-01'
  AND timestamp >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY requests DESC
LIMIT 200;

Appendix C — Known limitations
------------------------------
- This playbook assumes availability of per-token telemetry; teams without token-level traces must run longer shadow windows.
- Multi-tenant privacy constraints can limit prompt sampling for some customers — ensure opt-in is handled before sampling prompts.

Onboarding-to-service eval playbook: cost-latency-quality triage

Summary:
This playbook describes a prescriptive, reproducible process for taking a candidate model + runtime configuration from model-onboarding to production service with explicit gates for cost, latency, and output quality. It unifies eval harness runs, benchmark prompt sets, quantization triggers, and a compact regression triage flow so that engineers and ML owners can make consistent, auditable promotion decisions.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to text-generation and chat-capable transformer models being served on Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers staged validation: lab (controlled), shadow (traffic-mirroring), micro-canary (low-traffic), and canary-to-full rollout.
- Integrates: eval harness reports, prompt-slice benchmarks, quantization profiles, telemetry thresholds, and triage runbooks.
- Not covered: new multimodal model architecture onboarding (see separate spec), or offline-only research experiments.

Definitions:
- R-SI (Response Stability Index): the primary automated quality index computed by the eval harness; lower is better. Relative drop (%) is measured against the baseline model pinned to the serving route.
- Throughput SLO: tokens/sec per GPU under steady-state microburst.
- Latency SLO (p95): target p95 Round-Trip Token latency for a canonical request size (e.g., 256 tokens).
- Cost delta: per-1k token cost change projected by the Optimize toolkit comparing current and candidate config.

Owner and expected contributors:
- Model owner: individual or team responsible for model quality (ML team).
- Runtime owner: serving-runtime team (eng-serving-runtime).
- Eval steward: applied-ml team member running the harness and reviewing results.
- Release approver: product or platform PM for public routes.

Prerequisites (pre-run checklist):
1) Model artifact is registered in the model catalog with metadata (architecture, tokenizer, sequence-length, kv-cache compatibility, quantization hints).
2) A canonical prompt set exists for the target workload with representative slices (happy path, long-context, safety-sentinels, hallucination probes).
3) Baseline model pin and baseline telemetry baseline snapshot (last 30d).
4) CI job: eval-harness job and shadow-routing configuration are defined in the service's repo.

Evaluation stages (prescriptive):
1) Lab evaluation (local harness)
   - Purpose: find obvious regressions, sensitivity to context length and quantization.
   - Actions:
     a) Run eval-harness with the canonical prompt set (N=3 random seeds) and deterministic RNG where supported.
     b) Compute slice-level R-SI, semantic similarity (embedding cosine) against baseline, and answer acceptance rate on golden-label subsets.
     c) If candidate is quantized, include quant-replay test (replay identical inputs through quantized and fp32 variants).
   - Acceptance gate: no slice with >4% absolute drop in acceptance rate OR >8% relative increase in R-SI.

2) Shadow (mirrored traffic)
   - Purpose: collect real-traffic failure modes and latency/cost telemetry without impacting users.
   - Actions:
     a) Enable 100% mirror to candidate for a minimum of 24 hours or 1M tokens (whichever comes first).
     b) Capture production prompts and classify into slices offline; compare token-distribution differences.
     c) Compute live latency p50/p95 and error-rate delta vs baseline; calculate projected cost delta.
   - Shadow gates (auto-fail): p95 latency increase > 25% relative OR tail

into slices offline; compare token-distribution differences.
     c) Compute live latency p50/p95 and error-rate delta vs baseline; calculate projected cost delta.
   - Shadow gates (auto-fail): p95 latency increase > 25% relative OR tail error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute OR projected cost delta > +40% and no compensating quality improvement.

3) Micro-canary (live limited traffic)
   - Purpose: validate user-visible quality and operational behavior under small production load.
   - Actions:
     a) Route 0.1% traffic for 2 hours, then 1% for 6 hours, then 5% for 24 hours if stable.
     b) Activate short-window alerting for R-SI and user-complaint events.
   - Canary gates: any human-reported quality regression or R-SI drift > 3% triggers rollback.

4) Staged rollout and final promotion
   - Purpose: full production promotion with rollback/rollback-conditions defined.
   - Actions:
     a) Gradual shift by 10% every 6 hours with monitoring checkpoints.
     b) Post-rollout 72-hour quality audit comparing sampled prompts to baseline.
   - Final acceptance: no persistent slice-level regression after 72 hours, latency/cost within agreed band.

Quantization trigger matrix (when to try quantized candidate):
| Signal | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Cost pressure | Projected token cost delta > +30% on baseline | Evaluate quantization variant (8-bit or mixed) to recover cost budget |
| Throughput shortage | Observed tokens/sec per GPU < target by >20% | Evaluate reduced-precision and KV layout optimizations |
| Model size | Artifact > 80GB | Prefer 8-bit-mixed or per-channel quant profile |
| Quality sensitivity | Safety-heavy slices drop >2% when quantized | Run block-fallback profiling and finer-grain quant (per-layer) |

Quantization evaluation checklist:
- Maintain exact seed pairs for replay: store (input, seed, baseline_output, quant_output).
- Run per-layer activation-correlation and attention-distribution checks.
- Run the quantized artifact through the eval-harness slice-by-slice and produce a quant-delta report.
- If quant-delta > configured threshold for safety slices, mark as "requires manual tuning" and do not proceed to shadow.

- Small quality drift in low-impact slices: allow canary expansion only if compensating human-in-the-loop review plan is in place and mitigation (prompt rewrite or scoring filter) is added.

Model Onboarding: Fast-Feedback Readiness & Regression Escalation Lifecycle

Overview:

This guide defines the production-readiness lifecycle for newly onboarded models at Redwood Inference with an emphasis on fast automated feedback, deterministic gating, and a clear regression escalation path. The goal is to reduce time-to-serving while keeping user-facing quality and cost SLOs within approved bounds.

Audience:
- Model owners (Applied ML)
- Serving engineers and runtime owners
- QA/evaluation engineers
- SRE and oncall

Definitions and Services referenced:
- eval-harness-service: automated job runner that executes canonical prompt sets and scoring hooks.
- onboard-check-runner: lightweight job that performs smoke checks, latency/throughput probes, and quick safety heuristics.
- quant-profile-db: persisted quantization recommendations produced by QuantTuner jobs.
- model-cert-bucket: storage for artifacts and eval outputs (S3 path pattern: s3://model-cert/{model}/{version}/)

Readiness Gates (automated, required):
1) Build & Artifact Gate
   - Model artifact present in model-cert-bucket with metadata.json including: model_arch, tokenizer_version, expected_seq_len.
   - checksum validated against CI release tag.

2) Performance Gate (throughput/latency)
   - p95 generation latency for 512-token synthetic prompts: <= 220ms on target Dedicated instance type (A10xX).
   - throughput for batching profile B (batch_size=8, concurrency=4): >= 120 tokens/sec.

3) Quality Gate (eval harness results)
   - Primary prompt set: mean BLEU/ROUGE/ExactMatch (per-application) must be within -1.5% absolute of the baseline model or pass manual tolerance defined in metadata.
   - Safety heuristics: 0 high-confidence Toxicity flags on the safety prompt subset (see "safety-prompt-set").

4) Quantization Compatibility Gate (if quantized profile requested)
   - end-to-end generation delta (semantic similarity) computed by eval-harness-service must be >= 0.95 cosine similarity for embeddings and <= 3% token-level edit distance.
   - quant-profile-db entry created and signed by QuantTuner job.

Gate thresholds matrix (canonical):

| Gate | Metric | Threshold |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Performance | p95 latency (512 toks) | <= 220ms |
| Performance | tokens/sec (batch B) | >= 120 |
| Quality | BLEU/ROUGE delta vs baseline | >= -1.5% |
| Quality | Safety high-confidence flags | == 0 |
| Quant | Embedding cosine sim (quant vs float) | >= 0.95 |
| Regression | Eval variance vs rolling mean | <= 2 sigma |
Onboarding step-by-step (fast-feedback workflow):
1) Development -> CI
   - Push model artifact; CI builds container image and uploads model artifacts to model-cert-bucket.
   - CI triggers onboard-check-runner (smoke). Failure here blocks further steps.

2) Automated fast-eval (0-30 minutes)
   - onboard-check-runner invokes eval-harness-service with the "fast-feedback" prompt shard (subset ~200 prompts representing critical intents).
   - Command (examples):

   curl -X POST https://internal.eval/redwood/run \n     -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${EVAL_TOKEN}' \n     -d '{"model":"redwood/new-model:v1","profile":"fast-feedback","output_path":"s3://model-cert/new-model/v1/fast-eval.json"}'

   - eval-harness-service returns a job ID and a summary JSON. Fast-eval must pass all gates above to proceed to full-eval.

3) Full-eval (30 min - 3 hours)
   - On success of fast-eval, the full prompt catalog (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks) is executed. Results included: accuracy/ROUGE/BLEU distributions, calibration curves, perplexity, embedding drift metrics, and safety audit.
   - Full-eval artifacts are stored at model-cert-bucket.

4) Quant evaluation (parallel)
   -

the full prompt catalog (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks) is executed. Results included: accuracy/ROUGE/BLEU distributions, calibration curves, perplexity, embedding drift metrics, and safety audit.
   - Full-eval artifacts are stored at model-cert-bucket.

4) Quant evaluation (parallel)
   - If quantized variants are requested, QuantTuner schedules candidate quant profiles and runs the eval harness with quantized binaries.
   - Outputs a signed quant-profile-db entry with profile id and performance tradeoffs.

5) Review & Certification
   - If any gate fails, a regression triage ticket is created automatically. If all gates pass, the model transitions to "canary-serving" state under the rollout system.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Model owner: provides metadata, selects baseline, owns prompt set tagging and acceptance criteria.
- Eval owner: maintains eval-harness-service, ensures prompt shards and scoring hooks are up-to-date.
- Runtime owner: verifies performance profiles and kernel selection for deployment target.
- SRE: monitors canary and rollback triggers; owns PagerDuty policy for regressions.

Regression triage and escalation (integrated flow):
1) Detection:
   - Automated monitors compare current full-eval to rolling 30-day baseline. Any metric breach (see gates matrix) emits an alert to the eval-alerting pipeline.

2) Triage automation:
   - eval-alerting creates a JIRA with tags: regression, model:{name}, version:{v}. Summary includes links to model-cert-bucket artifacts and diff plots.
   - A Slack notification posted in #model-regressions with quick actions (view artifacts, run reproduce job).

3) Triage steps (recommended):
   1. Reproduce locally using the reproducible-runner container. Command: docker run --rm -e S3_KEY=... repro-runner:latest reproduce --job-id {job}
   2. If reproduction matches, escalate to model-owner and runtime-owner.
   3. If regression is quality (semantic), attach failing prompt examples and assign to Model owner for prompt-augmentation or model rollback.
   4. If regression is performance, open infra ticket and consider fallback to higher-cost but stable variant.

4) Rollback policy:
   - Automatic rollback triggers when user-facing error rate increases > 0.5% or latency p95 > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes during canary.
   - Manual rollback can be initiated by oncall with approvals from SRE and Model owner.

Operational runbook (quick troubleshooting):
- Symptom: Fast-eval failed with high toxicity flags.
  1) Inspect fast-eval summary at model-cert-bucket and open safety-audit job details.
  2) Run targeted safety prompt subset with a lower temperature; confirm deterministic repeat.
- Symptom: p95 latency violation in dedicated environment.
  1) Check kernel selection logs produced by runtime-telemetry (service: runtime-metrics).
  2) Re-run perf probe using runtime-local-prober and record nvprof traces.

Priming Lexicon and Quantization Robustness for Multimodal Onboarding

Summary
-------
This document defines a standard priming lexicon and a complementary robustness test matrix for onboarding multimodal models into Redwood's serving fleet, with a focus on quantized artifact resilience, priming stability across modalities, and explicit triage steps when degradation is observed. It is intended for Applied ML engineers, model onboarding owners, and evaluator teams responsible for promotion to shadow/dedicated/private stages.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
- Multimodal models (image+text, audio+text) show different failure modes under lower-precision kernels and KV-cache interactions.
- Current onboarding checklists focus on textual coherence and latency; this doc fills the gap for "priming" (how we initialize context across modalities) and explicit quantization robustness tests.
- Aligns with Redwood's production-first thesis: predictability and measurable regression guards before rolling to hosted/dedicated/private.

Goals
-----
1. Define a canonical priming lexicon (phrases, structure, metadata) used by eval harnesses and shadow traffic to ensure consistent prompting across services.
2. Provide a quant-robustness test matrix covering precision modes (fp16, int8, mixed), KV-cache stress, and multimodal encoding edge cases.
3. Specify telemetry, pass/fail thresholds, and an automated triage flow for regressions.
4. Offer a lightweight config snippet and example CLI commands to run the suite locally and in CI.

Scope
-----
- Applies to multimodal encoder-decoder and decoder-only families onboarded to Redwood's runtime.
- Includes both synthetic priming probes and live-traffic shadow probes.
- Excludes: model training guidance, hardware procurement, and customer-specific prompt engineering.

Definitions
-----------
- Priming lexicon: curated set of tokens/phrases and structure used to initialize the model across modalities (e.g., <IMG_DESC> ... <TEXT_PROMPT>).
- Quantization mode: the execution precision/configuration used (e.g., fp16, int8-static, int8-dynamic, mixed16/8).
- Shadow probe: a probe derived from live traffic but anonymized and reweighted for eval.

Priming lexicon: structure and examples
-------------------------------------
Design principles:
- Deterministic anchors: include a short, deterministic anchor sentence to stabilize generation (e.g., "Context anchor: describe the content concisely.")
- Modality markers: explicit tokens that indicate modality boundaries (TEXT_START, IMAGE_START, AUDIO_START)
- Minimalism: prefer concise anchors to avoid excessive token budgets and reduce KV-cache divergence.
- Diagnostic suffixes: append structured diagnostic fields when running evals: [PRIME_ID=xxx][SEED=42][MODE=shadow]

Canonical priming templates (examples)
- Image caption baseline:
  IMAGE_START
  <IMG_HASH>
  Context anchor: Describe the main subject and visible attributes in one sentence.
  TEXT_START
  Provide a concise caption.

- Multiturn assistant with image:
  TEXT_START
  User: I uploaded an image showing a chart. Provide a summary and 3 action items.
  IMAGE_START
  <IMG_HASH>
  DIAGNOSTIC: [PRIME_ID=chart-summarize][MODE=shadow]

Quantization robustness test matrix (table)
-----------------------------------------
| Test name | Input modality | Quant modes | Stressor | Metric | Pass threshold | Notes |
|-----------|----------------|-------------|----------|--------|----------------|-------|
| Priming-stability-image-anchors | image+text | fp16, int8-static, int8-dyn | image noise, resized to 64-2048 px | caption semantic

| Quant modes | Stressor | Metric | Pass threshold | Notes |
|-----------|----------------|-------------|----------|--------|----------------|-------|
| Priming-stability-image-anchors | image+text | fp16, int8-static, int8-dyn | image noise, resized to 64-2048 px | caption semantic overlap (BLEU/ROUGE) + embedding cosine | >= 0.87 cosine vs fp16 baseline | run 500 seeds per image family |
| KV-cache-consistency | long-conversation text | fp16, mixed8 | repeated prefix inflations | token-stream divergence ratio | <= 0.05 | measure at token 256 and 1024 |
| Modality-fallback-sanity | image absent but marker present | int8-dyn | missing modality | hallucination rate | <= 0.02 | detectors for hallucinated entities |
| Latency-tail-quant | multimodal batch | int8-static | microburst batching | p99 latency increase vs fp16 | <= 1.35x | target region-specific kernels |

Onboarding checklist (promote model -> shadow -> canary -> prod)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Preflight: run unit evaluations and ensure deterministic seed-based artifact generation for priming templates (artifact hashes stored in artifact-registry).
2. Quant-compatibility run: execute the quant-robustness matrix across the supported quant modes. Attach generated metrics to the model artifact metadata.
3. Shadow validation: launch shadow probes (1% of traffic equivalence) with priming lexicon enabled. Run for 48h or 500k generated tokens, whichever is sooner.
4. Canary rollout: if shadow passes, canary 5% traffic for 24h using mixed precision and KV-cache warming; enable automated rollback ACL.
5. Production promotion: require 4 consecutive days of stable SLOs and no regression ticket older than 24h in alerting queue.

Automated test runner: example config snippet
-------------------------------------------
(Place in eval-runner configs as eval/priming-quant.json)

{
  "suite_name": "priming-quant-robustness",
  "priming_templates": ["image-caption-baseline","multiturn-assistant-image"],
  "quant_modes": ["fp16","int8-dyn","mixed8"],
  "iterations_per_test": 500
}

CLI example
-----------
- Local run: 
  ./tools/eval-runner --config eval/priming-quant.json --model-repo /mnt/models/repo --mode local --out results/prime-2026.json
- CI run: 
  ci/eval-job --suite priming-quant-robustness --artifact $MODEL_ARTIFACT --commit $GITHUB_SHA

Telemetry, metrics and SLOs
--------------------------
- Primary metrics collected per-test: embedding_cosine_vs_fp16, semantic_score, hallucination_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency.
- SLOs for onboarding: embedding_cosine_vs_fp16 >= 0.87, hallucination_rate <= 0.03, p99_latency <= 1.5x baseline.
- Alerting: create a regression ticket automatically if any metric crosses a soft threshold (cosine<0.89) and page on hard thresholds (cosine<0.85 or hallucination>0.05).

Failure modes and triage playbook
--------------------------------
- If embedding_cosine drops by 0.03 vs fp16:
  1. Re-run with different seeds and higher iteration (x5) to reduce stochastic variance.
  2. Run per-slice breakdown (by modality, image resolution, language) to isolate failing cohorts.
  3. If concentrated on quant mode int8-static, escalate to Quant team for kernel re-evaluation.
- If hallucination_rate increases for missing-modality probes: revert to previous priming anchor and run a targeted priming-ablation test to identify sensitive tokens.

Manual inspection checklist
-------------------------
- Sample failed probes (50) and annotate: failure class, severity, suggested fix.
- Check model logits snapshots (use eval-logcat) at token positions where divergence observed.

Rollout and rollback controls

Appendix: sample probe generation recipe

3. For each variant, produce 50 prompt seeds using the canonical priming lexicon with diagnostic suffixes.
4. Run against fp16 baseline and each quant mode; store all outputs and embeddings.
