Annotator Identity Redaction and Privacy Protocol

Overview

This document defines Redwood's standard protocol for redacting and managing annotator identity and other sensitive metadata in probe and annotation pipelines used by the Applied ML & Evals teams. It covers the threat model, deterministic and probabilistic redaction rules, the end-to-end annotation lifecycle changes required, integration points with ProbeFarm and the Evaluator harness, monitoring and audit evidence requirements, and a staged rollout checklist.

Goals
- Eliminate storage and transit of direct identifiers for annotators (names, internal IDs mapped to payroll, email addresses) in datasets that are accessible outside the annotation service boundary.
- Maintain auditability and non-repudiation for operational and compliance review without revealing PII.
- Provide deterministic redaction heuristics that are reproducible and testable across environments (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Ensure annotation quality and productivity SLAs remain within acceptable bounds after redaction.

Scope and Definitions
- Annotator identity: any information that can be used to identify a specific human annotator (full name, corporate email, employee id).
- Annotator handle: anonymized persistent identifier assigned by the annotation service (example: ANNO::sha256(seed||region||role)).
- Probe record: the unit of work sent to annotators via ProbeFarm or the external vendor integration.
- Sensitive metadata: annotator identity, free-text comments containing PII, timestamps with sub-second precision tied to single-annotator sequences.

Threat Model
- Accidental exposure from dataset exports, debug logs, or telemetry pipelines.
- Malicious insider access to dataset stores containing raw annotation logs.
- Cross-tenant leakage in shadow evals or federated probe federations.

Redaction Principles
1) Minimize: only retain fields strictly necessary for evaluation and QA.
2) Transform: replace direct identifiers with deterministic, irreversible handles.
3) Separate: keep raw mapping (annotator handle -> identities) inside a restricted key-value store (KMS-protected, audited) with TTL and strict RBAC.
4) Audit: emit immutable audit events when mapping lookups occur; store audit records in the compliance bucket.
5) Fail-safe: pipeline components must be able to redact on-write and redact-on-read where necessary.

Redaction Rules (canonical)
- annotator_name -> REMOVE (never stored in evaluation datasets).
- annotator_email -> REMOVE.
- annotator_employee_id -> hash_sha256(lowercase(employee_id||salt)) stored as annotator_handle.
- annotator_handle: formatted as "ANNO::<first-8-hex-of-hash>". Always produced from a key derivation using a per-environment salt (salt stored in KMS).
- annotations.free_text: run PII detector; redact detected PII spans. Keep redaction markup consistent: [REDACTED:PII_EMAIL], [REDACTED:PII_PHONE], [REDACTED:PII_NAME].
- timestamps: round to nearest minute for exported datasets unless subsampled for temporal QA.

Example: redaction transformation pseudocode

1) input_record = {
  "probe_id": "pf-12345",
  "annotator_name": "Jordan Lee",
  "annotator_email": "jordan.lee@redwood.ai",
  "employee_id": "E-09876",
  "annotation": "Customer shared SSN 123-45-6789 and email alt@example.com"
}

2) salt = load_kms_secret("annotator-handle-salt")
3) handle_hash = sha256(lowercase(employee_id)+salt)
4) annotator_handle = "ANNO::" + handle_hash[0:8]
5) annotation_text = pii_detector(annotation); // returns redacted text with tags
6) output_record = {
  "probe_id": "pf-12345",
  "annotator_handle":

}

Operational Requirements
- Annotation service (ProbeFarm) must support redaction-on-write at the source connector for all internal and vendor systems.
- Exported evaluation bundles to S3/Blob must never contain annotator names or emails. Export job will run a post-export scanner with a zero-tolerance policy; any match blocks the export and alerts compliance.
- The raw mapping (annotator_handle -> real_identity) is stored in a dedicated vault: secret path /platform/annotations/annotator-mapper, accessible only by the Annotation Ops role and Security for incident investigation. Access is recorded with an immutable audit log (audit-entries stored in log-svc with retention 7 years).

Retention and Access Table
| Artifact | Location | Max Retention | Access Policy | Notes |
| ProbeFarm raw logs (with PII) | vaulted-store (ACM-backed) | 90 days | Annotation-Ops, Security (requires JIT approval) | used only for dispute resolution |
| Annotated dataset exports | eval-archives S3 (redacted) | 5 years | Engineering, Applied ML, Compliance | export scanned for PII before write |
| Annotator mapping table | KMS-protected vault | 30 days | Annotation-Ops (just-in-time) | rotated salt on 30-day cycle |

Integration and Tooling
- PII Detector: service name pii-detect-v2. Use model version v2025-12 with tuned thresholds: email/phone detection at 0.95 precision, names at 0.9 precision for redaction purpose. False positive handling: annotate redact spans plus keep canonical evidence for QA in the raw vault only.
- CLI Example: redaction check before export

  scan_action: block-on-detect

Annotation Workflow Changes (numbered)
1) Submission: probe -> ProbeFarm -> Anonymizer module (redact-on-write).
2) Work assignment: annotator receives task with annotator_handle visible; no name/email present.
3) Free-text comments: annotator UI provides auto-suggest redaction and warns against entering PII.
4) Completed annotations: saved to evaluation datastore with redaction markers.
5) QA and adjudication: adjudicators access redacted records. If identity is required for remediation, use the private accessor flow (JIT approval).

Owner and Roles
- Annotation-Ops (owner): implements and maintains the redaction runtime and the mapping vault. Service owner: Annotation-Ops team (pager: #annotation-ops).
- Applied ML (consumer): uses redacted exports for evals and reports regressions.
- Security & Compliance: periodic audits, approves JIT access.
- Vendor-Integrations: vendors must implement matching redaction transforms before sending back datasets; vendors without capability are blocked.

Rollout Plan and Validation
- Canary (Week 0–1): enable redaction-on-write for 5% of

- Pilot (Week 2–4): expand to 25% with escrowed raw logs in vault; run monthly compliance test: attempt export and verify block behaviour.
- Full rollout (Week 5–8): 100% redaction-on-write; rotate salt; decommission any caches that expose PII.

Success Metrics (targets)
- Export-block incidents due to PII: 0 after pilot.
- Annotation throughput delta due to UI redaction suggestions: <= 3% regression.
- QA disagreement rate between redacted and raw adjudication: <= 1.5% increase.
- JIT mapping lookups: all require approval and produce audit record; mean time to approve < 4 hours.

Monitoring and Alerting
- Alert if redaction scanner finds a direct identifier in exported dataset (severity: P1).
- Telemetry: track percent of annotations containing redaction tags, per-model and per-prompt slice. Unexpected spikes (>=5x baseline) trigger investigation.
- Daily compliance report: counts of mapping lookups, number of blocked exports, list of probes affected.

Testing and E2E Validation
- Unit tests: redaction ruleset must include positive/negative tests for 200 synthetic examples per PII class.
- Integration tests: nightly job that generates synthetic probes with seeded PII and verifies the pipeline redacts and blocks exports.
- Shadow run: run redaction module in shadow for private deployments and compare outputs to host redaction behaviour; metric: deterministic handle equality.

Synthetic Priming Sampling & Cost Framework

Overview:
This document defines the Synthetic Priming Sampling & Cost Framework: a structured protocol and accounting model for generating, validating, and sampling synthetic priming probes used across evaluation, regression triage, and quantization validation. Its goal is to balance detection efficacy with controlled operational cost while ensuring probes are representative of production prompt families.

Scope and motivation:
- Scope: applies to all synthetic probe generation and budgeted sampling used by the eval harness, offline probe harvesters, and shadow validation jobs for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Motivation: ad-hoc synthetic probes increased coverage but unpredictably inflated eval spend and caused noisy alerts. We need a reproducible sampling contract that:
  - Quantifies probe economic cost,
  - Enforces sampling fairness across prompt families and locales,
  - Provides gating thresholds before promotion or rollback decisions.

Definitions:
- Priming probe: a synthetic input (seed + priming tokens) designed to exercise a specific behavior slice (e.g., long-context coherence, numeric fidelity, functioncall stability).
- Probe family: grouping of probes by intent and template (e.g., "invoice-extraction-priming-v1").
- Probe unit cost: runtime cost to execute one probe against a model variant, calculated as tokens * model_unit_token_price + evaluation_overhead.
- Efficacy: weighted detection score combining recall_on_failing_slices and false_positive_penalty.

Key principles:
1) Cost-first sampling budget: every synthetic probe family must declare a monthly budget in token-equivalents before being registered in probe-store.
2) Fairness and stratification: sampling quotas are allocated by prioritized slice weight and regional/localization weight.
3) Deterministic seeding: synthetic generators must produce provably reproducible probes when given a seed and version tag.
4) Safety gating: before a probe family results in automatic rollout decisions, it must meet minimum efficacy and stability windows (see thresholds).

Registering a probe family (high level):
1. Create a probe-family manifest in probe-store with fields: name, description, intent, priming-template, seed-range, locality-tags, max_monthly_tokens.
2. Run the local validator (dev-run) to compute initial efficacy and cost estimate.
3. Submit for review: reviewers sign off on sampling budget and regional distribution.

Example probe-family manifest (YAML):

name: invoice-extraction-priming-v1
description: synthetic invoices with varying table layouts to stress tabular extraction and alignment when using primed contexts
intent: structured-extraction
priming_template: "You are a financial parser. Given the following invoice, extract line items as JSON: {{invoice_text}}"
seed_range: [1000,1999]
locality_tags: [en-US, en-GB]
max_monthly_tokens: 1_200_000

(Dev note: the above manifest is stored in probe-store under /manifests and versioned; the probe-store service is 'probe-store-v2' and indexed by name + semantic version.)

Sampling allocation algorithm (summary):
- Inputs: probe_families F, global_budget B (token-equivalents), slice_priorities P, regional_weights R.
- Steps:
  1) Compute family_weight = priority_score(F) * historical_failure_exposure(F).
  2) Tentative_alloc = (family_weight / sum_weights) * B.
  3) Apply floor (min_alloc) to ensure coverage for low-volume families (default floor=5000 tokens/month).
  4) Split tentative_alloc across regions

  4) Split tentative_alloc across regions by R.
  5) Convert tokens to job_count based on expected tokens_per_job for the family.
- Outcome: deterministic allocation for the month; allocations propagated to eval-orch scheduler.

Cost accounting and unit pricing (example):
- model_unit_token_price: 0.000004 USD/token (example for rdx-small-1)
- evaluator_overhead: 0.0025 USD/job (CPU + I/O)
- tokens_per_probe: 120 (average)
- probe_unit_cost = tokens_per_probe * model_price + evaluator_overhead = 120*0.000004 + 0.0025 = 0.00298 USD/probe
- Monthly spend = probe_unit_cost * expected_job_count.
- Billing integration: allocations are charged to the 'eval-budget' org account via the billing-bridge service.

Efficacy metrics and gates:
- Primary metrics: detection_recall (per-slice), false_positive_rate (per-family), stability_variance (rolling 7-day var of detection score).
- Minimum gates before automated actions (defaults):
  - detection_recall >= 0.72 (overhold: tests run across at least 3 seeds),
  - false_positive_rate <= 0.08,
  - stability_variance <= 0.06.
- If any gate fails, the family is flagged and placed in a manual-review queue; no automated rollback or canary will be triggered from that probe family.

Validation workflow (step-by-step):
1) Local dry-run (developer): run 'probectl validate --manifest invoice-extraction-priming-v1.yaml --seeds 5' against eval-sim to obtain preliminary metrics.
2) Shadow batch: schedule a shadow job in eval-orch with allocation=10% of family allocation and model=canary to measure real-world noise.
3) Stability window: collect metrics for 72 hours (or 24 hours for small allocations).
4) Evaluate gates and produce a validation report (JSON): includes per-region recall, FPR, sample transcripts, and a cost summary.
5) If gates pass, mark manifest 'approved' and schedule regular sampling; if not, iterate on template or reduce budget.

  "fpr": "0.04",
  "expected_monthly_cost_usd": "356.40"
}

(Reports are persisted in 'eval-reports' S3 bucket with encryption and linked in probe-store.)

- probe-store-v2: manifests, versioning, provenance. Owner: applied-ml team.
- eval-orch: scheduler that converts allocations into batch jobs and shadow loads. Owner: eval-infra.
- evaluator-sidecar: per-model adapter that computes scoring and returns telemetry. Owner: runtime team.
- billing-bridge: maps allocations to accounting centers. Owner: finance-tools.

Alerts, dashboards, and observability:
- Dashboards: 'Probe Economy' in Redwood Console showing budget burn rate, cost per family, expected vs actual spend.
- Alerts: PagerDuty only for: budget_exceed (threshold=120% of allocated tokens/month) and efficacy_regression (delta_recall_drop > 0.15 vs previous window).
- Traces: evaluator-sidecar emits span 'probe.execution' with tags family, seed, model_variant.

Few-shot Template Library and Localization Strategy

Summary:
This page describes a searchable, versioned Few-shot Template Library and the strategy for localizing templates across languages, regions, and product slices. It provides taxonomy, template examples, evaluation signals, and an operational rollout checklist for integrating new templates into our eval harness and production shadowing flows.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: few-shot prompting templates used by serving, shadow evals, and runbook-driven sanity checks (single-turn and multi-turn).
- Goals:
  1) Standardize template structure so probes are comparable across models and quantization profiles.
  2) Provide an explicit localization workflow (translation, culturalization, tokenization QA).
  3) Define acceptance criteria and telemetry to detect template-induced regressions.

Who should use this page:
- Applied ML engineers creating probe suites or prompt templates.
- Onboarding engineers promoting templates into the production probe catalog.
- Product teams requesting localized coverage for customer-facing features.

Taxonomy (table):
| Template family | Typical use case | Context tokens | Example length | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Instruction-based | Single request instruction (QA, rewrite) | short (<=128) | 1–3 shots | prompt-steering team |
| Multi-turn persona | Conversational flows with memory | medium (128–1024) | 3–8 turns | chat-evals |
| Example-based QA | Structured inputs -> structured output | medium | 1–5 examples | extraction-team |
| System-primed chain | Chained reasoning, tool calls | long (>1024) | 1–2 chains | reasoning-research |

Template structure standard (required fields):
- id: unique slug (prompt-family-language-version)
- family: taxonomy label
- description: 1–2 sentence intent
- shots: list of example pairs (user -> assistant)
- metadata: labels, token_estimate, expected_output_schema, stability_tags

Example template (JSON snippet) - store in library as a single-line escaped JSON in the DB.
```json
{
  "id": "instruction-qa-en-v1",
  "family": "instruction-based",
  "description": "Compact few-shot template for single-turn factual QA with a short context.",
  "shots": [
    {"input":"Who wrote 'The Tempest'?","output":"William Shakespeare."},
    {"input":"What is the capital of Japan?","output":"Tokyo."}
  ],
  "hints": "Prefer succinct answers, avoid adding new facts.",
  "token_estimate": "~35",
  "language": "en"
}
```

Localization strategy (high-level):
1) Prioritize languages and regions by customer usage (top 10 by monthly active users) and by legal/regulatory requirements.
2) For each template: translate shots and system hints using a bilingual team that includes a native reviewer and an applied ML reviewer.
3) Run tokenization parity checks: compare token counts between source and localized templates; reject localizations where token_inflation > 2x unless proven necessary.
4) Culturalization pass: replace locale-specific examples (dates, currencies, idioms) to preserve task semantics.
5) Create a localized test harness run (mini-eval) with 200 seeded probes per family/language before including in continuous evals.

Translation and QA checklist (numbered):
1. Machine translate using approved translation model (internal or trusted third-party).
2. Human first-pass review (bilingual linguist or native speaker).
3. Applied ML verification: check that tokenization, entity preservation (names, acronyms), and schema markers survived translation.
4. Run the mini-eval and inspect top-10 failure modes.
5. Tag template as 'localized-ready' or 'needs-rewrite' in metadata.

Tokenization and quantization considerations:
- Quant-sensitive families: chain-of-thought, long-context priming. For these, add a token budget field and a quant-sensitivity tag.
- When deploying quantized model variants (int8/4/QLoRA profiles), run the localized template through the quantized replay orchestrator and compare answer-identity and confidence distribution against FP16 baseline.
- Acceptance thresholds for quant-regression per-template: Exact-answer rate >= 95% of FP16 baseline OR semantic-similarity >= 0.90 (embedding cosine) for non-exact tasks.

Evaluation signals and monitoring (what to collect):
- Per-probe: latency, token_count_in, token_count_out, model_variant, deterministic_seed, response_embedding (for similarity checks), pass/fail (per-template rule), error_type.
- Aggregate metrics to track daily:
  - Template-level exact-match rate
  - Semantic-stability score (median embedding cosine vs baseline)
  - Token inflation (localized_vs_source)
  - Failure-mode distribution (hallucination, truncation, format-violation)

Acceptance criteria for promoting templates into the long-running probe set:
- Mini-eval: >= 90% pass rate across prioritized slices for the target language.
- Tokenization: localized token inflation <= 1.5x OR approved exception.
- Stability: semantic-stability >= 0.92 on shadow runs across 3 models (hosted, dedicated, private) OR a documented mitigation plan.
- Ownership assigned and runbook attached.

Operational rollout checklist (for template owners):
1) Create template in library and attach metadata, owner, tags.
2) Mark as draft and request localization if applicable.
3) Run mini-eval (200 probes) using the eval-harness micro-canary scheduler; attach results.
4) Address failures and update template shots or hints.
5) Request 'shadow' inclusion: add to shadow-replay list for 48–72 hours with traffic mirroring at 0.5–2% depending on risk level.
6) Review telemetry: if regressions appear, follow the regression triage playbook and consider rollback.
7) When stable, change status to 'active-probe' and include in daily continuous scans.

Failure triage quick-start (if template causes regression):
1. Reproduce locally: run the failing probe against baseline and target variants with deterministic seeds.
2. Check quantization tag: rerun in FP16; if regressed only under quant, escalate to quant-profiles team.
3. Inspect tokenization diffs and entity mismatch table.
4. Run subset bisect: remove each shot in turn to detect sensitivity to specific examples.
5. Create a regression ticket and tag with template ID, model_variant, and sample probe IDs.

- Localization owners: manage translations and culturalization (product-localization team).
- Evaluations owner: schedules and reviews mini-eval and shadow results (eval-harness team).

Context Fidelity Catalog and Seed Procedure

Summary
=======
This document defines a curated catalog of "context-fidelity" prompt cohorts and a repeatable, automated procedure for generating and versioning seed probes used by the eval harness, model onboarding, and regression triage teams. The goal is to produce seeds that exercise contextual sensitivity, priming behavior, and token-budget tradeoffs while ensuring reproducible measurement of fidelity-related regressions across model variants and quantization profiles.

Scope
-----
Applies to: prompt authors, evaluator engineers, model-onboarding owners, and quality-guardrails automation.
Excluded: ad-hoc user support prompts (those belong in product-driven prompt registries).

Definitions
-----------
- Context fidelity: the degree to which a model maintains instruction intent and response quality when context (priming, examples, history) changes.
- Seed: a single prompt instance (with metadata) used repeatedly across evals.
- Cohort: a named group of seeds that share a testing objective (e.g., "slot-anchored-multi-turn").
- Anchor prompt: a canonical prompt used as the base for synthetic augmentation and paraphrase generation.

Catalog: Cohorts and Targets
---------------------------
Below is the canonical catalog we maintain in the eval registry. Use this table to select the appropriate cohort for an onboarding campaign or regression sweep.

| Cohort ID | Purpose | Context Pattern | Fidelity target (RSI) | Token budget | Typical telemetry tags | Example anchor |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| CF-ANCH-MT | Multi-turn anchor sensitivity | 3-turn history + instruction | >= 0.92 | 256 | multi_turn, kv_cache_sensitive | "Plan a 3-step onboarding flow for a new user" |
| CF-PRIM-SHORT | Priming robustness (short) | 1-shot priming + single query | >= 0.95 | 64 | priming, short_ctx | "As an expert, summarize the paragraph:" |
| CF-PRIM-LONG | Priming robustness (long) | 5-shot priming + long context | >= 0.90 | 1024 | priming, long_ctx, cache_heavy | "You are a legal assistant. Provide key points:" |
| CF-SLOT-ANCH | Slot filling with distractors | template with 4 slots + noise | >= 0.91 | 192 | slot_filling, adversarial_noise | "Extract name, role, start_date, region from text:" |
| CF-FEWCLUSTER | Few-shot variability | 8-shot variable examples | >= 0.89 | 768 | fewshot, diversity | "Translate these examples and infer style:" |
| CF-STREAM-SEQ | Streaming/continuation fidelity | streaming tokens, functioncall-boundary | >= 0.93 | 512 | streaming, functioncall | "Continue the story preserving character voice:" |

Selection guidance
-------------------
- For latency-sensitive model families prefer CF-PRIM-SHORT or CF-ANCH-MT with reduced token budgets.
- For quantization regression analysis target CF-PRIM-LONG and CF-SLOT-ANCH to detect loss of long-context coherence and slot hallucination.
- Use CF-STREAM-SEQ for functioncall and streaming tail regressions.

Seed Generation Procedure (automated pipeline)
---------------------------------------------
1. Choose cohort (see Catalog) and select n_anchor anchors (default n_anchor=12).
2. For each anchor generate augmentations: paraphrase (2x), adversarial-noise insertion (1x), contextual-reorder (1x), synthetic-user-variant (3x).
3. Apply constraint filters: token budget (truncate or expand examples), anonymize PII, and ensure language-localization variants if cohort requires (en, es, fr).
4. Run classifier-based sensitivity checks: pass each augmented seed through the "prompt-sanity" classifier (threshold 0.6) to filter nonsensical augmentations.
5. Persist seeds to the eval registry with metadata: cohort_id, origin_anchor_id, augmentation_type, seed_version, creation_sha, and owner. See manifest YAML below.
6. Kick off small smoke eval against the shadow model (10 samples per seed) and compute RSI (Response Stability Index). If RSI < cohort target, flag for human review.
7. Approve seeds by reviewer group (applied-ml-evals) and promote seeds to "active" for continuous monitoring.

Automated QC checks and gating thresholds
----------------------------------------
- Response Stability Index (RSI): primary gate (computed as pairwise normalized similarity + instruction adherence score). Gate: pass if RSI >= cohort target.
- Embedding drift: mean cosine distance vs. anchor embedding must be <= 0.05 for paraphrase variants.
- Semantic F1 (slot cohorts): >= 0.88 for CF-SLOT-ANCH.
- Perplexity sanity: perplexity on baseline LMs must not exceed 3x median training perplexity for that cohort.
- Runtime checks: median latency on representative dedicated instance must be within 1.5x baseline for that cohort.

Onboarding checklist for model promotion using these seeds
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Register model with model-onboarding system and attach target cohorts (min: CF-ANCH-MT, CF-PRIM-LONG).
2. Run full seed sweep (all cohorts) in shadow for at least 10k aggregate requests.
3. Verify automated QC passes (RSI, embedding drift, semantic F1).
4. Run human spot-checks: sample 50 seeds across cohorts, annotate for instruction adherence and hallucination. Requirement: >= 95% pass on instruction adherence.
5. If any cohort fails, open a triage ticket (label: regression-cohort-<id>) and attach diagnostic artifact set (seed IDs, model run logs, kv-cache traces).
6. Post-approval: schedule weekly rolling checks for the first 2 weeks, then daily for the first month post-promotion.

Probe Curation Stewardship and Annotation Charter

Summary

Purpose: Define a repeatable, cross-team charter for curating, labeling, and stewarding probe sets (prompt probes and short synthetic interactions) that feed the eval-harness, regression triage tooling, and quantization-sensitivity suites. This document standardizes probe metadata, acceptance criteria, annotation contracts, and the rollout checklist for new probe bundles.

Scope
- Applies to probes intended for: production regression detection, quantization sensitivity, KV-cache stability tests, multi-turn coherence checks, and privacy/PII stress probes.
- Includes both synthetic probes (generated by internal seeders) and real-world-sampled probe candidates that enter the probe-store.
- Does not cover long-running offline benchmarks (>1M tokens) which are managed by the benchmarking-and-perf-suite team.

Definitions
- Probe: a single test request (prompt + optional context + expected behavioral signals) used by eval tooling.
- Probe Bundle: a versioned collection of probes with a manifest, metadata, and annotation state.
- Steward: owner responsible for the probe bundle lifecycle (curation, triage, retirement).

Roles and Responsibilities
1) Probe Steward (Primary): typically applied-ml engineer or product analyst. Responsibilities:
   - Define objectives and coverage matrix for the bundle (e.g., long-context coherence, entity hallucination).
   - Approve acceptance criteria and promotion readiness.
   - Own related JIRA/retro tickets and schedule canary evals.
2) Annotation Lead: manages labeler workforce and QA.
   - Produces annotation guide, trains annotators, runs adjudication.
3) Evaluator/CI Owner: integrates the bundle into eval-harness and sets runtime params.
4) Regression Oncall Contact: triages alerts generated by probes in production shadow pipelines.

Probe Manifest Schema (required fields)
- id: unique probe id (UUID)
- bundle_version: semver (e.g., 1.3.0)
- intent_tag: short string (e.g., refund-flow, multi-turn-summarize)
- slice_tags: list of strings (e.g., ["long_context", "numeric_answer"])
- sensitive_flag: yes|no|pii_masked
- expected_behaviors: list of behavior checks (e.g., ["correct_entity", "no-invented-dates"])
- ttl_days: integer (retirement after X days unless renewed)
- provenance: one of ["user-sampled", "synthetic-seeder", "partner-contrib"]
- annotation_state: draft|annotated|adjudicated|frozen
- annotation_version: semver
- steward: person/email
- created_at, last_updated (ISO dates)

Example JSON snippet (manifest):
{
  "id": "probe-8f4c2a6e",
  "bundle_version": "0.1.0",
  "intent_tag": "invoice-summary",
  "slice_tags": ["multistep", "financial"],
  "sensitive_flag": "pii_masked",
  "expected_behaviors": ["preserve-numeric-entities", "concise-summary"],
  "ttl_days": "365",
  "provenance": "user-sampled",
  "annotation_state": "annotated",
  "annotation_version": "1.0.0",
  "steward": "aisha.patel@redwood.ai",
  "created_at": "2025-11-14",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-03"
}

Acceptance Criteria and Quality Gates
- Coverage: every high-priority product intent (as defined in the coverage matrix) must have at least N=120 probes distributed across slices unless otherwise approved.
- Annotation quality: adjudicated inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff alpha or Cohen kappa) >= 0.80 for binary labels; >= 0.75 for multi-class.
- Stability probes: for each bundle, include 20% of probes marked as "stability" which exercise KV cache boundary conditions and quantized inference (see Quant Flagging below).
- Sensitivity tagging: probes that changed label under quantized runs or mixed-precision runs must be flagged with quant_susceptible=true.
- Regression detectability: historically validated bundles should map to

inference (see Quant Flagging below).
- Sensitivity tagging: probes that changed label under quantized runs or mixed-precision runs must be flagged with quant_susceptible=true.
- Regression detectability: historically validated bundles should map to at least 3 regression alert signatures when run against two different model variants.

Annotation Contract and Guide (short version)
1) Annotator tasks are atomic: each task contains a single probe and at most three micro-labels (correctness, hallucination, harmfulness).
2) Label definitions must include 3 canonical examples per label (positive/negative/edge-case).
3) Adjudication: any probe with >=25% disagreement moves to adjudication queue; adjudicator must provide a 1-3 sentence rationale.
4) Annotator throughput and QA: monthly spot-checks: 200 probes sampled per annotator; acceptable error rate <4%.

Probe Priority Scoring (curation heuristic)
- Score components (normalized 0-1): novelty(0.25), user-impact(0.35), regression-signal-history(0.2), coverage-gap(0.2).
- Priority = weighted sum; bundles with Priority >= 0.7 advance to canary eval stage.

Integration with Eval Harness and CI
- Bundle registration: use CLI `probectl register --manifest bundle.json` to publish to probe-store and tag for eval-harness.
- Canary policy: default canary runs: 3 seeds, two model variants (current-prod, candidate), runtime budget 1200 tokens per probe, sample 200 probes (top-priority subset).
- Runtime SLOs: smoke-eval < 2 hours, full-bundle-run < 24 hours (for bundles <5k probes). If runtime exceeds SLO by 25%, evaluator owner must be paged and a performance triage ticket opened.

Quantization and Hardware Sensitivity Flags
- Each probe must set quant_flag: one of [none, quant-8bit, quant-4bit] if it is intended for quant-sensitivity suites.
- For probes with quant_flag != none, Evaluator must run both FP16 and specified quant modes and produce a per-probe delta metric: response-change-score (0-1). Probes with delta >= 0.25 are `quant_susceptible` and must be included in follow-up diagnosis.

Regression Triage Fast-Path (procedure)
1) Alert fires from runtime monitoring: probe_failure_rate > threshold (default 5%) OR Response Stability Index delta > 0.05 over 1 day.
2) Triage steps (fast-path):
   a) Steward validates probe manifest and runs targeted shadow-run (single-variant replay) using `probectl replay --ids <list> --model current-prod`.
   b) If failure reproducible, annotate failure type (semantic drift, tokenization, quantization, runtime-eviction) and escalate to owner team.
   c) If not reproducible, expand scope to ensemble runs and collect traces (kv-cache logs, seed RNG, exact token stream).
3) Postmortem requirement: incidents with customer-visible impact must produce a 72-hour interim note and a 2-week formal RCA with mitigation plan.

Retention and Retirement Policy
- Active bundles: retain full annotation state and provenance for 540 days.
- Archive: after TTL expiration or steward retirement, move to cold-store (metadata retained) and mark public queryable but excluded from automated CI unless explicitly reactivated.

Metrics and Dashboards (concrete list)
- Probe health dashboard (prod): probe_failure_rate, mean_response_time, median_response_stability_index, quant_susceptible_count.
- Eval-harness job metrics: job_latency_p50/p95,

- Eval-harness job metrics: job_latency_p50/p95, tokens_consumed, and per-bundle success_rate.

Rollout Checklist for New Probe Bundle
1) Produce coverage matrix and steward assignment.

Latency and Token-Budgeted Prompt Design Guide

Summary:
This guide defines a repeatable design and validation workflow for authoring prompts when you have hard latency or token-budget constraints. It covers principled prompt composition, token accounting, cache-priming patterns, integration tests for the eval harness, and rollout checks for model promotion. The target reader is engineers and applied-ML owners preparing prompts for production endpoints (hosted, dedicated, or private).

Scope and objectives:
- Scope: customer-facing text- and chat-style prompts used in production inference paths (single-turn and multi-turn). Does not cover multimodal binary payload formats.
- Objectives:
  - Ensure prompts meet latency SLOs and token budgets for cost predictability.
  - Maximize reuse of KV/prefix caches and enable safe quantized deployments.
  - Provide testable templates and an automated validation checklist for onboarding.

Key definitions:
- Token budget: maximum average tokens per request (input + expected output) allocated to a route.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile latency target for generation portion of a request (example: 500 ms for 128-token responses on p4d).
- Priming slice: compact context intended to be cached (prefix) and not sent every request.

Principles for budgeted prompt design:
1) Make context scannable and compressible:
   - Prefer concise, semantically dense instructions (one short sentence per instruction).
   - Replace long enumerations with named anchors and include a short lookup when needed.
2) Partition mutable vs stable context:
   - Place stable facts, policy, or persona in a priming slice (cacheable).
   - Place request-specific data in the transient context (per-request tokens).
3) Budget first, optimize second:
   - Choose a hard token budget per route (example budgets below).
   - If quality drops, prefer targeted prompt edits and reranking over increasing budget.
4) Design for cache hits and graceful degradation:
   - Structure prompts so missing cache entries are safe: fallbacks should still be valid albeit more verbose.
5) Test under quantized kernels and batching:
   - Validate prompts with the quantization profile(s) that will be used in production.

Token budget examples (suggested starting points):
| Route class | Input budget (tokens) | Output budget (tokens) | Notes |
|-------------|----------------------:|-----------------------:|-------|
| Low-latency short response | 64 | 64 | Mobile search snippets, chat suggestions |
| Medium-latency assistant | 256 | 256 | Feature assistants with context and follow-ups |
| High-throughput embedding-driven | 128 | 64 | Embedding-based rerank + short answer |

Prompt composition templates (text):
- Compact instruction template (cacheable prefix):
  "SYSTEM: You are an assistant that answers concisely. STYLE: bullet-brief.
   FACTS: [stable facts — place in priming slice].
   --END PREFIX--
   USER: <customer prompt or example>"

- Split-prompt example for KV caching:
  1) Priming (cached): "Docs summary: <3-line abstract>. Safety: refuse hallucinations. Style: concise."

Token accounting rules (practical):
- Count tokens using the production tokenizer for the model family.
- Include: system + user + instruction + expected output budget. Exclude: wire/transport framing added by SDKs (we assert those are negligible but verify).
- Formula (string to implement in CI):
  expected_total = ceil(tokenize(prefix)) + ceil(max_input_tokens) + ceil(max_output_tokens) + safety_margin
  where safety_margin = max(16, ceil(0.05 * expected_total))

Service-level SLO guidance (example defaults):
- p95 generation latency: 500 ms for <= 128 output tokens on Dedicated p4d (single-request, no batching).
- Token budget compliance: <1% of requests exceed the configured budget in steady-state testing.
- Cache hit contribution: primed routes should target >= 60% cache-hit rate in steady traffic to justify the split.

Validation checklist (pre-promotion):
1) Tokenize all templates with production tokenizer and confirm expected_total <= route_budget for 99th pct of test inputs.
2) Run the sample prompt family through the quantized model artifacts (if using quant). Compare response-quality metrics (ROUGE/EM or task-specific thresholds) against baseline model.
3) Shadow-run the route for at least 24h (or 1M requests equivalent) with eval harness:
   - Verify p95 latency meets SLO under target batching levels.
   - Verify token-budget exceedance rate <1%.
   - Collect cache-hit telemetry.
4) Execute functional tests: safety-sentinels, hallucination probes, and continuity checks for multi-turn sequences.
5) Record rollout plan and rollback criteria in the release ticket.

- name: prompt-priming-budget-check
  type: shadow-scan
  routes: ["assistant-short", "assistant-medium"]
  samples: sampler.lookup("production-probe-anchored")
  checks:
    - name: token-budget-violation
      assert: percentile(tokens_total, 99) <= ${route.token_budget}
    - name: latency-p95
      assert: p95_generation_latency_ms <= ${route.p95_slo_ms}
    - name: quality-delta
      metric: fidelity_score
      assert: delta <= 0.03

Design patterns and anti-patterns:
- Pattern: "Prefix compression" — move stable long lists into a single-line compressed annotation with an index reference. This yields better cache behavior and smaller prefixes.
- Pattern: "Two-stage answering" — generate a compact plan in the first micro-call (<= 32 tokens) and expand in an allowed secondary call when more tokens are required; use only when latency SLOs permit.
- Anti-pattern: embedding a long dump of unrelated documentation in the per-request context — kills cacheability and unpredictably increases cost.

Annotation Reconciliation and Provenance Manifest

Overview

Purpose:
This document defines the standard process, tooling patterns, metrics and ownership for annotation reconciliation and provenance tracking used by Redwood Inference evaluation pipelines. It is intended for evaluator leads, data engineers, annotation vendors, and product owners that rely on labeled probe sets and human judgments for production quality gates.

Goals:
- Ensure label correctness, reproducibility and auditable lineage for any eval artifact that influences model promotion or rollback decisions.
- Minimize annotation drift and reduce labelling-induced regressions by defining concrete reconciliation steps, thresholds and rollback procedures.
- Provide a lightweight provenance schema that is compatible with our eval-harness ingestion and downstream dashboards.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: probe labeling tasks (classification, intent, slot, response-ranking), canonical ground-truth creation, and post-hoc adjudication for failed probes.
- Not covered: purely synthetic probe generation without human labels, low-risk exploratory annotations for research prototypes.

Ownership and roles

- Annotation Owner (AO): owns the labeling schema, sample packs, and the reconciliation plan. Typically the product or evaluation lead.
- Data Custodian (DC): owns storage of raw annotation artifacts, access control and retention. Typically Data Platform.
- Reconciliation Lead (RL): runs the triangulation workflow and signs-off final label sets.
- Audit Reviewer (AR): independent reviewer (cross-team) who spot-checks provenance and signs compliance for releases that affect customer SLOs.

Minimum metadata and provenance manifest

Every labeled dataset that enters the eval-harness must be accompanied by a flat provenance manifest (JSONL or CSV fields). The eval pipeline expects the following columns (table shown as text):

| field | description | required | example |
|---|---|---:|---|
| dataset_id | internal id used by eval-harness | yes | probe-pack-2026-02-14 |
| schema_version | label schema semantic version | yes | v1.2 |
| source_uri | S3 or GCS path to raw annotations | yes | s3://redwood-evals/probes/pack-2026/annotations.jsonl |
| created_by | annotator id or vendor tag | yes | vendorA_batch_42 |
| created_at | ISO timestamp | yes | 2026-02-10T15:03:00Z |
| reconciliation_run_id | reconciliation job id (if applicable) | conditional | recon-2026-02-12-07 |
| reconciled_by | person or automation that finalized labels | conditional | recon-bot OR Priya Khatri |
| reconciliation_notes | short rationale for changes | conditional | merged label conflicts: majority 3/5; kept gold anchors |
| audit_checks_passed | boolean string (true/false) | yes | true |
| retention_policy | storage TTL label | yes | 2y |

Note: The manifest must be stored alongside the dataset (same bucket/prefix) and registered in the eval-harness catalog via the dataset_id.

Reconciliation workflow (step-by-step)

1) Pre-flight (AO)
   - Freeze schema_version and publish labeling instructions. All changes require a patch note and version bump.
   - Generate anchor set (gold items) of 50–200

Reconciliation workflow (step-by-step)

1) Pre-flight (AO)
   - Freeze schema_version and publish labeling instructions. All changes require a patch note and version bump.
   - Generate anchor set (gold items) of 50–200 probes covering high-risk slices. Anchors carry a single-source-of-truth label created by Subject Matter Experts (SMEs).

2) Labeling (vendor or internal annotators)
   - Collect 3 independent labels per non-anchor probe by default (configurable by task complexity).
   - Emit raw annotations as JSONL with fields: probe_id, annotator_id, label, confidence, payload.

3) Automated conflict detection (DC)
   - Run a conflict detection job that computes inter-annotator agreement (IAA) per-slice and flags probes where majority agreement < 0.6 or where label entropy > threshold (default 0.8).
   - Produce conflicts CSV at s3://redwood-evals/{dataset_id}/conflicts.csv

4) Triaging conflicts (RL)
   - Resolve conflicts via the following ordered strategies until resolved:
     a) Majority rule if agreement >= 0.5 and no anchor disagreement.
     b) SME adjudication for anchors and high-severity slices (see severity mapping below).
     c) Pairwise adjudication: present annotator pair histories and ask RL to pick or suggest a new label (allow relabeling across categories).
     d) Consensus adjudication meeting for ambiguous probe families (calendar scheduled within 48 hours).

5) Finalization and provenance capture (RL + DC)
   - Produce reconciled JSONL with final_label, rationale_tag, reconciled_at, reconciled_by.
   - Update the provenance manifest (reconciliation_run_id and reconciliation_notes).
   - Push reconciled artifact to a guarded prefix (e.g., /reconciled/) and set read-only ACLs.

6) Audit and sign-off (AR)
   - AR must sample at least 5% of reconciled probes or 200 items (whichever is larger) across slices and verify: manifest correctness, frozen schema_version, anchor agreement intact.
   - AR signs off by updating 'audit_checks_passed' to true in manifest and adding a short audit log entry.

Severity mapping and when to require SME adjudication

- Severity: high/medium/low (example mapping)
  - High: probes that directly affect customer-facing decision logic or safety sentinels (anchor mismatch -> SME required).
  - Medium: slices with business impact but not immediate safety effect (default RL adjudication allowed).
  - Low: exploratory labels or internal-only slices (automated reconciliation acceptable).

Inter-annotator agreement (IAA) and thresholds

- Global acceptance criteria for production ground-truth:
  - Krippendorff's alpha >= 0.65 OR majority agreement >= 0.7 across core slices.
  - For high-severity slices, alpha >= 0.75 and anchors must remain unchanged.
- If thresholds are not met for any critical slice, labeling batch must be escalated to SME review and reannotation plan.

Quality gates and SLOs for annotation processes

- Turnaround SLAs:
  - Automated conflict detection: within 2 hours of raw ingestion.
  - Reconciliation initial triage: within 48 hours of conflict detection.
  - Full SME adjudication: within 5 business days for high-severity items.

- Quality SLOs (monthly rolling):
  - Anchors agreement retention: 99.5% remain unchanged unless schema_version bump.
  - Reconciliation precision: sample-verified precision >= 95% (AR sampling).
  - Dataset completeness: 100% manifest fields populated.

Versioning and schema evolution

- SemVer-style schema_version managed in the repo: schemas/label-schemas.yaml. Changes must include: change log, migration plan, sample migration script.
- Backwards compatibility rule: readers must be tolerant of older schema fields; conversions should be defined in data-platform transformations.

Retention and access controls

- Default retention: 2 years for reconciled artifacts, 90 days for raw transient annotations (unless flagged for legal retention).
- Access: Reconciled artifacts are read-only to non-DC teams. DC and AO have write privileges. Export for external vendors require signed NDA and temporary access tokens.

Integration with eval-harness and pipelines

- Registration: After reconciliation, AO must register the dataset_id in the eval-harness catalog using the CLI:

Failure modes and remediation

- Failure: Anchors drift after reconciliation. Remediation: freeze rollouts, notify model-ops and product, re-run anchor validation and if >2% anchor divergence, rollback promotions that used the dataset.
- Failure: IAA below threshold across many slices. Remediation: escalate to SME, possibly re-run labeling with expanded annotator training and updated instructions.

Operational runbook (short)

  3) DC marks dataset status as 'recon-in-progress' in catalog.

Semantic Anchoring and Response Synthesis Benchmark

Overview:

This document describes the Semantic Anchoring and Response Synthesis Benchmark (SARS-Bench), a targeted prompt-suite and evaluation protocol designed to measure model sensitivity to semantic anchors and to synthesize controlled, high-variance response references for stress testing. SARS-Bench is intended for integration into the eval-harness and for use by model-onboarding, quantization profiling, and regression triage workflows.

Goals:
- Quantify how model outputs change when semantically equivalent anchors (context markers) are inserted, relocated, or removed.
- Generate synthetic but plausible reference responses that exercise long-tail behavior without requiring large human labeling budgets.
- Provide clear thresholds and triage playbooks for when a change constitutes a regression in production quality.

Scope and applicability:
- Target models: causal and chat LLMs used by Redwood API and Redwood Dedicated (all sizes).
- Eval modes: offline eval-harness runs, shadow-to-prod mirroring, and synthetic field probes.
- Not intended to replace safety or hallucination audits; use in combination with existing safety sandbox and content filters.

Design principles:
1) Anchor-aware sampling: prompts are partitioned by where semantic anchors (phrases that alter context emphasis) appear.
2) Controlled response synthesis: use an ensemble of lightweight models to create high-diversity reference responses; filter using heuristics and a small human-in-the-loop pass.
3) Quant-aware evaluation: metrics are computed separately for float, mixed-precision, and quantized variants to isolate quantization-induced shifts.

Prompt suite composition (example):
- Base prompt (P0): a canonical user request without explicit anchors.
- Anchor insertion (P1): P0 + leading anchor token/phrase (e.g., "Note: focus on X").
- Anchor relocation (P2): P0 with anchor moved to the end or embedded in a subclause.
- Anchor removal (P3): P0 with implied context removed to create ambiguity.
- Stressor variants: paraphrase perturbations, noise injection (50% token-level swap probability), and context-length stretchers (append irrelevant paragraphs to 2x/4x tokens).

Dataset schema (text table):
| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| prompt_id | unique id | sars-2026-0001 |
| variant | one of [P0,P1,P2,P3,STRESS] | P1 |
| user_intent | coarse label (inform, summarize, classify, code) | summarize |
| anchor_text | literal anchor if present | "Important: prioritize accuracy" |
| metadata | comma-separated tags | long-context,paraphrase |
| synthetic_refs | pipe-separated synthetic reference ids | ref-01|ref-03 |

Synthesis pipeline (1–6):
1. Candidate generation: run 3 lightweight decoders (e.g., trimmed-200M ensembles) with temperature sweep [0.2,0.8] to produce 20 candidates per prompt variant.
2. Heuristic filtering: remove candidates with repeated token ratio > 0.35 or length outside ±30% of median.
3. Diversity selection: cluster by embedding distance (cosine) and select top-k per cluster (k=2).
4. Safety and policy filter: run safety classifier; drop flagged candidates and flag for human review.
5. Human quick-pass: label a 5% sample to

distance (cosine) and select top-k per cluster (k=2).
4. Safety and policy filter: run safety classifier; drop flagged candidates and flag for human review.
5. Human quick-pass: label a 5% sample to estimate noise; if > 7% of synthetic refs are incoherent, increase human sampling to 15%.
6. Canonicalization: normalize punctuation and white-space, convert numbers to canonical form.

Key metrics (computed per prompt variant and aggregated):
- Anchor Consistency (AC): fraction of synthetic_refs where core-entity extraction agrees across variants (range 0–1). Threshold: AC >= 0.92 for promotion.
- Response Divergence Index (RDI): mean pairwise embedding cosine distance between P0 refs and P1/P2 refs (higher = more sensitive). Regression trigger: RDI increase > 0.06 relative to baseline.
- Surface Drift (%) : token-level BLEU-style change normalized by length. Acceptable: < 3% delta.
- Coherence Drop (%): fraction of references flagged as incoherent by automatic coherence model. Action if > 2.5%.
- Quantization Sensitivity Delta (QSD): difference in AC or RDI when comparing float32 baseline to quantized run. Investigation if QSD > 0.04.

Example CLI integration with eval-harness:
- Submit a batch run (YAML payload):
  redwood-eval run --suite sars-bench-2026 --workdir /tmp/sars --batch-size 128 --model-id rwd-open-1-8b

- Pull results (JSON summary):
  redwood-eval summarize --run-id sars-2026-15 --metrics AC,RDI,QSD --output sars-2026-15-summary.json

Labeling contract for human review:
- Each sampled item must be labeled with: core_entity (short string), factuality {true|false|uncertain}, best_ref (index).
- Annotation SLA: initial pass within 72 hours; critical regressions require 24-hour expedited labeling.
- Inter-annotator agreement target: Cohen's kappa >= 0.75 on core_entity extraction.

Regression triage playbook (detection → ownership → rollback):
1. Detection: automated alerts in Redwood Console when AC < 0.90 or RDI changes exceed thresholds in production-shadow runs.
2. Fast replicate: re-run failing prompt_ids with identical seeds against baseline commit and current commit using the eval-harness "replay" mode.
3. Attribution: compare token-level edit traces and KV-cache utilization logs. If change correlates with quant profile, tag quantization and notify model-onboarding.
4. Immediate mitigation: route affected API route to fallback model family (configured in smart routing) and create incident.
5. Investigation: root-cause checklist — prompt drift, tokenizer change, model weights change, kernel selection/precision change, inference runtime bug.
6. Resolution & validation: once fix applied, run the full SARS-Bench + regression subset and close incident when metrics return within acceptance thresholds.

Quantization considerations and experiment guidance:
- Run SARS-Bench for each quant profile prior to promotion (int8, int4, mixed16).
- Use QSD to prioritize weight-clipping or recalibration experiments; record calibration seeds and the full quantization config.
- Recommended experiment matrix: model-size × quant-profile × seed (3 seeds) × prompt-partition (P0,P1,P2,P3,STRESS).

Acceptance criteria for model promotion (example):
- AC >= 0.92 on aggregated suite;
- RDI within ±0.06 of baseline;
- QSD

matrix: model-size × quant-profile × seed (3 seeds) × prompt-partition (P0,P1,P2,P3,STRESS).

Acceptance criteria for model promotion (example):
- AC >= 0.92 on aggregated suite;
- RDI within ±0.06 of baseline;
- QSD <= 0.04 for all quant profiles;
- Coherence Drop <= 2.5% and Surface Drift <= 3%.

Rollout checklist (canary → phased → global):
1. Canary: 0.5% traffic on Redwood Dedicated with full telemetry collection (tokens, latency, AC, RDI).
2. Phase 1: 5% traffic after 24h stable metrics.
3. Phase 2: 25% traffic with automated rollback watch for AC dips > 0.02.
4. Global: complete after 72h of stable telemetry.

Cross-Probe Contrastive Stability Suite and Labeling Contract

Overview
========

This document defines the Cross-Probe Contrastive Stability Suite (CPCSS): a standardized benchmark and labeling contract used to detect, triage, and quantify subtle fidelity regressions across probe families (priming, few-shot, function-calls, and long-context). CPCSS is intended for evaluators, model-onboarding engineers, and quality guardrails owners who manage shadow-to-canary promotions for mixed-precision and quantized artifacts.

Why this exists
----------------
- Many regressions are only visible when comparing closely related probes (e.g., two priming variants) rather than absolute thresholds.
- Contrastive, cohort-based checks surface small but systematic semantic shifts that break downstream heuristics.
- A labeling contract ensures consistent human annotations and enables automated signal fusion across telemetry, evaluator outputs, and user-facing metrics.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: probe families used in production prompt sets, evaluator-driven shadow traffic, and canary promotion workflows.
- Audience: evaluator team, model-onboarding, applied-ML SREs, product owners of ML-features.

Key definitions
---------------
- Probe: an input variant used to exercise a narrow slice of model behavior (e.g., few-shot prompt for entity extraction).
- Anchor probe: canonical reference input for a slice.
- Contrast pair: (anchor, variant) used to compute a directional delta.
- Stability delta: aggregated metric representing deviation (semantic + token-level) between anchor and variant.

Suite components (high level)
----------------------------
1) Probe catalog: canonicalized probe families, priming lexicon, and minimal postprocessing rules.
2) Contrast scoring: multi-signal score combining semantic similarity, function-call parity, and tokenization drift.
3) Labeling contract: human review guidelines, annotation matrix, and adjudication rules.
4) Triaging playbook: priority matrix, automated bisect suggestions, and rollback gates.

Probe catalog requirements (table)
----------------------------------
| field | example | requirement |
|---|---|---|
| probe_id | priming-weather-v1 | short, unique, hyphenated |
| family | priming | one of: priming, fewshot, functioncall, longcontext |
| seed_inputs | 250 | minimum 200 inputs per probe for statistical power |
| anchor_policy | most-recent-stable | anchors must be pinned to a model version and stored in the probe registry |
| max_context_tokens | 4096 | documented per-probe |

Contrast scoring algorithm (conceptual)
----------------------------------------
- Compute three signals for each (anchor, variant) pair:
  1. Semantic alignment (SA): embedding cosine of normalized outputs (use embedding service: redwood-emb-v1).
  2. Function-call parity (FCP): boolean + weighted token difference for functioncall probes.
  3. Token drift (TD): BPE token divergence normalized by reference length.
- Combined stability delta (SD) = 0.6*SA_delta + 0.3*FCP_penalty + 0.1*TD_score (tunable per-family).
- Thresholding: SD > 0.12 triggers automated triage; SD in [0.08,0.12] creates a medium-priority alert.

Concrete example (command snippets)
----------------------------------
1) Run a local contrast job against shadow cohort:

$ rwd-eval run contrast --probe priming-weather-v1 --anchor-version v2025-11-02 --variant-version staging-quant-v3 --sample 1000 --out results/priming-weather-contrast.json

2) Compute embedding SA (example Python):

from redwood_sdk

----------------------------------
1) Run a local contrast job against shadow cohort:

$ rwd-eval run contrast --probe priming-weather-v1 --anchor-version v2025-11-02 --variant-version staging-quant-v3 --sample 1000 --out results/priming-weather-contrast.json

2) Compute embedding SA (example Python):

from redwood_sdk import EmbeddingsClient
emb = EmbeddingsClient(model='redwood-emb-v1')
anchor_vecs = emb.embed_batch(anchor_texts)
variant_vecs = emb.embed_batch(variant_texts)
# cosine per pair -> SA_delta = 1 - mean(cosine(anchor,variant))

Labeling contract (human annotation)
------------------------------------
Purpose: produce consistent human labels for contrast cases where automated signals are ambiguous.

1) Triage classes (single-label per example):
   - NO_REGRESSION: outputs are functionally equivalent for the use-case.
   - MINOR_QUALITY_CHANGE: cosmetic or brevity-related differences not affecting downstream decisions.
   - FUNCTIONAL_REGRESSION: meaningful change that alters correctness or safety.
   - BEHAVIORAL_DRIFT: change in tone/persona or contextual hallucination risk.

2) Annotation guidelines (bullet form):
   - Annotators must read both outputs in context and assume the downstream consumer is a "structured ingestor" (e.g., extraction pipeline).
   - If function-call probes differ in arguments or call/no-call, label FUNCTIONAL_REGRESSION.
   - For multi-turn longcontext probes, check memory consistency for the last 3 turns.

3) Adjudication flow: 3-annotator consensus with majority label; if all three disagree, route to SME for adjudication and add to gold set.

--------------------------
| probe_id | input_id | anchor_output | variant_output | label | annotator | notes |

Quality gates and rollout integration
-------------------------------------
- Canary promotion block: any probe family with SD > 0.12 and label ratio (FUNCTIONAL_REGRESSION) > 1% for samples >= 500 blocks rollout.
- Auto-fallback: if rollout proceeds and live telemetry (user-error-rate) increases by 20% vs baseline within first 6 hours, trigger automatic fallback to previous model.
- Canary sampling: 0.5% live traffic min, stratified across tenant cohorts for at least 24 hours before scale-up.

Monitoring and SLOs
-------------------
- Probe stability SLO: 99.5% of contrast pairs must have SD <= 0.08 in promotion windows.
- Annotation latency SLO: 90% of queued contrast samples labeled within 48 hours for priority alerts.
- Telemetry drift SLO: deploys must show <15% relative increase in user-facing error signals (extraction failures, function-call mis-invocations) for 72-hour evaluation window.

Automated triage playbook (numbered steps)
------------------------------------------
1. Run contrast job against staged model with the full probe catalog (CI hook).
2. If any family reports SD > 0.12, auto-open a regression ticket in JIRA with priority P1-P2 depending on impact.
3. Attach 500 randomly sampled contrast pairs to the ticket and kick off labeling (auto-assign rounds).
4. If labeled FUNCTIONAL_REGRESSION ratio > 1% -> block canary and assign to model-onboarding owner.
5. If labeled MINOR_QUALITY_CHANGE -> schedule follow-up evaluation with increased sample size and localized prompt rewrite experiment.
6. Once triage completes, produce a regression summary

Annotation steward rotation and drift amortization playbook

Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable program for rotating annotation stewards, amortizing label drift remediation costs, and keeping probe/annotation inventories healthy across tenant cohorts. It combines human steward scheduling, automated drift detection, and sample-based reannotation to reduce cost while maintaining slice-level fidelity guarantees.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-detect and cost-to-repair annotation drift while ensuring service-level quality on critical slices (latency-sensitive, safety, and top-10 tenant slices).
- Scope: Applies to all production probes, human-labeled datasets, and stewarded annotation pools used by the Eval Harness, Prompt Catalog, and Onboarding pipelines. Excludes ephemeral synthetic probes created for single-shot diagnostics.

Principles:
1) Small, frequent steward rotations beat large, infrequent edits — maintains institutional knowledge while reducing bias accumulation.
2) Drift repairs are funded and prioritized by slice impact, not raw volume.
3) Prefer stratified sampling + targeted reannotation over full re-labeling when measurable quality recovery is achievable.
4) All remediation actions must be traceable and reversible; annotate changes with provenance metadata.

Definitions:
- Steward: a trained annotator (internal or contractor) assigned to own a set of slices / tenants for a rotation window.
- Steward rotation: scheduled handoff of ownership, knowledge transfer artifacts, and annotation backlog.
- Amortization: spreading the cost of reannotation across time and tenant cohorts using sampling and prioritization policies.
- Drift event: any alert where slice-level eval metrics (Fidelity Delta, Coherence Score, Anchor Loss) exceed configured thresholds.

Ownership and roles:
- Steward Lead (Applied ML): primary owner of scheduling, training, and steward health.
- Eval Owner (Service team): specifies slice SLA and approves reannotation budget for their service.
- Platform Ops: runs drift detection jobs and provides tooling for reruns and annotation assignments.
- Data Compliance: reviews high-sensitivity slice changes before remediation.

Steward rotation schedule and onboarding checklist:
1) Rotation cadence: 8-week windows for core stewards; 4-week windows for high-throughput slices.
2) Handoff items (to be included in rotation ticket):
   - Current slice inventory CSV (slice-id, priority, last-labeled, steward, failure-mode tags)
   - Known heuristics/labeling guidance docs (versioned)
   - Outstanding correction backlog and rationale
   - Recent drift incidents and mitigation history (links to triage notes)
3) Training checkpoint (first 3 days after takeover):
   - 8-hour shadowing with outgoing steward and evaluator team
   - 100 sample audit with kappa >= 0.75 against prior steward
   - Sign-off by Steward Lead recorded in ticket

Drift detection and alerting:
- Automated signals (run hourly, default):
  - Fidelity Delta (FD): 7-day rolling window increase > 6% triggers P1 candidate
  - Anchor Loss (AL): absolute anchor mismatch increase > 0.03 triggers P2 candidate
  - Coherence Drop (CD): decrease in coherence score > 0.08 triggers P2 candidate
- Composite rule: FD > 4% AND (AL > 0.02

absolute anchor mismatch increase > 0.03 triggers P2 candidate
  - Coherence Drop (CD): decrease in coherence score > 0.08 triggers P2 candidate
- Composite rule: FD > 4% AND (AL > 0.02 OR CD > 0.04) => immediate steward assignment and start of amortization workflow.
- Alert destinations: steward on-call Slack channel, eval-owner pager if P1, and incident log in Opsboard.

Prioritization and amortization algorithm (high level):
1) Rank impacted slices by impact_score = (tenant_traffic_weight * fidelity_delta) + (sla_weight * slice_priority) - (annotation_age_factor).
2) Assign budget band: High (auto reannotation up to 5k samples), Medium (sample & validate 500–2k), Low (monitor + periodic sampling).
3) Choose repair mode: sample-relabel -> targeted augmentation -> synthetic expansion -> full relabel. Prefer the lowest-cost mode that historically achieves >=90% recovery for that slice class.

Sample-based reannotation protocol (step-by-step):
1) Pull stratified sample: 500 samples stratified by tenant and prompt-family.
2) Run double-blind annotation (two stewards); compute inter-annotator agreement (IAA).
3) If IAA >= 0.7 and fidelity improvement simulated >= target, schedule staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
4) If IAA < 0.7, escalate to expert adjudication and consider annotator retraining.

Cost allocation and billing tags:
- Each remediation job must attach the following billing tags: project_id, service_owner, slice_id, steward_rotation_id, cost_center.
- Cost is amortized across tenants by tenant_traffic_weight with a minimum 10% shared platform subsidy for safety-critical slices.
- Monthly cost report columns: steward_id, hours, samples_relabelled, infra_time_hours, total_cost_usd, allocation_split.

Quality gates and SLAs:
- Slicing SLAs (examples):
  - Top-10 tenant slices: Fidelity delta must be <3% over 30 days or remediation must complete within 7 days.
  - Safety slices: Any measurable semantic regression must be remediated within 48 hours with rollback plan.
  - Low-risk slices: Monitor; remediation within 30 days.
- Promotion gate for repaired slices: after staged rollout, run a 7-day shadow evaluation comparing pre/post labels. Passing criteria: net fidelity delta <1%, no increase in false positive safety flags.

Automated tooling and jobs (examples):
- drift-detector --slice-regex "^safety.*" --window 7d --thresholds fd:0.06,al:0.03,cd:0.08
- steward-assign --slice-id S-12345 --rotation 8w --handoff-ticket 5678
- sample-diff-analysis --before-labels s3://probes/before.csv --after-labels s3://probes/after.csv --metrics fidelity,coherence,anchor

Example YAML config for a slice (to be stored in repo: /datasets/slices/configs):
---
slice_id: S-12345
priority: high
steward_rotation_weeks: 8
fidelity_thresholds:
  fidelity_delta: 0.03
  anchor_loss: 0.02
  coherence_drop: 0.05
repair_budget_usd_month: 1500
billing_tags:
  project_id: eval-harness
  service_owner: payments-team
---

Escalation and rollback steps (operational runbook):
1) If a P1 drift alert triggers, steward creates triage ticket and notifies Eval Owner.
2) Run the stratified 500-sample pull and perform immediate spot-checks (1 hour).
3) If regression confirmed and safety risk assessed > medium: pause any rollout using affected labels, open emergency remediation ticket, and notify Data Compliance.
4) Execute a staged remediation: 10% -> validate 72h ->

regression confirmed and safety risk assessed > medium: pause any rollout using affected labels, open emergency remediation ticket, and notify Data Compliance.
4) Execute a staged remediation: 10% -> validate 72h -> 50% -> validate 7d -> 100%. If at any gate metrics worsen, rollback to prior label snapshot (s3://probes/snapshots/<timestamp>).

Operational metrics dashboard (KPIs):
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for drift events (target <= 12 hours)
- Mean time to remediate (MTTR) by slice priority (top-10 target <= 7 days)
- Annotation disagreement rate after steward rotation (target kappa >= 0.75)
- Cost per mitigated 1% fidelity delta (track trend monthly)

Reporting cadence and governance:
- Weekly steward sync (30 minutes): incoming handoffs, active drift items, backlog.
- Monthly cost & outcomes review with Product & Finance: present allocation reports and proposed budget adjustments.
- Quarterly audit: Data Compliance reviews a stratified set of label changes and steward decisions.

Few‑shot Memory Footprint Benchmark and Priming Budget Spec

Overview

Purpose: This document defines the Few‑shot Memory Footprint Benchmark (FMFB) and the associated Priming Budget Spec. FMFB measures how adding few‑shot examples (priming) affects memory usage, KV cache pressure, batching efficiency, latency SLOs, and generation quality across representative models and hosting modes (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to produce actionable priming budgets and runtime guardrails that minimize operational cost and regression risk.

Scope
- Applies to text-only autoregressive and chat models used in production (decoder‑only LLMs and chat variants).
- Evaluates both default full‑context priming and compact priming (fewshot compressed templates).
- Runs across three representative hardware classes: GPU-large (A100 40GB), GPU-mid (H100 80GB), and edge/accelerator class (L4/NVIDIA T4 class).
- Integrates quantized and full‑precision model artifacts; measures changes per quant profile.

Goals and Acceptance Criteria
- Derive a per-model priming budget expressed as: max_examples, max_tokens_from_examples, and recommended_template (string).
- For any model+deployment tier, priming must not increase median p95 latency by > 15% or p99 latency by > 25% versus a no‑priming baseline under the target QPS.
- KV cache memory delta from priming should be bounded so that cache eviction rate stays < 5% in steady state for dedicated and private deployments.
- Batch utilization must not drop by > 10 percentage points due to priming-induced sequence length variance.
- Quality: Minimal acceptable change in automated coherence score (see Metrics) is delta >= -0.03 absolute (calibrated per task).

Benchmark design
1) Workload selection - Choose three workload archetypes: instruction completion, multi‑turn chat, and structured data extraction. For each archetype, select 6 canonical prompts representing head/mid/tail frequency.
- For each prompt, create three few‑shot templates: long (6 examples), medium (3 examples), short (1 example). Examples span token lengths 30–220 tokens.
2) Model matrix - Evaluate against the following model variants where available: base fp16, q4_K, q5_0, and int8 (if supported).
- Run on both streaming and non‑streaming generation modes.
3) Load profile - Two traffic profiles per workload: steady (50 RPS) and bursty (peak 400 RPS with 5s bursts). Scale test to saturate target SLOs for each deployment tier.
4) Measurement probes - Capture tokenized lengths, KV cache allocation snapshots, scheduler queue lengths, batch sizes, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput, and generation quality metrics (see metrics).

Metrics (definitions and collection)
- Priming memory delta: peak resident memory attributable to prompt tokens + per‑example KV allocations (bytes). Collected via runtime allocator sampling and process RSS differencing.
- Cache eviction rate: percent of requests experiencing an eviction event within a 1h window.
- Batch utilization: ratio of effective tokens processed per batch to theoretical max for hardware.
- Latency: end‑to‑end request latency excluding client network (p50/p95/p99).
- Quality metrics: task‑specific

within a 1h window.
- Batch utilization: ratio of effective tokens processed per batch to theoretical max for hardware.
- Latency: end‑to‑end request latency excluding client network (p50/p95/p99).
- Quality metrics: task‑specific automatic metrics (BLEU/F1 for extraction, coherence score for open generation — see calibration below), semantic similarity to golden answers (embedding cosine), and hallucination rate estimator via heuristic checks.
- Cost proxy: tokens processed * model_cost_per_token + extra GPU seconds attributable to priming overhead.

Calibration and quality thresholding
- Calibrate coherence score using a 500 sample annotated set per archetype. Coherence score maps human ratings (0–1) to automated heuristics combining log‑prob delta and embedding consistency. Documented calibration artifact stored in internal registry.
- Set per‑service minimal acceptable quality delta based on business criticality: high (delta >= -0.01), medium (delta >= -0.03), low (delta >= -0.06).

Runbook: executing FMFB
Preconditions
1. Select model artifact tags and quant profiles to test.
2. Ensure telemetry ingestion for runtime allocator, batcher, and KV cache deltas is enabled.
3. Provision test dedicated pools or isolated private deployment (shadow).
Procedure
1. Prepare template corpus
   a) Generate tokenized versions for each example and save as JSON lines.
   b) Annotate golden outputs for extraction tasks.
2. Baseline run (no priming)
   - Warmup 10k requests across archetypes.
   - Collect baseline metrics for 30 minutes under steady and bursty profiles.
3. Priming runs
   - Run short, medium, long priming templates sequentially.
   - For each run: execute warmup, then 30m steady profile, 1h burst simulation.
4. Postprocessing
   - Compute deltas against baseline for memory, latency, batch utilization, cache eviction, and quality.
   - Produce per-model CSV report and a summarized Confluence table.
5. Decisioning
   - If any acceptance criteria are violated, mark model+template as "Not Approved" for the deployment tier.
   - If memory but not quality is violated, evaluate compact priming (template compression, example truncation).
   - If latency violated but memory within bounds, surface to serving runtime with suggested batching overrides and autoscaling adjustments.

Compact priming strategies (automated mitigations)
- Example trimming: reduce each example to core tokens using extractor heuristics (retain first and last 12 tokens).
- Example summarization: generate compressed summaries with a 4–8 token anchor plus 8 token paraphrase.
- Template condensation: move metadata outside the token budget into structured tool calls or functioncall metadata where supported.

Triage playbook (if regression detected)

Notes and considerations
- Edge deployments with strict memory caps should default to compact priming templates and explicit template truncation in the SDK.
- Streaming mode exposes a different cost profile — capture streaming-specific allocation traces as part of FMFB.
- Priming interacts with functioncall routing and tool arguments; for tool‑heavy flows prefer moving examples to metadata where supported.
